display.story_text:
After back-to-back years spent on the road the day after Thanksgiving, Utah finally gets a Black Friday game at Rice-Eccles Stadium, and it's Senior Night for an 11-0 team ranked No. 2. My West Virginia vs Utah prediction lays the big spread with Utah Utes −22.5 and takes the Under 68.5 on the over/under.

Aspen Mortensen has been waiting for this. "Home on Black Friday, unbeaten, seniors on the field. Two Thanksgivings I spent watching this game from somebody else's stadium."

Jolene Buckhannon hums a few notes of Country Roads. "Enjoy the ceremony, Aspen. We've got a few folks who'd like to ruin it."

They'll need more than a few. West Virginia allows 34.7 points a game and has given up 37 or more six times: 41 to Oklahoma State, 45 at Iowa State, 52 to Arizona, 42 to Cincinnati, 53 at Texas Tech and 37 to Kansas. Utah scored 48 on this defense last September. The best comparison is Kansas: the Utes beat the Jayhawks 41-24 in this building, and the Jayhawks went to Morgantown and won 37-14.

Devon Dampier runs the Utah offense with 24 touchdown throws against 8 interceptions, and he threw for 278 yards and ran for two scores at TCU last week. Wayshawn Parker and Braden Pegan each have 9 touchdowns. The Utes score 37.9 a game. West Virginia has dropped three in a row, 48-53, 14-37 and 31-34, and needs a sixth win to save its season.

The market has climbed toward the Utes. DraftKings opened Utah −20.5, per ESPN. It now reads Utah Utes −22.5. Utah Utes 44, West Virginia Mountaineers 20 is a 24-point win, a point and a half past it.

The Under rests on Utah's defense at home. The Utes allow 18.5 a game, and four of six visitors to Rice-Eccles scored 14 or fewer. Only the 66-14 opener against Idaho topped this total. West Virginia runs through Cam Cook, who has 243 carries for 1,215 yards, and a ground game keeps the clock moving.

This room is all over the place. Letdown Watch is closest to me at 45-16, with Utah Utes −22.5 and the Under 68.5. Next Man Up also takes Utah, at 49-24, but likes the Over. The Formula goes the other way on the side, 38-21 with West Virginia Mountaineers +22.5, and joins me on the Under. In The Trenches calls the fronts split, has no score this week, and takes no side or total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

The Formula: "Utah beat Houston by eight and BYU by eight in this stadium. Twenty-three is a lot of points to give."

Letdown Watch: "West Virginia lost by 23 at home to Kansas. A Senior Night crowd and a team that's dropped three straight. That isn't a trap. That's a send-off."

My number is Utah by 24 with 64 points, four and a half under. The seniors get their night, and the Mountaineers get a quiet flight east.

Utah Utes 44, West Virginia Mountaineers 20. Utah Utes cover the 22.5. Under 68.5.

display.fanatic_story:
For two straight years Utah spent the day after Thanksgiving in somebody else's stadium, and this Black Friday the Utes finally stay home. West Virginia Mountaineers vs Utah Utes is Senior Night at Rice-Eccles Stadium with an 11-0 team ranked No. 2 in the country, a 7 p.m. kickoff in Salt Lake City, and Aspen Mortensen in her seat early enough to cheer every senior by number while Jolene Buckhannon, two time zones from home, hums Country Roads under her breath like a dare.

"Two years," Aspen says. "Two Black Fridays I watched this team play somewhere else. Tonight they're ours. Tonight it's Senior Night. Tonight the whole state gets to say thank you."

"Thank them all you want," Jolene says. "Just leave room at the end for one more song."

"You're not singing Country Roads in my stadium."

"I sing it everywhere, Aspen. I sang it in the shower in the hotel this morning. The fella next door joined in on the chorus."

There's not much Jolene can say about the season Aspen is having. Utah has won all eleven, scoring 37.9 points a game and giving up 18.5. Devon Dampier has thrown for 2,535 yards and 24 touchdowns, and last week at TCU he threw for 278 and ran for two more in a 38-17 win. Wayshawn Parker has 765 rushing yards and nine scores. Braden Pegan has 718 receiving yards and nine scores of his own. On defense, Elijah Elliss has 5.5 sacks and Trey Reynolds has 63 tackles.

"Eleven and oh," Aspen says, slowly, the way you'd read a grandchild's report card out loud at the dinner table. "Do you want me to say it again?"

"I want you to say forty to thirty-nine," Jolene says. "That's what you beat Arizona by. And twenty-seven to twenty-four at Colorado. Your perfect season has a couple of fingernail marks on it."

Aspen allows that. The Utes have survived some close nights, and Houston and BYU both came into this building and stayed within eight. But the last time these two met, last September, Utah won 48-14, and the time before that, a bowl game in December of 2017, it was 30-14.

"We have history," Aspen says.

"You have two games. We have mountains older than your stadium."

"We have mountains too, Jolene. Look up."

West Virginia limps in at 5-6 after three straight losses, every one of them painful. The Mountaineers lost 53-48 at Texas Tech, got beat by Kansas at home, and dropped a 34-31 heartbreaker to Houston on Senior Day last week. They need one more win to get to six, and they're carrying it on Cam Cook's back. Cook has run 243 times for 1,215 yards and nine touchdowns, and he went for 131 against Houston. Michael Hawkins Jr. has thrown 14 touchdowns against just three interceptions, and he once threw for 464 yards in a shootout win over Cincinnati. DJ Epps has 648 receiving yards and Isaiah Patterson leads the defense with 74 tackles.

"Cam Cook is a mountain," Jolene says. "You don't tackle a mountain. You go around it, and that takes all day."

"We have all night," Aspen says. "Kickoff's at seven."

West Virginia also went into Fort Worth and won 24-20 in October, a month before Utah did its own damage there, and Jolene brings that up twice before the national anthem.

Here's the night. The seniors walk out to a roar that Jolene can feel in her shoes, and Utah plays like it wants to send them off in style. Dampier finds Pegan early, Parker breaks one up the middle, and the Utes are up three scores before the Mountaineers get settled. Cook keeps West Virginia in it for a while, grinding out first downs and a touchdown before halftime, and Hawkins hits Epps for another in the third quarter that gets the small gold-and-blue section on its feet. But Elliss and the Utah front clamp down, the Utes keep stacking points, and the fourth quarter belongs to the seniors.

Jolene will sing the first verse of Country Roads in the parking lot anyway, and Aspen, against every instinct she has, will know the words.

My call: Utah Utes 44, West Virginia Mountaineers 20.

display.story_text:
Louisville vs Kentucky for the Governor's Cup lands in the middle of Thanksgiving break, with students scattered for the holiday until Big Blue Nation comes back for a Blue Out and Senior Day at noon. My Louisville vs Kentucky pick is Louisville Cardinals −3 with the Over 54.5, and the trend that matters most is how each team has played in November.

Bianca Thornberry has made the drive east with a smile she hasn't wiped off since last week. "Five touchdown throws against Pitt. Lincoln Kienholz has 20 on the year and 4 picks. Bring your Blue Out. We'll bring the scoreboard operator a snack. He's going to be busy."

Rhett Abernathy-Coyle is not in the mood. "We've lost three straight. I know. But this is the Governor's Cup, on Senior Day, at our place. Records go out the window."

They don't, really. Louisville is 8-3 and has won five straight. Kentucky is 7-4 and has lost three in a row, scoring 6 at Tennessee, 14 against Florida and 14 at Missouri. Kenny Minchey threw 43 times at Missouri and came away with no touchdowns and 2 interceptions. Kentucky's offense has gone cold at the worst possible time.

Louisville's offense hasn't. The Cardinals score 38.6 a game. Isaac Brown has 834 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns, Tre Richardson has 822 receiving yards, and Louisville runs for 5.7 yards a carry against a Kentucky defense that allows 3.9. Clev Lubin has 9 sacks on the other side.

DraftKings opened Kentucky Wildcats −1.5 with a 54.5 total. The side has swung all the way to Louisville Cardinals −3 since, which tells you how the market reads the last three weeks.

The Over is where Louisville lives. Nine of the Cardinals' eleven games went past 54.5, including 52-24 over Stanford and 44-17 at Georgia Tech. Kentucky can still score when it's right. CJ Baxter has 8 rushing touchdowns, Kenny Darby has 711 receiving yards, and the Wildcats put up 35 in overtime wins over South Carolina and LSU. The series has seen 41-14 and 41-0 the last two years, both Louisville.

The room splits on the side and the total. The Formula has 30-26 and takes Louisville Cardinals −3 with the Over 54.5. Next Man Up has 31-29, takes Kentucky Wildcats +3 and the Over. Letdown Watch has 32-22, takes Louisville and the Under 54.5. In The Trenches has no pick in this game. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "Two points, Letdown Watch. That's what a rivalry game on Senior Day is worth to me. You've got Kentucky scoring 22 and acting like that's generous."

Letdown Watch: "Kentucky scored 14 last week, Next Man Up. Twenty-two is generous. I'm practically handing out pie."

My final is Louisville Cardinals 31, Kentucky Wildcats 26. Five points clears the 3, and 57 combined gets past the total by two and a half. Kentucky's seniors get a fight to remember, and the Governor's Cup rides back to Louisville with Bianca.

Louisville Cardinals 31, Kentucky Wildcats 26. Louisville Cardinals cover the 3. Over 54.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Louisville Cardinals vs Kentucky Wildcats for the Governor's Cup is Senior Day and a Blue Out at Kroger Field, and it falls smack in the middle of Thanksgiving break, when the University of Kentucky campus empties out and the students who left their cars behind had to move them to the Comers and South Broadway lots by Tuesday. Rhett Abernathy-Coyle says the place will be full and loud by noon Saturday anyway, and Bianca Thornberry says that's fine, because it will be very quiet by about three.

"You're going to be lonely in that Blue Out," Bianca says. "The whole state's going to be watching you look at a scoreboard."

"It's Senior Day," Rhett says. "Seniors don't lose the Governor's Cup on Senior Day."

"Your seniors lost it 41-0 last year."

Rhett lets that one sit for a while. The last two years of this rivalry haven't been kind to Lexington. Louisville won 41-14 in 2024 and 41-0 last year, and Bianca has both final scores saved as the wallpaper on her phone, just to be safe.

"Before that, we won five straight," Rhett says. "Remember 2018? Fifty-six to ten. I wore that shirt until it fell apart."

What he doesn't want to talk about is November. Kentucky started this season like a team on a mission. The Wildcats won at Texas A&M, beat South Carolina and LSU in overtime, won at Oklahoma, and were 7-1 at the end of October. Then the road got hard. They lost at Tennessee, at home to Florida and at Missouri, scoring 14 points or fewer in all three.

"Every team hits a wall," Rhett says. "We hit ours early so we can climb over it on Saturday."

Kenny Minchey has had a good year overall, with 15 touchdown throws and only four interceptions, but Missouri made it a long afternoon for him. CJ Baxter has 610 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and Kenny Darby is the receiver Minchey trusts most, with 711 yards. On defense, Grant Godfrey has 96 tackles and is the heartbeat of that group, and Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace leads the Wildcats with six sacks.

Bianca's team has no such wall. Louisville is 8-3, has won five straight and just put 42 points on Pittsburgh. Lincoln Kienholz threw five touchdowns in that game, and he has 20 on the season against four interceptions. Isaac Brown has 834 rushing yards and runs like he's late for supper. Tre Richardson caught eight balls for 114 yards and two scores against Pitt.

"Nothing bothers Lincoln," Bianca says. "You could play this game in a snowstorm and he'd ask if it was supposed to get cold."

"He's never played in front of a Blue Out," Rhett says.

"He played at North Carolina two weeks ago and won 16-14. He's played in front of worse."

The Louisville defense has its own name to watch. Clev Lubin has nine sacks, and Bianca says he's the first guy she watches on every snap. Stanquan Clark leads the team in tackles.

Rhett's real hope is the noise and the moment. Kroger Field on Senior Day, with blue in every seat, has been a hard place for anybody to win this year. Kentucky lost only twice there, to Alabama in September and to Florida.

"You've got to beat us here, in this," Rhett says, waving at the stands. "On Senior Day. I don't care what happened the last two years."

Here's how Saturday goes. Kentucky comes out flying, the way rivalry teams do, and Baxter scores early to make the Blue Out roar. Louisville settles down and gets Brown going on the ground, and Kienholz finds Richardson behind the defense for the go-ahead score before halftime. The second half turns into a shootout. Minchey answers twice, once to Darby, and with five minutes left the Wildcats are within a score. But Lubin gets to Minchey on a big third down, Louisville runs the clock with Brown, and the Cardinals hang on.

When it's over, Bianca walks past Rhett on her way to the exit and pats him on the shoulder, gently, the way you'd pat a cousin at Thanksgiving who just lost the backyard football game for the third year running, and tells him the cup will be well taken care of until he comes to visit it.

My call: Louisville Cardinals 31, Kentucky Wildcats 26.

display.story_text:
Saturday is Canes 4 Life Day at Hard Rock Stadium, Miami's Senior Day, and the Hurricanes walk their seniors out already holding a ticket to the ACC title game. My Boston College vs Miami pick is Miami Hurricanes −25.5 and the Over 53.5, because the Eagles need this game more than anybody in the building and still don't have the horses to stay close.

Javi "The Breeze" Castillo has his sunglasses on before noon. "Seniors in the sun, Charlotte when we're done. Darian Mensah throws it, and Boston College runs."

Siobhan Dunleavy opens her case anyway. "Objection, Javi. We're 5-6. One win and we're in a bowl. You've got nothing to play for but a parade. We've got everything."

She's right about the stakes. Boston College has to win to get to six, and the Eagles came in hot after a 27-15 win over Syracuse in which Bo MacCormack III ran 30 times for 236 yards. That's the BC plan: run it, shorten it, and hope. Mason McKenzie can help that plan with his legs. He leads the team in passing yards at 1,798 and in rushing yards at 718.

The problem is what happens when that plan meets a real team on the road. Boston College lost 47-2 at Duke and 41-7 at Notre Dame. The Eagles score 21.0 points a game and give up 27.2. Miami is 10-1, 8-0 in the ACC, scoring 42.6 a game. Mensah has 3,317 yards with 29 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, and Malachi Toney has 73 catches for 1,027 yards and 13 scores.

Here's my worry, and I'll say it out loud. Miami has clinched. Wake Forest is waiting in Charlotte, and a coaching staff with a title game next week might pull its starters early. But this is the seniors' last home game, Miami's last two wins over Duke and Virginia Tech were tighter than the program likes, and Mensah threw two interceptions against the Hokies. A team that wants to look sharp heading into a title game scores early and often against a defense like this one. My margin of 29 assumes Miami is up big at halftime and coasts the rest.

The Over needs Miami to do most of the work, and it can. The Hurricanes have scored 52 or more three times at home. I have 55, a point and a half past the number. DraftKings opened Miami Hurricanes −26.5 with a 53.5 total, and the side has come down a point.

The room is mostly on Miami. The Formula has Miami 40-14 with the Hurricanes −25.5 and the Over 53.5. Next Man Up has 44-13 and likes the Canes and the Over. Letdown Watch has 41-12, likes Miami −25.5, and goes Under. In The Trenches has no score this week, sees the fronts as split, and takes neither side nor total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "Letdown Watch, a team clinches and you still take its side. Did you lose your own playbook?"

Letdown Watch: "I'm with you on Miami. I just think they get bored in the fourth quarter."

My final is Miami Hurricanes 42, Boston College Eagles 13. Javi does the U. Siobhan files an appeal on the flight home.

display.fanatic_story:
Miami's seniors get one more walk onto the grass at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday, and the school has named the day Canes 4 Life Day. Boston College Eagles vs Miami Hurricanes pits a team that has already punched its ticket to the ACC title game against a team that needs one more win just to see December, and Javi "The Breeze" Castillo is calling it a farewell party while Siobhan Dunleavy calls it a hearing.

"Court is in session," Siobhan says, and sets a toy gavel on the armrest. "The Eagles are 5-6. Win, and we're bowl-eligible. Lose, and we go home. I'd say we have the more motivated client."

"Motivated is nice," Javi says. "Seniors in the sun, Charlotte when we're done. You can be motivated from the visitors' bench."

Miami clinched its trip to Charlotte last week with a 28-20 win over Virginia Tech, and Mark Fletcher Jr. ran for three touchdowns to make sure of it. Wake Forest is waiting on Dec. 5. That leaves Saturday as a send-off for the seniors on a team that went 8-0 in the league, with its only loss coming at Notre Dame.

"This team is the best thing I've watched since I hung up my own cleats," Javi says. "And I was a defensive back, so I watched a lot of guys run past me."

His case is mostly one man. Darian Mensah has 3,317 yards with 29 touchdown throws and only 4 interceptions, and he has the kind of accuracy that makes defensive coordinators stare at the ceiling at night. He went 27 of 30 for 401 yards at Stanford in the opener and never really slowed down. Malachi Toney is the guy on the other end: 73 catches, 1,027 yards, 13 touchdowns. Javian Mallory has 624 rushing yards and 9 scores. On defense, Marquise Lightfoot has 7 sacks and Mohamed Toure has 76 tackles.

Siobhan has heard all of it. She has a rebuttal, and his name is Bo MacCormack III.

"Exhibit A," she says. "Saturday against Syracuse. Thirty carries. Two hundred thirty-six yards. A 47-yard run on our first drive and a 56-yard touchdown in the third quarter. That kid ran like he was late for the T."

That was a wicked good afternoon in Chestnut Hill. Mason McKenzie threw touchdowns to Zeke Moore, his first as an Eagle, and to Nedrick Boldin Jr. on a screen that went 22 yards. Luca Lombardo hit field goals from 46 and 32. Charlie Comella had a career-high nine tackles. BC won 27-15 and walked off the field with a chance.

McKenzie is the engine of this offense in every way. He leads the Eagles in throwing yards and in rushing yards, 718 on the ground, which tells you how much this team asks of him. Anthony Palano has 93 tackles at linebacker. Demetrius Ballard has 4.5 sacks.

"Now here's the part where I object to myself," Siobhan says. "We lost at Duke. We lost at Notre Dame. Those weren't close, and I'm not going to pretend they were."

"I appreciate the honesty," Javi says. "It's very Boston of you."

"It's very law school of me."

The last time these two met, Miami won 45-20. The time before that, in 2018, Boston College won 27-14, and Siobhan has a printout of that box score she keeps in the same folder as her diploma. She brought it to Florida. She will not be showing it to anyone in the parking lot.

Here's how Saturday goes. The seniors get their moment, the stadium gets loud, and BC tries to do exactly what it did to Syracuse, handing it to MacCormack and grinding the clock. It works for one drive. Then Mensah finds Toney on a deep ball, Mallory punches one in, and the Hurricanes start pulling away before halftime. BC gets a field goal out of a long drive and a late touchdown, and MacCormack gets his yards, but the Eagles never get close enough to make Javi take his sunglasses off.

Siobhan bangs the gavel one last time on the walk out and rules that next season is now in session. Javi does the U with both arms in the tunnel and rhymes something about Charlotte that nobody can hear over the band.

My call: Miami Hurricanes 42, Boston College Eagles 13.

display.fanatic_story:
Somebody online started calling it the Bowl Eligibowl, and Rutherford "Ruff" Pegram has decided that's the best name anybody has given a game in years. NC State Wolfpack vs North Carolina Tar Heels is Senior Day at Kenan Stadium on Saturday, both teams are 5-6, and Ainsley Pemberton points out that whoever loses gets to watch the bowl season on television like everybody else.

"Sixth win goes to a bowl," Ainsley says. "Loser goes Christmas shopping."

"I already finished my Christmas shopping," Ruff says. "I bought five little Wolfpack ornaments. One for every year in a row we've beaten you."

Ainsley would like it noted that she hung up her own ornaments a long time ago, and that North Carolina still leads the all-time series 68-41-6. Ruff would like it noted that nobody alive remembers most of the 68.

It's been a strange fall on both sides of the Triangle. In Raleigh, Dave Doeren was fired on Oct. 24, special teams coordinator Todd Goebbel took over as interim head coach, and the Wolfpack lost to Duke and blew a fourth-quarter lead against Syracuse. Then, on Nov. 16, NC State introduced Philip Rivers as its next head coach, at the indoor practice building right there on campus, and the whole program seemed to stand up straighter.

"Philip Rivers," Ruff says, as if the name explains itself. To him, it does.

The Wolfpack went to Tallahassee last Saturday and beat Florida State 28-10. CJ Bailey threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns, the defense shut the Seminoles out in the second half, and Keenan Jackson, who leads the team with 529 receiving yards, kept moving the chains. Popo Aguirre has 90 tackles at linebacker and Elijah Satchell has 5 sacks.

"We've been through a coaching change, a hiring and a lot of Sunday mornings," Ruff says. "And here we are, still standing, playing for a bowl in your house. Feels about right."

Ainsley's fall has been strange in its own way. Carolina has lost four of its last five, including a 16-14 home loss to Louisville in which Billy Edwards Jr. was hurt in the third quarter. That's how true freshman Travis Burgess got his first start, last Saturday at Virginia, and that's how Ainsley ended up spending the next 24 hours rewatching a game her team lost by 17.

"He threw for 354 yards," she says. "He ran for 106. He's one of four quarterbacks in the whole country this season to throw for 300 and run for 100 in the same game. We lost, and I still drove home happy."

Bill Belichick did not drive home happy. He called the Virginia game a bad performance all the way around and said his team was out-everythinged, which Ruff has already printed on a piece of paper and taped to his fridge. Carolina had three trips inside the Virginia 30 that came up empty and drew 11 penalties. Still, Jordan Shipp caught nine balls for 149 yards. Derek McDonald has 107 tackles. Xavier Lewis has 7.5 sacks and spent the whole afternoon chasing the quarterback.

"Clean up the penalties and that game looks different," Ainsley says. "Clean up the penalties Saturday and Burgess beats you."

"He's a freshman."

"Your new coach was a freshman once."

That stops Ruff for a second, which almost never happens.

Here's how I see Saturday going. The seniors get their moment in Kenan, the Pack scores first behind Bailey and Jackson, and for a while it looks like that ornament collection is about to get a sixth. But Burgess settles in. He hits Shipp on a long one before halftime, then runs for a score in the third quarter on a play that leaves the NC State sideline staring at each other. Bailey answers with a touchdown, and the rivalry goes into the fourth quarter tied up and loud. McDonald makes the stop that matters on a late third down, and Carolina kicks a field goal and adds a short touchdown to get to six wins.

Ruff takes it like a gentleman, more or less. He shakes Ainsley's hand outside Kenan, then informs her that Philip Rivers will not be losing this game next year, and walks off toward his car humming the NC State fight song a little too loudly.

My call: North Carolina Tar Heels 29, NC State Wolfpack 23.

Syracuse has its first sellout of the season at the JMA Wireless Dome for Senior Day and the final game in the Loud House, and the Orange need a win over Notre Dame to get to six. For this Notre Dame vs Syracuse prediction, I'm siding with the Orange against the spread at Syracuse Orange +24.5, and the over/under call is Over 52.5.

Declan Moriarty-Chen pours coffee from his thermos and offers Nico a cup. "Last year was 70-7, Nico. I'm only mentioning it so you hear it from a friend."

Nico Calabrese waves the cup away. "Last year we weren't in our building with a full house. Different afternoon."

He's right about the building. Syracuse has played four FBS teams at home and none of them won by more than eight: Cal 21-18, Louisville 34-26, Clemson 18-13, and the Orange beat SMU 30-27. Umari Hatcher is the reason this offense can keep up with anybody. He has 77 catches for 1,257 yards and caught 11 balls for 212 yards at Boston College last week, even in a 15-27 loss. Keyshawn Johnson has 9 sacks.

CJ Carr has 24 touchdown throws and 3 interceptions, Nolan James Jr. has 11 rushing touchdowns, and the Irish allow 12.8 a game. Their only loss came at BYU, 24-28. But the price has gone a long way. DraftKings opened Notre Dame −21, per ESPN. It's Notre Dame −24.5 now, a jump of three and a half points. Notre Dame Fighting Irish 38, Syracuse Orange 15 is a 23-point win, a point and a half short of that.

The quarterback question is real. Steve Angeli has the most yards, 1,886, but Malachi Nelson took most of the snaps in the loss at Boston College, and Amari Odom threw five touchdowns in the overtime win at UConn. I'm pricing a 15-point day no matter which of them is out there, and Hatcher makes that reachable.

The Over is mostly Notre Dame. The Irish score 38.1 a game and have hung 41 or more on five teams. Seven of Syracuse's eleven games have finished above 52.5. The total opened at 54.5 on DraftKings, and it has come down to 52.5.

The room is split. The Formula is with me on the side at 36-16, Syracuse Orange +24.5, but goes Under 52.5. Next Man Up has 37-17, takes the Orange and goes Over. Letdown Watch has a 41-11 rout with Notre Dame Fighting Irish −24.5 and the Under. In The Trenches calls the fronts split, has no score this week, and takes no side or total. The Formula: "A repeat of what? Syracuse hasn't lost at home to an FBS team by more than eight."

My final is Notre Dame by 23 with 53 points, half a point over. The seniors get a full house, and the Orange stay within reach.

display.fanatic_story:
The JMA Wireless Dome is sold out for the first time this season, and it took Notre Dame Fighting Irish vs Syracuse Orange on Senior Day, the final game in the Loud House this year, to fill every seat. Nico Calabrese has been telling everyone in Syracuse since Thursday that the Orange are one win from six, and Declan Moriarty-Chen came in from South Bend in his sweater vest with a thermos of coffee and the patience of a man who has watched his team win ten of eleven.

"First sellout," Nico says. "Seniors on the field. One win from a bowl. You picked a bad day to visit, Declan."

"I picked the only day the schedule gave me," Declan says, pouring a cup. "Also, I'd like to gently bring up last year."

"Don't."

"Seventy to seven."

"I said don't, and you did it anyway, and now you have to live with yourself."

Declan sips his coffee and does live with himself, quite comfortably. Notre Dame is 10-1, and the one loss came at BYU by four in October. CJ Carr has thrown for 2,697 yards with 24 touchdowns and three interceptions, which is the kind of number Declan recites at Thanksgiving dinner instead of saying grace. Nolan James Jr. has run for 742 yards and 11 scores. Jordan Faison has 724 receiving yards, and he caught seven for 109 in the 24-3 win over SMU last week. The Irish defense allows 12.8 points a game, with Boubacar Traore up front and Adon Shuler patrolling the back end.

"We gave up three points to SMU," Declan says. "Three. I've seen more points on a church raffle ticket."

"You've been to some low-scoring raffles."

Nico has his own case, and it's built on noise. Syracuse is 5-6, but the Orange have been brutal to visit. Cal won here by three. Louisville won here by eight. Clemson won here by five on homecoming. SMU came in and lost 30-27. Not one FBS visitor has walked out of this dome with a comfortable win all year, and none of them had to face a sellout.

"The Loud House isn't a nickname," Nico says. "It's a warning label."

The Orange offense runs through Umari Hatcher, and Nico won't stop talking about him. Hatcher has 77 catches for 1,257 yards and nine touchdowns, and last week at Boston College he caught 11 balls for 212 yards, even as Syracuse lost 27-15. Steve Angeli has thrown for 1,886 yards, Malachi Nelson took the snaps in Chestnut Hill, and Amari Odom once threw five touchdowns in an overtime win at UConn. Three quarterbacks, one Hatcher.

"Whoever's throwing, he's open," Nico says. "Hatcher is open in his sleep. He's open at the grocery store."

On defense, Keyshawn Johnson has nine sacks and Chris D'Appolonia has 78 tackles, and both of them are going to be busy. The Irish just don't hand the ball away very often.

"Your quarterback has three interceptions," Nico admits. "That's annoying. That's genuinely annoying."

"Thank you," Declan says. "I'll tell him you said so."

Here's how Saturday goes. The seniors walk out to a roar that rattles the roof, and Syracuse comes out swinging, with Hatcher catching a long one on the first drive and the place shaking like a subway car. Notre Dame answers, calmly, the way it does. James runs it in, Carr finds Faison, and the Irish lead by two scores at halftime. Syracuse keeps fighting, with Johnson getting home for a sack in the third quarter that makes Nico hug a stranger in the next row. But Carr keeps moving the chains, the Irish defense keeps the Orange out of the end zone on two long drives, and Notre Dame pulls away late. Hatcher gets one more touchdown before the clock runs out, and the sold-out crowd roars for him like he won the game.

Nico will stay in his seat after the final whistle and clap until every senior has left the field. Declan will stay right beside him, quiet for once.

My call: Notre Dame Fighting Irish 38, Syracuse Orange 15.

games.gambler_story:
Syracuse has its first sellout of the season at the JMA Wireless Dome for Senior Day and the final game in the Loud House, and the Orange need a win over Notre Dame to get to six. For this Notre Dame vs Syracuse prediction, I'm siding with the Orange against the spread at Syracuse Orange +24.5, and the over/under call is Over 52.5.

Declan Moriarty-Chen pours coffee from his thermos and offers Nico a cup. "Last year was 70-7, Nico. I'm only mentioning it so you hear it from a friend."

Nico Calabrese waves the cup away. "Last year we weren't in our building with a full house. Different afternoon."

He's right about the building. Syracuse has played four FBS teams at home and none of them won by more than eight: Cal 21-18, Louisville 34-26, Clemson 18-13, and the Orange beat SMU 30-27. Umari Hatcher is the reason this offense can keep up with anybody. He has 77 catches for 1,257 yards and caught 11 balls for 212 yards at Boston College last week, even in a 15-27 loss. Keyshawn Johnson has 9 sacks.

CJ Carr has 24 touchdown throws and 3 interceptions, Nolan James Jr. has 11 rushing touchdowns, and the Irish allow 12.8 a game. Their only loss came at BYU, 24-28. But the price has gone a long way. DraftKings opened Notre Dame −21, per ESPN. It's Notre Dame −24.5 now, a jump of three and a half points. Notre Dame Fighting Irish 38, Syracuse Orange 15 is a 23-point win, a point and a half short of that.

The quarterback question is real. Steve Angeli has the most yards, 1,886, but Malachi Nelson took most of the snaps in the loss at Boston College, and Amari Odom threw five touchdowns in the overtime win at UConn. I'm pricing a 15-point day no matter which of them is out there, and Hatcher makes that reachable.

The Over is mostly Notre Dame. The Irish score 38.1 a game and have hung 41 or more on five teams. Seven of Syracuse's eleven games have finished above 52.5. The total opened at 54.5 on DraftKings, and it has come down to 52.5.

The room is split. The Formula is with me on the side at 36-16, Syracuse Orange +24.5, but goes Under 52.5. Next Man Up has 37-17, takes the Orange and goes Over. Letdown Watch has a 41-11 rout with Notre Dame Fighting Irish −24.5 and the Under. In The Trenches calls the fronts split, has no score this week, and takes no side or total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "Seventy to seven a year ago. Bowl spot on the line for Syracuse, and Notre Dame still has something to play for. I don't see a letdown, I see a repeat."

The Formula: "A repeat of what? Syracuse hasn't lost at home to an FBS team by more than eight."

My final is Notre Dame by 23 with 53 points, half a point over. The seniors get a full house, and the Orange stay within reach.

Notre Dame Fighting Irish 38, Syracuse Orange 15. Syracuse Orange cover the 24.5. Over 52.5.

display.story_text:
Michigan vs Ohio State comes to Ohio Stadium without a Senior Day attached, because the Buckeyes moved theirs to the September opener this year so nothing would compete with The Game. Smart call. My Michigan vs Ohio State pick is Ohio State Buckeyes −10 with the Over 38.5, and the number that decides it is the one Michigan's own notes put on the front page.

The team that wins the rushing battle in this rivalry has won twenty-four straight meetings. Michigan runs for 3.7 yards a carry, and Ohio State allows 3.2. Ohio State runs for 4.0, and Michigan allows 3.0. Those are tight numbers, and they're the reason In The Trenches won't take a side. What breaks the tie is who has to throw.

Buck Holloway is happy to explain. "Jeremiah Smith has 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns. He caught 6 for 165 at Nebraska. You can win the rushing battle all day and still lose the football game to one guy."

Gus Hartwell doesn't flinch. "We've won two straight in this building. Bryce Underwood is back throwing, our defense gives up 17.5 a game, and John Henry Daley has 8 sacks. Bring your gold pants. Bring the spare set."

Michigan's defense is real. The problem is everything else. The Wolverines score 18.3 a game, put up 6 against Indiana and Michigan State and 7 at Oregon, and needed overtime to beat UCLA 18-16 last week. Underwood went 11 for 24 in that one and has 6 touchdowns and 6 interceptions on the year. Ohio State has its own question at quarterback. Luke Fahey has taken the most throws in each of the last four games after Julian Sayin led the way through mid-October, and the Buckeyes are 1-3 in that stretch. But Fahey has thrown for 259 or more in three of those four, because his top target is Smith.

That's the Over, too. Ten of Ohio State's eleven games cleared 38.5, and the Buckeyes score 34.3 a game. DraftKings opened Ohio State Buckeyes −14 with a 46.5 total, and both have dropped hard since, the total all the way to 38.5. That's the market pricing in Michigan's defense and Ohio State's losses. I think it went too far on the total.

All three scoring cards agree. The Formula has 31-16, Next Man Up has 30-11 and Letdown Watch has 30-13, and all three take Ohio State Buckeyes −10 and the Over 38.5. In The Trenches has no pick in this game. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

The Formula: "Next Man Up has Michigan at 11. That's not a projection, that's a grudge."

Next Man Up: "Michigan scored 6 twice and 7 once this year, The Formula. My 11 is a compliment. You're the one handing them 16 because you got nervous."

My final is Ohio State Buckeyes 30, Michigan Wolverines 13. Seventeen points clears the 10 by a touchdown, and 43 combined clears the total by four and a half. Bo Jackson wins the ground game by a little, Smith wins the game by a lot, and the gold pants get handed out again.

Ohio State Buckeyes 30, Michigan Wolverines 13. Ohio State Buckeyes cover the 10. Over 38.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Michigan Wolverines vs Ohio State Buckeyes in Columbus has no Senior Day this year, because Ohio State moved its seniors' big moment all the way to the September opener against Ball State so that nothing, not even a farewell, would get in the way of The Game. Buck Holloway calls that focus, Gus Hartwell calls it nerves, and the two of them have been arguing about it since the Skull Session at St. John Arena let out Saturday morning.

"You moved Senior Day," Gus says. "You moved Senior Day because of us. I want that framed."

"We moved it so the seniors could enjoy it," Buck says. "This Saturday isn't for enjoying. This Saturday is for winning."

That's the thing about this rivalry. Everybody knows the history, and everybody uses it differently. Gus will remind you that Michigan won four straight meetings before last year, including two right here at Ohio Stadium, 45-23 in 2022 and 13-10 in 2024. Buck will remind you that Ohio State won 27-9 in Ann Arbor last November and handed out gold pants for it, a tradition the Buckeyes have kept since 1934.

"Gold pants," Buck says, pretending to polish a tiny pair on his keychain. "Ninety-two years and they still shine."

"You've had to polish them a lot less lately," Gus says.

Both teams arrive with bruises. Ohio State is 7-4 and has lost three of its last four, including a 31-28 heartbreaker at Nebraska last week. Michigan is 6-5 and needed overtime to beat UCLA 18-16 in Ann Arbor. Neither side is where it expected to be in August, and that might make this one meaner than usual.

Michigan's case is its defense, and Gus will walk you through every piece of it. The Wolverines give up 17.5 points a game. John Henry Daley has eight sacks off the end, Troy Bowles has 89 tackles, and Chris Bracy has been everywhere in the secondary, with two interceptions and three sacks of his own.

"You want to throw on us?" Gus says. "Go ahead. Ask UCLA how that went."

"We're not throwing at you," Buck says. "We're throwing to Jeremiah."

And that's Ohio State's case in one name. Jeremiah Smith has 86 catches for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns this season. He caught six balls for 165 yards and two scores at Nebraska. According to Ohio State's own notes, he needs one touchdown, nine catches and 125 yards on Saturday to break all three school single-season records at once.

"In The Game," Buck says. "He's going to do it in The Game. You can't write that. Well, you can. I'm going to."

There's one stat Michigan's notes put right at the top this week, and Gus has it memorized. In 24 straight meetings, the team that won the rushing battle won the game. Savion Hiter has 542 yards for Michigan and carried 26 times for 104 against UCLA. Ohio State's Bo Jackson has 851 yards and nine touchdowns.

"Win the ground, win the day," Gus says. "Savion's going to carry it thirty times if he has to."

"Then Bo carries it thirty-one," Buck says.

The quarterbacks are the wild card. Bryce Underwood took most of Michigan's throws against UCLA after Tommy Carr handled the job from late October into mid-November, and Underwood has had a hard year throwing the ball. For Ohio State, Luke Fahey has taken over most of the throws since Halloween, and his job is simple: find Jeremiah Smith, and then find him again.

Here's how Saturday goes. Michigan's defense makes the first quarter a street fight, and Hiter grinds out a long drive that ends in a field goal. Ohio State answers when Fahey finds Smith down the sideline for a long touchdown, and Ohio Stadium shakes. Michigan hangs in until halftime. But in the second half Jackson starts breaking tackles, the Buckeyes win the ground game by a little, and Smith takes care of the rest, scoring again in the fourth quarter to grab one of those school records in front of a full Horseshoe.

When it's over, Buck pulls out his keychain and holds up the tiny gold pants, and Gus, to his credit, shakes his hand and says the same thing he says every year, win or lose: see you in Ann Arbor, and bring a coat.

My call: Ohio State Buckeyes 30, Michigan Wolverines 13.

display.story_text:
Wyoming says goodbye to its seniors at War Memorial Stadium on Saturday with a 10 a.m. local kickoff, the same morning downtown Laramie hands out Shop Laramie bags for Small Business Saturday. My UConn vs Wyoming pick is Wyoming Cowboys +3 and the Over 47.5: UConn wins a close one, but not by more than a field goal, and the Huskies' offense keeps the scoreboard busy.

Colter Sprague doesn't waste words. "Seniors. Cold. Home. Three points is plenty."

Jo Ferrante flew in from Hartford with a heavy coat. "Plenty for what? We've scored 33.7 a game. You've scored 21.9. I'll take our offense at altitude any day."

Jo has the numbers on her side, at least on offense. Kalieb Osborne has 2,615 yards with 20 touchdowns and 5 interceptions, and Cyncir Bowers has 867 rushing yards and 11 scores. UConn is 6-5 and has won two straight, 46-22 over James Madison and 29-21 over Old Dominion, with Bowers running for 105 yards in the second one. A team that already has six wins, flying across two time zones for a morning kickoff, is not one I trust to win by more than three.

Wyoming is the opposite story. The Cowboys are 7-4, 6-2 in the Mountain West, and Saturday is their last chance to send the seniors out right after a 24-17 loss to New Mexico. Landon Sims has taken the most throws in each of the last two games, going 19 of 25 for 289 yards at UTEP and 13 of 23 for 142 against the Lobos. Tyler Hughes leads the team in both throwing and rushing yards, but I'm pricing this as a Sims game, and the Cowboys still keep it inside the number at home. Kyle Frendt has 425 receiving yards at tight end, and Ethan Stuhlsatz leads a defense that allows 21.3 points a game with 88 tackles.

The side comes down to the building. Wyoming has lost only once at War Memorial this year, and that was to New Mexico last week. UConn's road games went 48-20 at Southern Miss, 21-24 at Miami (OH), 34-20 at Temple and 26-35 at Air Force.

The Over is UConn's doing. The Huskies' games have gone past 47.5 combined points in 10 of 11. Wyoming's haven't, but Sims has thrown it more than Hughes did, and a game where the visitors score 27 doesn't need much from the Cowboys. I have 52. DraftKings opened UConn Huskies −2.5 with a 49.5 total, and by Monday it was −3 with the total down to 47.5.

The room is mostly with the Cowboys. The Formula has UConn 28-24, takes the Huskies −3 and likes the Over 47.5. Next Man Up has 26-24, takes Wyoming Cowboys +3 and likes the Over. Letdown Watch has 25-24, takes Wyoming and goes Over. In The Trenches has 28-27, likes the Cowboys and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

In The Trenches: "Four points for the Huskies? That's not a trench read. That's a basketball score."

The Formula: "And you're on a team that just lost at home. Enjoy the cold."

My final is UConn Huskies 27, Wyoming Cowboys 25. Colter says "Close," and that's the whole interview.

UConn Huskies 27, Wyoming Cowboys 25. Wyoming Cowboys cover the 3. Over 47.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Colter Sprague has a problem on Saturday morning, and it's a Laramie kind of problem: Downtown hands out Shop Laramie bags at The Collective on Second Street from 9 to 11 for Small Business Saturday, and Wyoming kicks off its Senior Day against UConn at 10. UConn Huskies vs Wyoming Cowboys closes the home schedule at War Memorial Stadium, and Jo Ferrante, who flew out from Connecticut, cannot believe a man would even think about skipping kickoff for a tote bag.

"First 250 bags have goodies in them," Colter says. "Gift certificates, maybe."

"That's the most words I've heard you say in a row," Jo says.

"Nine," Colter says. "Close to a record."

He'll be in his seat. He just wants it known that he gave the bag real thought, because this whole weekend in Laramie is built around downtown. Friday was Plaid Friday, when folks wore plaid to shop local instead of hitting the big box stores, and The Knothole on Second Street is running a store-wide sale on Wyoming gear for anybody who wants a new brown-and-gold hoodie before the first snow. Colter plans to buy two.

"You need two?" Jo asks.

"Cold."

Now the football, which Jo has been waiting to talk about since she landed in Denver. UConn is 6-5 and coming off its best two weeks of the year, a 46-22 win over James Madison and a 29-21 win over Old Dominion. Kalieb Osborne has thrown for 2,615 yards and 20 touchdowns with only 5 interceptions, and Cyncir Bowers has 867 yards and 11 scores on the ground. Shamar Porter only has 23 catches, but they've gone for 509 yards, which tells you exactly what he does.

"Porter runs past people," Jo says. "Every time he catches one, it's a fast break. We're a basketball school that learned how to throw it deep."

"Wind," Colter says.

He means it. War Memorial in late November isn't a friendly place for a deep ball, and the Cowboys know how to play in it. Wyoming is 7-4 and 6-2 in the Mountain West, and the Cowboys have only lost once at home this year. Unfortunately, that one was last week, a 24-17 loss to New Mexico that still has Colter staring at the wall.

Here's the twist for Wyoming. Tyler Hughes leads the team in throwing and rushing yards, but Landon Sims has taken the most throws in each of the last two games, and he went 19 of 25 for 289 yards in a win at UTEP. Kyle Frendt, the tight end, has 425 receiving yards and caught a touchdown against New Mexico. Ethan Stuhlsatz leads the defense with 88 tackles. Esaia Bogar has 5.5 sacks coming off the end, and he's the guy who needs to make Osborne uncomfortable.

"Sims is good," Colter says. Then, after a long pause: "Frendt's better."

UConn's defense has its own leader in Hayden Pegg, who has 83 tackles, and Joshua Mickens has 4 sacks. Jo admits the Huskies give up some points, and she remembers the 42-41 overtime loss to Syracuse well enough to wince when anybody mentions it.

"We don't do boring," she says. "That's a promise and a warning."

The only time these two have met in the last decade, Wyoming won 24-22, and Colter has the program from that game somewhere in a drawer at the ranch. He is not going to find it before Saturday. He looked.

Here's how Saturday goes. The seniors walk out to a loud, cold crowd, and Wyoming comes out running the ball and keeping Osborne on the sideline. Sims hits Frendt down the seam for an early score. UConn answers with Porter behind the defense, because of course it does, and Bowers grinds out the second half. It goes back and forth into the fourth quarter, the Cowboys get one last drive, and they come up short by a couple of points. Nobody leaves early, even with the bag table still open downtown.

Colter stands, tips his hat to the seniors, and says "Proud." Jo counts it as one more word for his season total and heads off to find a hot chocolate on Ivinson Avenue.

My call: UConn Huskies 27, Wyoming Cowboys 25.

Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather is still glowing from Annapolis. "Down ten in the fourth quarter to a ranked team, and we won it on fourth-and-one with fifteen seconds left. Priya, I've seen a lot of Senior Days. That was the best."

Priya Halloran has had a different kind of season. "Annabel, we're 1-10. Our seniors would like one good afternoon. They can have it against anybody, and today it's you."

Navy is the better team, and it isn't close. Gutierrez has 1,400 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns and ran 35 times for 241 against Memphis. Navy scores 30.1 points a game. Charlotte allows 36.7 and lost 42-14 at Tulsa last week. The Niners have given up 50 or more twice.

The case for Charlotte at this price comes from Navy's defense, which allows 30.8 points a game. The Mids gave up 34 to Memphis, 35 to Temple and 49 to North Texas. They don't blow teams out often, either. Their only win by more than eight came against Towson. Navy is 4-6 because it plays close games and finishes on the wrong side of most of them.

Charlotte has been in some close games of its own. The 49ers lost 43-41 in overtime to The Citadel, 38-31 in overtime to Tulane and 17-16 to East Carolina. Conner Harrell has taken the throws for seven straight games, and Jaden Barnes has 66 catches for 626 yards. Gavin Willis leads the defense with 98 tackles.

display.fanatic_story:
Fifteen seconds were left on the clock in Annapolis last Saturday when Vic Listorti got stood up at the 1, and two teammates shoved him the rest of the way into the end zone. Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather has watched the replay of that fourth-and-1 more times than she'd admit, and now she's heading south for Navy Midshipmen vs Charlotte 49ers, where Priya Halloran will be waiting at Jerry Richardson Stadium for Senior Day and Fan Appreciation.

"Navy came back from ten down in the fourth quarter against a ranked team on our own Senior Day," Annabel says. "Brian Newberry didn't kick the tying field goal. He went for it. I nearly lost my hat."

"Great," Priya says. "Now come to ours and be polite about it."

Priya has had a long season. Charlotte is 1-10, and the one win came at Temple in October. She can tell you about the near misses without looking anything up: a 43-41 overtime loss to The Citadel to open the year, a 38-31 overtime loss to Tulane on Halloween week, and a 17-16 loss to East Carolina two weeks ago in a game the 49ers had every chance to steal. Last week was worse, a 42-14 loss at Tulsa.

"I keep showing up," Priya says. "Our seniors keep showing up. I'll take that over a lot of things."

That's what Saturday is for, in her mind. The 49ers want fans there early for the pregame ceremony, when the seniors walk out for the last time, and there are fan appreciation giveaways all afternoon. Norm the Niner will be working the crowd. Priya plans to give him a high five and a pep talk, in that order.

Annabel came to Charlotte with a quarterback who doesn't throw much and doesn't need to. Jackson Gutierrez has 1,400 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns. He ran 35 times for 241 yards and two scores against Memphis, his third 200-yard game this season, which tied Malcolm Perry's school record. He's the only player in the country with three of them this year.

"He's not a runner who throws," Annabel says. "He's a quarterback who happens to run past everybody. It's different."

Priya's defense has a big job and a short history of doing it. Charlotte allows 36.7 points a game, and Navy's option is the kind of offense that makes a defense count every man every snap. Gavin Willis leads the 49ers with 98 tackles, and he'll need about twenty more on Saturday. Collin Gill has 4 sacks from the secondary. The one thing working for Charlotte is that Navy's own defense has given up 30.8 points a game. Memphis put up 34 on the Mids, Temple 35 and North Texas 49.

"So we can score," Priya says. "Conner Harrell finds Jaden Barnes, Henry Rutledge runs hard, and we keep the ball away from your quarterback as long as we can."

Barnes has 66 catches for 626 yards. Harrell has been taking the throws for seven straight games. Rutledge leads the team with 529 rushing yards, and Khamani Alexander ran for 93 at Tulsa.

Annabel's guys up front have their own leaders. Aiden Lyczek had 10 tackles, a sack and a forced fumble against Memphis. Coleman Cauley has 75 tackles from linebacker. And Navy has a reason to stay sharp, because Army is next, and Annabel will talk about Army for as long as anybody lets her.

"We're playing for a bowl," she says. "Win here and win in December and we're going bowling. Nobody on this team is looking past the 49ers."

Here's how I see Saturday. Charlotte comes out loose and plays like the seniors mean it, and Harrell hits Barnes for an early score that brings the whole home side to its feet. Navy answers the Navy way. Gutierrez keeps it on the option, cuts back, and goes 40 yards, and the Mids grind out a pair of long drives before halftime. Charlotte keeps swinging. Rutledge scores in the third quarter, and Barnes catches another one late. Gutierrez scores twice more, and Navy pulls away in the fourth.

Annabel stays in her seat after the final whistle to applaud Charlotte's seniors as they walk off. Priya notices and walks over to thank her. Then Annabel asks if Norm the Niner is available for Army week, and Priya tells her she'll check.

My call: Navy Midshipmen 34, Charlotte 49ers 22.

Ball State played three straight midweek MAC games in November, and its reward is a Saturday noon kickoff on Fan Appreciation Day to close the season at Scheumann Stadium. Central Michigan Chippewas −4 is my side in this Central Michigan vs Ball State prediction, laying a short spread on the road, and Over 47.5 is my over/under call.

Gus Ponder has his red sweater on again. "Saturday football, Brynn. Daylight. I forgot what it looked like."

Brynn Haverkamp zips her parka. "Enjoy the sunshine, Gus. We're here for win number six."

That's the stake for Central Michigan. The Chippewas are 5-6 and a win gets them to six. They lost 21-40 at Buffalo last week, but the season has been about running the ball, and quarterback Angel Flores leads the team with 618 rushing yards. Jadyn Glasser threw three touchdowns in the Buffalo game and has been the main passer since late October. Mayson Hitchens has 79 tackles.

Ball State is 3-8 and the defense is the problem. The Cardinals allow 34.2 points a game, and nine of their eleven games have gone past 47.5. They gave up 56 to Ohio State, 51 at Liberty and 45 at Northwestern, and 35 at Ohio last week. Keldric Luster can make it interesting: he threw for 257 yards and ran for 109 in that Ohio loss, and TJ Horton has 10 rushing touchdowns.

The side is about who can stop anybody. Central Michigan allows 23.7, more than ten points better than Ball State. Two of Ball State's three wins came against Stony Brook and Sacramento State, and its November went 30-31 in overtime at Massachusetts, 7-28 at home to Buffalo and 28-35 at Ohio. Central Michigan beat Akron 41-17 and Eastern Michigan 35-7.

The market came down. DraftKings opened Central Michigan −6.5 and 46.5, per ESPN. It now sits at Central Michigan Chippewas −4 and 47.5. Central Michigan Chippewas 28, Ball State Cardinals 23 is a five-point road win, one clear of the number.

The total has my attention more than the side. The Chippewas have scored 24 or more in five games, and Ball State's defense hands out points to everyone. Their last meeting, in 2024, finished 37-34, and the 2019 game ended 45-44. I have this at 51.

The room agrees on the total, if nothing else. The Formula has 28-23, Central Michigan Chippewas −4, and likes the Over 47.5. Next Man Up has 26-24 and takes Ball State Cardinals +4, but also likes the Over. Letdown Watch is at 27-21 with Central Michigan and the Over. In The Trenches says the fronts look even, has no score this week, and takes neither side nor total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "Two points. Ball State has lost one-possession games all month. I'll take the four."

Letdown Watch: "Central Michigan has a bowl-eligibility game. Ball State has a Fan Appreciation Day. I know which team is hungrier."

My final is Central Michigan by five with 51 points, three and a half over. Gus gets his Saturday sunshine, and the Chippewas get their sixth win.

display.fanatic_story:
Ball State spent the first three weeks of November playing on Wednesday and Tuesday nights, so Central Michigan Chippewas vs Ball State Cardinals at noon on the Saturday after Thanksgiving feels almost luxurious in Muncie. It's Fan Appreciation Day at Scheumann Stadium, the last game of Mike Uremovich's second season, and Gus Ponder is in his red sweater soaking up actual daylight while Brynn Haverkamp, down from Mount Pleasant in a parka, is here for one thing: win number six.

"Saturday," Gus says, squinting at the sky like a man coming out of a movie theater. "A Saturday game. I'd started eating dinner at halftime. My wife thought I'd joined a bowling league."

"Enjoy it," Brynn says. "We're taking it home with us."

"Taking what? The sunshine?"

"The sixth win. You can keep the sunshine. We have plenty of snow in Mount Pleasant to make up for it."

That's the stake for Central Michigan, and Brynn isn't shy about it. The Chippewas are 5-6. Six wins means a bowl conversation all December. A loss means the season ends on a bus ride north. Last week at Buffalo was rough, a 40-21 loss, but Jadyn Glasser threw three touchdowns, and Brynn insists that counts for something in the moral column.

"There's a moral column?" Gus asks.

"In Mount Pleasant there is. It's next to the hot cocoa."

The heart of this Central Michigan team is a quarterback who runs. Angel Flores leads the Chippewas with 618 rushing yards, and when he's in there the whole offense turns into a long, grinding conversation with your front seven. Glasser handles most of the throwing now. Langston Lewis is the top target, and Mayson Hitchens has 79 tackles from linebacker. Central Michigan beat Akron 41-17 in October and handled Eastern Michigan 35-7 on a neutral field.

"We grind," Brynn says. "We don't do fireworks. We do tractors."

Gus has heard this before. His Cardinals are 3-8, but they've been entertaining in the way that makes your hair go gray. Ball State lost 31-30 in overtime at Massachusetts, beat Bowling Green 32-31 in overtime, and gave Ohio all it wanted last week before falling 35-28. Keldric Luster threw for 257 yards and ran for 109 in that one. TJ Horton has 10 rushing touchdowns, and Eli Hohlt caught four balls for 112 yards in Athens.

"We're the most exciting 3-8 team in America," Gus says. "Nobody leaves early. They can't. Every game comes down to the last drive."

"That's not a brag, Gus. That's a cardiology appointment."

The trouble for Ball State is on the other side of the ball. The Cardinals give up 34.2 points a game, and there's no getting around it. Sterling Smith leads the team with 60 tackles and Jared Badie has 3.5 sacks, but this group has been tested all fall.

There's history to argue about, too. Central Michigan won the last meeting 37-34 back in 2024. Ball State took the 2022 game by a single point. In 2019, Central Michigan won 45-44, and Gus says he still has the scarf he chewed through that day.

"Nine meetings since 2016," Brynn says. "Five for us."

"Four for us," Gus says. "And a whole lot of heartburn for both."

Here's how Saturday goes. The fans get their appreciation in the form of a wild first half. Luster scrambles for a big gain on the first drive, Horton punches it in, and Scheumann is rocking. Central Michigan answers the way it always does, with Flores keeping it on the ground and the clock grinding along. The teams trade touchdowns into the fourth quarter, Gus chewing on his sweater cuff and Brynn pacing like she's waiting on a weather report. Then the Chippewas put together one more long drive, Flores barrels in, and a late Ball State field goal isn't enough.

Brynn will hold up six fingers in the parking lot, then put her mittens back on. Gus will tell her it was the best Saturday he's had all month, and he'll mean it.

My call: Central Michigan Chippewas 28, Ball State Cardinals 23.

display.story_text:
Louisiana Tech vs Georgia Southern decides who hosts the Sun Belt Championship, on a Senior Day and Blue Out at Paulson Stadium, with Georgia Southern chasing its first-ever trip to the league title game. My Louisiana Tech vs Georgia Southern pick is Louisiana Tech Bulldogs +2.5 with the Under 52.5.

Booker "Champ" Tullos has brought his whole Ruston attitude east. "Seven and oh in the conference. Blake Baker has 21 touchdown throws and 1 interception. One. You can count that on one finger, Royce."

Royce Ogeechee doesn't take the bait. "We held Troy to 7 last week and App State to 3 in October. Bring your one interception. Our linebackers will find it."

Both men have a point, and that's why I want the points. Louisiana Tech is 9-2 with losses only at LSU and Baylor, and its defense has two shutouts, 24-0 at UL Monroe and 26-0 over Old Dominion. Alonzo Jackson Jr. leads the Bulldogs in both sacks and tackles, with 11 sacks and 81 stops. Baker threw for 291 yards and 4 touchdowns in the 48-3 win over Arkansas State.

Georgia Southern is 7-4 but 6-1 in the league and has won five straight since the James Madison loss. Max Johnson has 20 touchdown throws and only 3 interceptions, and Alex Taylor has 691 receiving yards. The Eagles gave up 18.3 points a game, and they've been better than that lately.

So why Louisiana Tech? These teams are close to even, and the Bulldogs are 9-2. Tech runs for 4.0 a carry against a Georgia Southern defense that allows 3.5, while the Eagles run for 4.3 against a Tech defense that allows 3.3. Neither team is going to bully the other on the ground, and the quarterback who protects the ball wins a game like this. Baker has thrown 1 interception all year.

The same defenses point to the Under. Seven of Georgia Southern's eleven games finished under 52.5, and Louisiana Tech allows 19.8 a game. DraftKings opened Georgia Southern Eagles −1.5 with a 50.5 total, and the total has climbed two points since. I'll take the Under at the higher number.

The room is together on both. The Formula has Louisiana Tech 26-25, Next Man Up has Louisiana Tech 27-25, and Letdown Watch has Georgia Southern winning 26-25, and all three take Louisiana Tech Bulldogs +2.5 and the Under 52.5. In The Trenches has no pick in this game. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "I've got Georgia Southern winning and I still like Tech with the points. That's called nuance, Next Man Up."

Louisiana Tech Bulldogs vs Georgia Southern Eagles at Paulson Stadium is Senior Day, a Blue Out and First Responders Appreciation all at once, and the winner gets to host the Sun Belt Championship. Royce Ogeechee has been waiting his whole life to see Georgia Southern play for a league title, and Booker "Champ" Tullos drove all the way from Ruston to make sure he waits a little longer.

"Blue Out," Champ says, looking around at the stands. "Y'all picked our color. That's hospitable."

"Ours is a different blue," Royce says. "Older. Wiser. It's been to more championships."

That's the heart of the thing for Royce. The Eagles have won national titles at the lower level and built a proud program in Statesboro, but they have never played in the Sun Belt Championship. One win on Saturday changes that, and it gets the game at home, too.

"First-ever," Royce says. "You know what that word means in Bulloch County? It means my uncle cries in the truck on the way home."

Champ understands. Louisiana Tech has been waiting a while, too. This is the Bulldogs' first year in the Sun Belt, and they've gone 7-0 in it, which is not how most newcomers introduce themselves. Tech is 9-2 overall, with the only losses coming at LSU and at Baylor in September, and the Bulldogs haven't lost a home game or a conference game all year.

"We came into this league like we'd been here forever," Champ says. "Like we were just back from a long hunting trip."

The man Champ wants you to meet is Blake Baker. The quarterback has 21 touchdown throws this year and exactly one interception, and last week he accounted for five touchdowns in a 48-3 win over Arkansas State, four through the air and one on his feet. Jalen Mickens is his go-to receiver, with 805 yards on the year and a 110-yard day last week.

"One interception," Champ says, holding up a single finger. "I keep it up so I don't forget it. Because he won't throw another."

On defense, Tech has a guy Royce has been watching on film all week. Alonzo Jackson Jr. leads the Bulldogs in both sacks and tackles, with 11 sacks and 81 stops. The Bulldogs shut out UL Monroe and Old Dominion back to back in October.

Royce has a quarterback story of his own, and it might be the best one in the league. Max Johnson is a seventh-year quarterback, which in Royce's mind makes him basically a member of the family. He has 20 touchdown throws and only three interceptions, and last week at Troy he went 22 for 26 for 227 yards and three scores. Andre Greene Jr. caught two of those touchdowns.

"Seven years," Royce says. "He's been in college longer than some of our professors. He's earned a home title game."

But the thing Royce is proudest of is the Georgia Southern defense. Against Troy, the Eagles allowed 127 total yards and negative rushing yards. Linebacker Brandon Tyson returned an interception on the very first play of that game. Against App State in October, the Eagles allowed three points.

"Minus seven yards rushing," Royce says. "Troy ran backward all afternoon. We should've charged them for the tour."

These two have only met once before, back in December 2020, and Georgia Southern won that one 38-3. Royce brings it up. Champ points out that none of these players were on the field for it, and also that it was a long time ago, and also that it doesn't count.

Here's how Saturday goes. Both defenses come out swinging, and the first quarter is all punts and loud stands. Johnson finds Taylor for the first touchdown, and Paulson Stadium shakes. Baker answers before halftime with a strike to Mickens. In the second half, it turns into a field-goal game, the kind where every third down feels like the whole season. Georgia Southern takes a two-point lead late. Then Baker, calm as a Sunday morning, drives Tech down the field, and the Bulldogs kick the go-ahead field goal with under a minute to play. Jackson gets home on the last Eagles drive to finish it.

Royce takes it hard, but he takes it like a Georgia Southern man. He shakes Champ's hand, tips his cap to the first responders being honored near the end zone, and tells Champ that the Eagles will be the ones hosting next year.

My call: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs 26, Georgia Southern Eagles 25.

display.fanatic_story:
Margery Vandermolen has never sat in Northwestern's new Ryan Field, and neither has any Illinois team, so she plans to get to Evanston early Saturday and take notes on the place like she's grading it. Illinois Fighting Illini vs Northwestern Wildcats is the Land of Lincoln Trophy game, it's Senior Day for the Wildcats, and Ezra Lindqvist has already written a welcome speech with three footnotes for the visitors.

"Footnote one," Ezra says. "Welcome. Footnote two: the trophy is staying. Footnote three: see footnote two."

"We've had that trophy for two years," Margery says, tapping a slide rule against her orange notebook. "It likes Champaign. It's used to the corn."

She's not wrong about the run. Illinois has won the last two meetings and wants to keep the trophy for a third straight year, and the Illini have done it with a guy Ezra can't stop talking about. Collin Dixon has 80 catches for 1,088 yards and 13 touchdowns. He caught eight balls for 142 yards against Iowa last week, which is the kind of afternoon that makes a secondary go home and stare at the ceiling.

"Dixon is a problem," Ezra admits. "I have a whole chapter on him. It has its own appendix."

The problem for Illinois is that the rest of the Iowa game went badly. The Illini lost 34-17 at home, Katin Houser threw two interceptions after throwing three at UCLA the week before, and the ground game got nowhere. Houser can still sling it, with 2,449 yards and 20 touchdowns, and he threw for 318 against the Hawkeyes, but he's been giving the ball away at the worst times. Matthew Bailey leads the defense with 85 tackles from the secondary, and that group is going to see a lot of running backs on Saturday.

Margery has a bigger memory to hold onto, one from this very season. Illinois beat Oregon 21-10 in October. Nobody in Champaign has stopped talking about it.

"We beat the Ducks," she says. "I graphed it. The graph is one arrow pointing up."

Northwestern is coming off a rough month and isn't hiding from it. The Wildcats have dropped four in a row, the last one a 20-17 heartbreaker at Minnesota. Nicco Marchiol led a 10-play, 70-yard drive late in the fourth quarter and ran in the tying touchdown from seven yards out, and then the Gophers kicked a 44-yard field goal on the last play. Before that, Griffin Wilde had caught a 49-yard touchdown to cap a 98-yard drive right before halftime.

"Ninety-eight yards," Ezra says. "I footnoted that one twice."

Marchiol has taken the most throws in each of the last three games, and he's been steady, with a touchdown in each. The real engine is Caleb Komolafe, the redshirt junior running back who went for 109 yards on 19 carries in Minneapolis and now has seven career games over 100 yards, the most by a Wildcat since Evan Hull. Wilde has 920 receiving yards. Braydon Brus leads the defense in tackles and sacks.

"Komolafe against your run defense is my whole thesis," Ezra says. "The rest is citations."

The Wildcats are 5-1 at home this year, and the seniors are walking out of the tunnel for the last time in a building most of them only got to call home this season. That counts for something on a cold November morning by the lake.

Here's how Saturday goes. Illinois goes right to Dixon early, and he gets his catches, because he always does. Northwestern answers the way it wants to, feeding Komolafe until the Illinois front gets tired. Marchiol hits Wilde for a big gain in the second quarter, the Wildcats take a lead into the half, and Houser has to throw his way back into it. He moves the ball, but the Northwestern defense gets one big stop in the fourth quarter, and Komolafe grinds out the last few minutes behind the senior linemen.

Ezra marches down to the field and publishes a correction to everybody who wrote off the Wildcats in November. Margery tucks her slide rule into her coat, writes "next year, Champaign" in orange ink, and underlines it twice.

My call: Northwestern Wildcats 28, Illinois Fighting Illini 21.

Lane Kiffin's first LSU season has gone sideways in November, and now the Tigers climb The Hill in Fayetteville for the Golden Boot on Arkansas's Senior Day. For LSU vs Arkansas, the spread and total I'm playing are Arkansas Razorbacks +14.5 and the Over 48.5.

Cece Thibodeaux has stopped apologizing for the month. "Alabama, Texas by one, Tennessee. Fine. We still beat Clemson 51-10 and Texas A&M 35-6. Bubba, the Boot's been ours four years running. Pack it gently."

Bubba Fayette-Dorsey is one week removed from a 45-3 loss in Austin and still talking. "We beat South Carolina 34-6 two weeks ago. Coach Silverfield's got these boys playing hard at home. You come up here at lunchtime with a three-game skid. Good luck with that."

LSU has the talent. Sam Leavitt has 3,019 yards and 20 touchdowns, Jackson Harris has 871 receiving yards, and Princewill Umanmielen has 9.5 sacks. The defense allows 18.9 points a game. That's a team that should win this game by double digits.

The problem is the road and the turnovers. LSU is 1-3 away from home this year, and Leavitt has thrown 12 interceptions, three of them in the one-point loss to Texas. The LSU offense hasn't topped 21 points in any of its last three games. It's hard to lay two touchdowns with a team that hasn't scored three in a month.

Arkansas isn't good, but it's better at home. KJ Jackson has thrown for 2,231 yards, and Chris Marshall has 867 receiving yards and caught nine balls for 106 in Austin. The Razorbacks lost by seven to Tennessee and by three at Auburn. This is a senior class that will want one more good afternoon.

The total opened at 47.5 at DraftKings and ticked up a point. LSU's season scoring of 33.5 points a game says the Tigers have it in them, and Arkansas gives up 27.1. If LSU's offense wakes up, the Hogs still find enough on the other end to push it over.

LSU Tigers 31, Arkansas Razorbacks 18 is a 13-point win, a point and a half short of the spread, and 49 total points, half a point past 48.5.

The three scoring cards are all on the Hogs with the points. The Formula has LSU 31-18 with Arkansas Razorbacks +14.5 and the Over 48.5. Next Man Up has 31-19, likes Arkansas and takes the Over. Letdown Watch has 30-19, likes Arkansas plus the points and takes the Over. In The Trenches calls the two fronts even and has no score and no side this week. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "A team that lost three straight playing on the road at lunchtime? I've been waiting all year for this one."

Next Man Up: "You've been waiting all year for every one of them. That's your whole personality."

The Tigers keep the Boot, Bubba gets a fourth quarter he can live with, and the Hogs hang inside two touchdowns for their seniors.

LSU Tigers 31, Arkansas Razorbacks 18. Arkansas Razorbacks cover the 14.5. Over 48.5.

Razorback Stadium will glow red on Friday night, the way it has before every home game since 2014, and by Saturday morning Bubba Fayette-Dorsey intends to be at HogTown on Maple Street for the Hog Walk, two and a half hours before LSU Tigers vs Arkansas Razorbacks kicks off. Cece Thibodeaux drove up from Baton Rouge for the Battle for the Golden Boot and says she plans to take the trophy home in the passenger seat, buckled in.

"It rides up front," Cece says. "It's been riding up front for four years."

"That's a long time to have a boot in your car," Bubba says.

"It's a gold boot, Bubba. It gets whatever seat it wants."

Bubba concedes the point. LSU has won the Boot four straight times and nine of the last ten. The last Arkansas win in the series came in overtime in Baton Rouge in 2021, 16-13, and Bubba still has the box score in his wallet. It has gotten soft from all the folding.

But this is a different weekend than most of the ones Cece has spent winning that trophy. LSU is 6-5 and has lost three in a row: Alabama by 18, Texas by one and Tennessee by 14 last week in Knoxville. Lane Kiffin's first season went from a 51-10 win over Clemson in September to a long, gray November, and the playoff talk in Baton Rouge has gone quiet.

"I'm not here to talk about November," Cece says. "I'm here to talk about Sam Leavitt."

Leavitt has thrown for 3,019 yards and 20 touchdowns. He threw for 388 at Auburn and 380 against Alabama. Jackson Harris has 871 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns, and Trey'Dez Green caught seven balls and a score at Tennessee. On defense, Princewill Umanmielen has 9.5 sacks and TJ Dottery has 83 tackles, and the Tigers have only given up 18.9 points a game.

"We lost to Texas by one," Cece says. "One. And we gave Alabama everything they wanted for a half. That's not a bad team. That's a team that got unlucky in the wrong month."

Bubba nods, politely, like a man who has heard a lot of LSU fans say that over the years.

He has his own bad month to explain. Arkansas lost 45-3 at Texas last Saturday. Two weeks before that, the Razorbacks lost 26-23 at Auburn, and in between, they crushed South Carolina 34-6 at home. Ryan Silverfield is in his first year in Fayetteville, and the team is 4-7, but Bubba will tell you the Hogs play harder on The Hill than anywhere else.

"Look at Tennessee," he says. "Lost by seven. Look at South Carolina. That's who we are at home."

KJ Jackson has thrown for 2,231 yards. Chris Marshall has 867 receiving yards, and he caught nine for 106 in Austin when nothing else was working. Cam Settles leads the ground game, and Khmori House has 70 tackles in the secondary. It's Senior Day, the band has its Senior Best Of Show at halftime, and there's a DJ battle at HogTown before kickoff.

"A DJ battle," Cece says. "You're really pulling out everything."

"You're in the Ozarks now," Bubba says. "We throw a party when we feel like it."

Here's how I see the afternoon. The crowd is up before the opening kick, the flyover rattles the press box, and Arkansas scores first on a long Jackson throw to Marshall that brings out every Hog call in the building.
