Senior Day at Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium closes East Carolina's home schedule, and Florida Atlantic Owls vs East Carolina Pirates gives Greenville a 1 p.m. send-off against a team that throws the ball like it's trying to empty the building. Bart Quidley has a purple flag flying from his truck bed and a speech ready for every senior, and Kaia Brightwater has come up from Boca Raton with sunscreen in her bag out of habit and an Owls team that is already going bowling for the first time since 2020.

"Bowl team," Kaia says, before she's even sat down. "Bowl. Team. I'm going to keep saying it until it feels normal."

"Say it all you want," Bart says. "We've beaten you three straight. Twenty-two to seven. Forty-nine to fourteen. Forty-two to three last year. You've scored twenty-four points in three games against us, Kaia."

"That was before Veltkamp."

That's the name Kaia has been saying all season like it's a weather forecast for sunshine. Caden Veltkamp has thrown for 3,472 yards with 33 touchdowns and just six interceptions. Last week he went 30 for 38 for 386 yards and four scores against South Florida. Easton Messer has 90 catches, 1,097 yards and 15 touchdowns. Under Zach Kittley, the Owls score 38 points a game and treat the clock like a suggestion.

"We don't run plays," Kaia says. "We run sprints. The other team has to chase us around for three hours."

Bart nods slowly. "And then what happened at Florida?"

Kaia's smile drops a few degrees. "Sixty-six," she says quietly. "We don't talk about it."

"And Army?"

"We definitely don't talk about Army."

Bart has reason to be smug. Florida Atlantic gives up 33.4 points a game, and on the road the Owls have been shaky, losing 56-24 at Army, 48-41 at North Texas and 38-21 at Tulsa. East Carolina, meanwhile, is 7-4, second in the American, and riding four straight wins. They just haven't been pretty. The Pirates beat Temple 17-9, South Florida 20-17, Charlotte 17-16 and then Army 10-6 at West Point last week.

"Ten to six," Kaia says. "Ten. That's not a score. That's a phone number missing some digits."

"It's a win," Bart says. "Our defense held Army to six points at West Point. You gave Army fifty-six."

He has her there, and he knows it. Crews Law leads the Pirates with 74 tackles from linebacker, and Kendrick DuJour is the guy who brings the pressure. TJ Engleman Jr. carries the offense with 808 rushing yards, and he ran 22 times for 113 yards against Army. Emory Williams handles the throwing, and Landon Sides is his top target. It's a team built to shorten the game and squeeze the other side.

"We're a pirate ship," Bart says. "We don't race. We board."

"That's a terrible metaphor."

"It's the only kind of metaphor we have in Greenville."

There's a real question underneath all the jokes. East Carolina's offense hasn't topped 20 points in a month. To beat this team, the Pirates are going to have to score like they did a year ago, when they put up 42 on the Owls. Kaia thinks they can't. Bart thinks Senior Day is the day they will.

Here's how Saturday goes. The seniors walk out to a purple roar, and Florida Atlantic wastes no time spoiling the mood, with Veltkamp hitting Messer for a long touchdown on the first drive. East Carolina answers with Engleman, carry after carry, and the Pirates tie it before the first quarter ends. The two teams trade scores all afternoon, the Owls through the air and the Pirates on the ground, and it's tied going into the fourth. Then Law makes the play of the day, a third-down stop that forces a field goal, and East Carolina marches down for one more score. Veltkamp gets the ball back with a chance, but DuJour gets to him on the last drive, and the Pirates hang on.

Bart will climb into his truck bed and wave the purple flag until the last senior leaves the field. Kaia will stand under it, shake her head and say, "Bowl team," one more time anyway.

My call: East Carolina Pirates 30, Florida Atlantic Owls 27.

But Brock Glenn is a tough runner with 642 yards and 9 touchdowns on the ground, and the Hilltoppers beat Missouri State 34-13 and Jacksonville State 34-24 at home. display.fanatic_story:
Kennesaw State Owls vs Western Kentucky Hilltoppers is Senior Day and Big Red, White and Blue Day in Bowling Green, part of the country's 250th birthday celebration, with the whole crowd asked to wear red and the Big Red Marching Band leading the team down Avenue of Champions for one last Topper Walk. Tops Whitsitt closed his barber shop early to be there, and Ximena Holcombe-Reyes rode up from Kennesaw with a four-game winning streak and a plan to make it five.

"Red, white and blue," Ximena says. "I'm wearing two of the three. I'll let you figure out which one's missing."

"Red's the important one," Tops says. "Red's what we wear. Big Red's what we hug. The rest is just decoration."

Tops has seen a lot of this season from his barber chair. Western Kentucky is 4-7, and every customer since September has had a theory about what went wrong. A brutal early stretch didn't help: the Hilltoppers played at Nevada, at Georgia and at Indiana in the first three weeks. Then came a long, uneven fall, with a big win over Missouri State and a 34-24 Homecoming win over Jacksonville State sprinkled in among the losses.

"I tell everybody the same thing," Tops says. "Keep your head still and let me finish. It's good advice for a haircut and a football season."

The seniors are what Tops came for. This is their final regular-season home game, and he plans to clap for every name. The Hilltoppers are 3-1 at home this year, and he'd like to make it 4-1 before anybody gets to the parking lot.

Ximena's team is on a different road entirely. Kennesaw State started 1-6, lost three straight one-score games in late September and October, and looked like a team that would be done by Halloween. Then something clicked. The Owls won at Middle Tennessee, beat Delaware 42-40, won at Sam Houston 26-7 and handled FIU 35-24 last week. A win in Bowling Green gets them to six.

"We're still building this program," Ximena says. "Brick by brick. Every year, we add a new floor. This year we might add a whole bowl game on top."

The guy holding the bricks is Landon Varnes. He took over most of the throwing in early November, and the Owls haven't lost since. Last week he went 21 for 27 for 219 yards and two touchdowns. Boogie Woods III is the engine, with 649 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns on the ground, and he ran for 100 yards and two scores against FIU. Dylan Gary leads the Owls in receiving yards.

"Boogie," Ximena says. "You can't stop a guy named Boogie. It's not allowed."

Tops has his own answer in Brock Glenn, who leads Western Kentucky in both throwing and running. He has 642 rushing yards and nine touchdowns on the ground. When a play breaks down, he's the most dangerous Hilltopper on the field. Jonathan Stafford Jr. has 61 catches and is the receiver Glenn trusts on third down. Jaylen Lewis leads the defense in tackles.

"Brock runs like he's late for his own wedding," Tops says. "You don't want to be standing in the aisle."

The only time these two programs have met, in 2024, Western Kentucky won 31-14. Tops mentions it once, politely, and Ximena points out that this is a different Kennesaw State team. Both of them are right.

Here's how Saturday goes. Kennesaw State comes out running, and Woods pounds out an early score. Glenn answers with his legs, breaking a long run up the middle that gets the red in the stands on its feet. It's tight all afternoon, a game of long drives and field goals. Varnes hits Gary for a touchdown in the third quarter, and Western Kentucky answers again. With a couple of minutes left, the Hilltoppers get one last chance, but the Owls' defense holds near midfield, and Kennesaw State runs out the clock.

When it's over, Tops claps for the seniors as they walk off Feix Field for the last time, and then he walks over to Ximena and tells her he'd give her a free haircut if she ever needs one, but she'll have to come to Bowling Green and sit in a red chair to get it.

My call: Kennesaw State Owls 28, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 26.

display.fanatic_story:
The last time Marshall and the school in Monroe played for something big, it was 1987 in Pocatello, Idaho, and the Northeast Louisiana Indians beat the Herd 43-42 for the I-AA national championship. Marshall Thundering Herd vs UL Monroe Warhawks on Saturday is the Herd's first trip ever to Monroe, and Darnell Vidrine has been playing tapes of that title game on his overnight radio show all week while Mercy Holderby pretends she can't hear him.

"Forty-three to forty-two," Darnell says. "I was not born yet. I remember it anyway."

"You're welcome to remember it," Mercy says. "We remember 2024. Twenty-eight to twenty-three, in Huntington, on the way to a conference title."

That's the whole series, as far as the record books go: one wild title game when ULM still had another name, and one Marshall win at the FBS level two years ago. Saturday is the tiebreaker, and Darnell is treating it like a national holiday. His optimism counter, the one he resets to a hundred every week no matter what happened the week before, is at a hundred and ten.

"That's illegal," Mercy says.

"That's faith," Darnell says.

He needs it. UL Monroe is 2-9, and the two wins came on the road, 21-14 at Troy and 19-17 at Arkansas State. But last week the Warhawks went up to Boone and took App State to overtime before losing 17-16, and Austin Carlisle played the best game of his year. He threw for 167 yards and a touchdown and ran for another, and he leads the team with 524 rushing yards. Aidan Armenta has thrown for more yards this season, but Carlisle is the one who's been making things happen lately. Marcellus Jackson leads the receivers with 421 yards. Noah Flemmings has 95 tackles at linebacker, and Kevontay Wells has 4 sacks up front.

"Austin Carlisle runs like he's got somewhere to be," Darnell says. "Usually that place is the end zone. Sometimes it's the sideline. I love him either way."

Mercy is not here to make friends. Marshall is 6-5 and already has its six wins, and the Herd just beat Georgia State 28-27 in a game that came down to the wire. Carlos Del Rio-Wilson threw three touchdowns in that one, including a 94-yarder to Chris Culliver on Culliver's only catch of the day. That's the kind of thing that happens when the Herd lets it fly. Del Rio-Wilson threw for 413 yards against Gardner-Webb back in September, so he can do it.

"We are," Mercy says, before anybody even asks how she's doing.

Jo'Shon Barbie leads the backs with 482 yards, Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw leads the receivers, and Caleb Clark-Glover has 82 tackles from the secondary. Kenyatta Hardge has 3.5 sacks.

Neither defense is going to win any awards. Marshall gives up 30.4 points a game, ULM gives up 33.8, and both of them have had days they'd rather forget. The Herd lost 45-0 at Penn State in the opener and 49-13 at Georgia Southern. ULM lost 62-13 at Mississippi State and 52-35 at South Alabama.

"So it's going to be a shootout," Darnell says.

"It's going to be a Marshall shootout," Mercy says. "We'll let you shoot. We'll just shoot more."

Here's how Saturday goes. Monroe comes out loud for a 2-9 team, because it's the last home game and there's nothing else on the schedule. Carlisle runs for a long one on the opening drive and Darnell is out of his seat. Marshall answers through the air, Del Rio-Wilson finds Turner-Bradshaw twice, and the game turns into the kind of back-and-forth afternoon both defenses would rather not watch on film. The Herd gets a late stop, Barbie grinds out a few first downs, and Marshall leaves Louisiana with a seventh win and the series lead.

Mercy ties a fresh green ribbon on her microphone in the parking lot. Darnell signs on for his overnight show, announces the score, resets the counter to a hundred, and plays the 1987 tape one more time anyway.

My call: Marshall Thundering Herd 29, UL Monroe Warhawks 24.

Downtown Norfolk's Great Hot Cocoa War ends Saturday, the same afternoon Old Dominion hosts Southern Miss for Senior Day and Military Appreciation at S.B. Ballard Stadium. Two 3-8 teams, one last game, and a Southern Miss vs Old Dominion prediction that takes Southern Miss Golden Eagles +6 and the Over 50.5.

Winnie Pocklington has her cup and her side picked. "We went to Conway and held Coastal to 8 points. We play defense in this town, Dee. Ask anybody at the shipyard."

Dee Broussard is not impressed. "Winnie, your team scored 17 points a game this year. We scored 35 last week and lost. Our problem is the other end. Yours is every end."

Dee has the stronger argument. The two teams have the same record, but they got there in very different ways. Southern Miss scores 27.6 points a game and allows 36.8. Old Dominion scores 17.2 and allows 26.1. Only one of these offenses can win a shootout, and it isn't the home team.

John White has taken the throws for Southern Miss the last three weeks, and he threw for 294 yards and three touchdowns against South Alabama. Mario Sanders caught seven of those for 143 yards and two scores, and he has 960 receiving yards with 9 touchdowns on the season. Steven Robinson has 958 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns.

Old Dominion has been stuck in neutral. Jaxon Potter has taken the throws the last four games and has two touchdown throws on the season against five interceptions. Devin Roche leads the backs with 481 yards. The Monarchs were shut out at Louisiana Tech and scored 10 at Georgia State. Their defense, led by Lucas Struck with 77 tackles and Javen Gibson with 5.5 sacks, has carried them.

DraftKings opened ODU at 4.5 and the total at 50.5. The side has crept up, and I'll take the extra point and a half with the better offense.

On the total, the case is simple. Southern Miss games pile up points because of that defense, and the Golden Eagles have allowed 40 or more four times this year. Even a sleepy ODU offense should get into the high 20s against that group.

Old Dominion Monarchs 29, Southern Miss Golden Eagles 24 is a 5-point win, a point short of the spread, with 53 total points, two and a half past 50.5.

The three scoring cards agree on all of it. The Formula has Old Dominion 28-25 and likes Southern Miss Golden Eagles +6 and the Over 50.5. Next Man Up has 28-23 with the Golden Eagles and the Over. Letdown Watch has 29-24, takes Southern Miss plus the points and likes the Over. In The Trenches sees the fronts as a split and has no score and no side this week. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "Three of us on the same side. Somebody check if we accidentally copied The Formula's homework."

The Formula: "You did. You're welcome."

ODU's seniors win their last home game, Dee drinks her cocoa on the losing side, and Southern Miss keeps it to a field goal and change.

display.fanatic_story:
The cups are already out on Granby Street, and the marshmallows in downtown Norfolk are about the size of a fist. The Great Hot Cocoa War ends Saturday, the same day Southern Miss Golden Eagles vs Old Dominion Monarchs closes the season at S.B. Ballard Stadium, and Winnie Pocklington has told Dee Broussard that she has to choose a side in both.

"It says it right on the sign," Winnie says. "Get your cup and choose your side."

"Easy," Dee says. "I choose the side that scores."

Winnie lets that one go, because it's Senior Day and Military Appreciation at Old Dominion, and in a Navy town that matters more than a hot chocolate argument. The Monarchs will honor their seniors before kickoff and the service members in the stands all afternoon, and Winnie plans to spend the first half thanking people and the second half yelling at the officials, which she considers a balanced day.

Both teams are 3-8. Both have had the kind of season that makes a fan count the days to spring practice. But the two records came about in totally different ways, and Dee has been explaining the difference since she arrived from Hattiesburg.

"Our problem is defense," she says. "Yours is everything else."

Southern Miss allows 36.8 points a game, and that's how a team that scores 27.6 ends up 3-8. The Golden Eagles lost 63-31 at Louisiana Tech, 54-23 to James Madison and 55-34 at Troy. Last week they scored 35 against South Alabama on Senior Day at The Rock and still lost by five. John White threw for 294 yards and three touchdowns in that game, and Mario Sanders caught seven balls for 143 yards and two scores.

"Mario can play for anybody," Dee says. "Put him in a crowd and he's the one that comes out with the ball."

Sanders has 960 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns. Steven Robinson has run for 958 yards and 11 touchdowns. Mathis Haygood leads the defense with 97 tackles, and Jameer Lewis has 4.5 sacks. When the offense gets rolling, Southern Miss can keep up with anyone in the Sun Belt. The trouble is, so can the other team.

Winnie's team is the reverse. Old Dominion allows 26.1 points a game, which is respectable, and scores 17.2, which is not. The Monarchs went to Conway two weeks ago and beat Coastal Carolina 21-8, and Winnie talks about that game the way some people talk about their wedding day. They also lost 26-0 at Louisiana Tech and 42-10 at Georgia State.

"We don't score," Winnie says. "I know. You know. Everybody on the Elizabeth River knows. But Jaxon Potter just went 23 for 29 at UConn. He's figuring it out."

Potter has taken the throws for four straight weeks. Josh Rodriguez is the top receiver with 514 yards, and Devin Roche caught seven balls and a touchdown at UConn on top of leading the backs. On defense, Lucas Struck has 77 tackles from safety, and Javen Gibson has 5.5 sacks.

"Our defense is going to be the best defense Mario Sanders sees all year," Winnie says.

"He's seen Auburn," Dee says.

"Then the second best."

Here's how I see Saturday. ODU comes out of the pregame ceremony fired up and scores on its first drive, with Potter hitting Rodriguez on a third down that wakes up the whole stadium. Southern Miss answers right away when White finds Sanders deep. That sets the tone, and the game turns into exactly what Winnie was afraid of: two defenses getting tired. Robinson runs for a couple of scores, Roche gets in from close range, and the Monarchs take the lead for good on a field goal and a late touchdown run. Sanders gets one more score in the final minutes to make the seniors sweat, and ODU holds on.

Dee and Winnie walk back downtown afterward, because the Cocoa War is still on until the end of the night. Dee buys two cups from the stand Winnie hates, and makes her drink one on the way to the car.

My call: Old Dominion Monarchs 29, Southern Miss Golden Eagles 24.

display.story_text:
The Knights make their first-ever trip to Boulder exactly 29 years after Scott Frost quarterbacked Nebraska to a win at Folsom Field. Now he brings the Knights in as the coach, and my UCF vs Colorado prediction is UCF Knights +2.5 on the spread with the Under 51.5 on the over/under.

Moss Feldstein is already defending the altitude. "Nobody comes up here for the first time and feels great, Knox. Ask your lungs in the second half."

Knox Brevard-Stiles grins. "My lungs are bowl eligible, Moss. Yours aren't."

That's the gap in motivation. UCF beat Iowa State 48-17 to reach 6-5. Colorado lost 28-35 at Cincinnati, fell to 4-7, and is playing for pride in its finale. Alonza Barnett III has taken the job back this month and threw four touchdowns against Iowa State, three of them to Josh Derry, who had 125 yards. UCF Knights vs Colorado Buffaloes is the first football game UCF has ever played in Boulder, and it falls on November 28, the same date that Scott Frost, now the Knights' coach, ran in a touchdown as Nebraska's quarterback here 29 years ago. Knox Brevard-Stiles is treating the whole trip like the opening day of a new ride, while Moss Feldstein, who has watched every visitor show up at Folsom Field gasping for air, is waiting with a thermos of hot chocolate and a grin.

"First time in Boulder," Knox says, staring up at the Flatirons. "Look at that. That's a postcard. That's a screensaver."

"That's a mile of altitude," Moss says. "Enjoy the view in the first quarter. In the third quarter you're going to be looking at the ground."

"I'm from Orlando, Moss. I've waited two hours for a roller coaster in August. I can handle a little less oxygen."

That isn't the kind of brag Moss is used to hearing, and he takes a second to respect it. Then he goes right back to work, because he has a home game to defend. Colorado is 4-7 and the bowl dream died last week in a 35-28 loss at Cincinnati, but this is still the Buffaloes' last game of the season, and nobody in Boulder wants to send the team into winter on a losing note.

"We're playing for pride," Moss says. "Pride is a powerful thing at altitude. It's lighter up here, so you can carry more of it."

Knox has more than pride on his side. UCF is 6-5 after a 48-17 thumping of Iowa State last week, which makes the Knights bowl eligible. Alonza Barnett III threw four touchdowns in that game, three of them to Josh Derry, and Duke Watson ran for 113 yards. Derry has 833 receiving yards on the year. Tackett Curtis leads the defense with 69 tackles, and Isaiah Nixon brings the pressure off the end. UCF also knocked off BYU in double overtime back in October, a win Knox has framed in his living room.

"We beat a top-two team," Knox says. "Twice overtime. My heart rate still hasn't recovered."

"And then you lost to Baylor by thirty-two," Moss says.

"We don't ride that ride anymore. It's closed for maintenance."

Moss's best case is his top receiver. Joseph Williams has 67 catches for 1,045 yards and eight touchdowns, and he went for 112 yards against Cincinnati. Isaac Wilson threw for 312 yards in that game, though he also threw three interceptions, and Moss admits the turnovers keep him up at night. Wilson has 12 touchdown throws and 12 interceptions. JaQuail Smith leads the backfield.

"Isaac is a gunslinger," Moss says. "Sometimes the gun slings back."

The two programs have met once, in Orlando two years ago, and Colorado won that one 48-21. Moss reminds Knox about it twice before kickoff. Knox reminds Moss that UCF has a different quarterback, a different coach and, as of last week, a bowl game to look forward to.

There's also the Frost connection, which Moss finds a little personal. Twenty-nine years ago today, the man on UCF's sideline ran 19 yards for a touchdown in a 27-24 Nebraska win on this field. In 2019, as Nebraska's coach, he watched Colorado come back from 17 points down and win in overtime.

"So he's one and one in Boulder," Moss says. "Today's the rubber match."

"Rubber match," Knox says. "I like the sound of that."

Here's how Saturday goes. Colorado comes out fired up, and Wilson finds Williams deep for a touchdown on the first possession, sending Folsom Field into a frenzy. UCF answers with Watson grinding up the middle, and Barnett hits Derry on a long one before halftime. The teams trade scores in the third quarter, and Knox starts breathing a little harder, though he swears it's nerves and not the altitude. Late in the fourth, with the score tied, Wilson tries to force one more throw, and the Knights intercept it near midfield. Barnett moves UCF into range, and the Knights kick the go-ahead field goal. Colorado gets one last shot and comes up just short.

Knox will take one last photo of the Flatirons on the way out. Moss will tell him to come back in the spring, when the air is easier and the Buffaloes are, too.

My call: UCF Knights 26, Colorado Buffaloes 25.

display.fanatic_story:
Kansas State Wildcats vs Iowa State Cyclones is Farmageddon, and this year it comes with a lump in the throat. These two have played every season since 1917, and the Big 12 schedule doesn't have them meeting in 2027, so Saturday at Jack Trice Stadium could be the last one for a while. Hattie Brandvold drove up from Manhattan for it, and Twyla Hemmingsen has been in Ames all week, getting more nervous every day.

"Since 1917," Twyla says. "My great-grandpa could've gone to the first one. He didn't. He had cows. But he could have."

"Mine went to every one he could," Hattie says. "He'd be furious about this. He'd write a letter. To somebody. In pencil."

Neither of them can believe it. This rivalry is two farm towns and two fan bases that know exactly what the other one had for breakfast. And now nobody knows when it comes back.

"So we have to make this one count," Twyla says. "And I need it to count for us, because we're 5-6."

That's the other part of the story. Iowa State needs this win to reach six and go to a bowl game in Jimmy Rogers' first year as head coach. The Cyclones have been up and down all fall. They beat West Virginia 45-42 and Oklahoma State 51-49 at home, then lost by double digits on the road at BYU, Arizona and UCF. The loss in Orlando last week was ugly, 48-17.

"We're a different team at home," Twyla says. "At home, we're the team I raised. On the road, we're a teenager."

Hattie's team can't get to six. Kansas State is 4-7 in Collin Klein's first year, and the Wildcats have lost five straight. Some of those hurt more than others. Last week in the rain in Manhattan, Kansas State had an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter against Arizona and lost 35-28 in overtime. The week before that it was 10-20 at TCU. Before that, the Wildcats took Colorado to overtime and lost by three.

"We've been close so many times I should get a punch card," Hattie says. "Ten close ones, and you get a free win. We're due."

And that's what makes her dangerous on Saturday. Kansas State has nothing to lose and everything to spoil. Nothing would make Hattie happier than to drive home knowing the Cyclones are spending December at home.

"That's my bowl game," she says. "You not having one."

The man Twyla is counting on is Aiden Flora. The running back has 1,506 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns, and he went for 171 yards and two scores even in the loss at UCF. When he gets to the second level, he's gone.

"Fifteen hundred yards," Twyla says. "In the Big 12. And nobody outside of Ames talks about him. Good. Keep it quiet. Let him surprise people."

Kansas State has a runner of its own. Rodney Fields Jr. had his best day of the year against Arizona, 144 yards on 28 carries, and he has 751 on the season. The Wildcats have used several quarterbacks this fall, and Dillon Duff took most of the throws the last two weeks. Hattie wants the ball in Fields' hands until his arms get tired.

"Run it at them," she says. "Run it at them, run it again, and run it some more. That's what my granddad would've said, if he weren't busy writing his letter."

Iowa State has won three straight in this series, including the opener in Dublin, Ireland, to start last season, 24-21. Twyla brings up Ireland a lot. Hattie mentions that the Wildcats won 10-9 in 2022, which in her mind was the finest football game ever played.

Here's how Saturday goes. Both teams come out running, and neither defense can stop it for very long. Flora breaks a long one in the first quarter, and Fields answers with a touchdown drive that eats half the second quarter. It's a back-and-forth game all afternoon, the kind this rivalry has always been. Iowa State takes a late lead on a Flora run, and Kansas State gets one last chance but comes up short near midfield. The Cyclones get to six.

When it's over, the two of them stand at the rail longer than everybody else, and neither one wants to be the first to leave. Hattie finally says it: see you whenever they let us do this again. Twyla says she'll be here, and that she'll save Hattie a seat.

My call: Iowa State Cyclones 30, Kansas State Wildcats 27.

Rice closes its season Saturday with Senior Day and Salute to Service Day at First Community Stadium, honoring members of the military on the same afternoon the Army Black Knights come to Houston needing a sixth win. My Army vs Rice pick is Army Black Knights −6.5 and the Over 48.5, because the cadets have a bowl to chase and the Owls haven't shown they can stop a team that runs it at them.

Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke has the plan laid out like a supply route. "Five wins. One more before Navy. Cale Hellums carries it, the backs carry the rest, and we're on the bus by dark."

Odalys Chen-Moreau polices that take on arrival. "Three straight losses, Captain. Six points against East Carolina. Your sample's trending the wrong way."

She's not wrong. Army lost 49-22 at Memphis, 24-21 to Air Force and 10-6 at home to East Carolina, and the offense didn't reach the end zone in the last one. Hellums went 7 of 16 throwing and ran 19 times for 62 yards. That's the bad news.

The good news is what Hellums is when things go right. He has 970 rushing yards and 18 touchdowns this year, and Army put up 56 on Florida Atlantic and 38 at Tulsa with him running the show. Army scores 29.6 a game. Rice gives up 32.1, and the Owls allowed 51 at FAU and 52 at North Texas in back-to-back games before tightening up. An option team that holds the ball against a defense that struggles to get off the field is how a game gets away.

Rice does come in feeling good. The Owls won 31-27 at Temple last Thursday, and D'Andre Hardeman Jr. ran for 137 yards on 17 carries. Gael Ochoa threw two touchdowns. But Rice is 2-9 and has scored 21.7 a game, and it hasn't beaten an FBS team at home this season. Army has won the last four meetings, including 37-14 in 2024.

My margin is nine. That clears the number by two and a half and leaves room for a late Rice score.

The Over is the closer call against an Army team that likes to shorten games. But Rice's games have gone past 48.5 in 7 of 11, and the Black Knights' defense has given up 24 or more in four of its last six. I have 51. DraftKings opened Army Black Knights −7.5 with a 50.5 total, and the side has dropped a point and the total two, to −6.5 and 48.5.

Every card in the room is on Army and the Over. The Formula has Army 30-23 with the Black Knights −6.5 and likes the Over 48.5. Next Man Up has 29-20, likes Army and goes Over. Thaddeus Rourke will spend the pregame standing at attention and Odalys Chen-Moreau will spend it trying to explain to him that the ceremony is not technically for him.

"I'm a retired officer at a Salute to Service game," the Captain says. "It's a little bit for me."

"It's for everyone who served," Odalys says. "You're in the sample. You're not the whole sample."

Rice will honor its seniors before kickoff and honor members of the military during the game, and the Captain is treating the whole afternoon like a mission briefing. He has a laminated card. It has the kickoff time, the parking plan, and the words "BEAT NAVY" written at the bottom, even though Navy is nowhere near Houston this week.

"It's always relevant," he says.

The Captain stands, salutes the field, almost smiles, and tells Odalys a dad joke about a supply truck. She rates it as not significant. Then he says it: "Beat Navy."

My call: Army Black Knights 30, Rice Owls 21.

The Marching Royal Dukes alumni are coming back to Harrisonburg this weekend, and Lila Shenandoah has already told three of them where to sit. Coastal Carolina Chanticleers vs James Madison Dukes is Senior Day, the MRD Alumni Game and Letterwinner Weekend all at once at Bridgeforth Stadium, and Marigold "Goldie" Seabrook has driven up from the Grand Strand to watch the whole purple-and-gold reunion.

"Every old trumpet player in Virginia is going to be in the stands," Lila says. "We're going to be loud, and we're going to be on key."

"I've heard about the on-key part," Goldie says. "I'd like to see some evidence."

Lila laughs that cheer-captain laugh. Then she gets to the stakes, because it's Senior Day and JMU has some explaining to do. The Dukes are 8-3, and they went into their bye week after a 46-22 loss at UConn that nobody in the Shenandoah Valley wants to replay. Before that, they'd lost two overtime games in a row, 34-31 at App State and 24-21 to Troy at home.

"Two overtime losses and one bad day in Connecticut," Lila says. "That's three losses. We had two weeks to think about it. You don't want to be the team that walks in after a JMU bye."

Goldie's team has had a different kind of year. Coastal Carolina is 4-7. The Chanticleers lost 21-8 to Old Dominion at home the week after a win at Georgia State, then beat Arkansas State and lost 38-24 at Louisiana last Saturday. Deuce Bailey has thrown for 2,517 yards and 21 touchdowns, and he can make throws that make you sit up. He also has 11 interceptions, and Goldie flinches every time he cocks his arm into traffic.

"Deuce is a gunslinger," Goldie says. "Sometimes the gun goes off in the wrong direction."

That's the worry against a JMU defense that has given up 21.7 points a game. JT Hooten has 6 sacks from linebacker, and Nakian Jackson has 82 tackles. Lila expects Saturday to look a lot more like the 54-23 night at Southern Miss than the one in Connecticut.

The history doesn't help Goldie, either. The Dukes have played the Chanticleers four times as Sun Belt teams and won all four, by scores like 47-7, 56-14 and last year's 59-10. Lila keeps those numbers in her phone. Goldie keeps hers in a drawer she doesn't open.

"That's history," Goldie says. "We're talking about this Saturday."

"So am I. This Saturday, there's free fries."

That much is true. Every time the Dukes kick a field goal at home, fans get a free small fry from McDonald's, and three field goals means a large. When the Dukes win, your ticket gets you free nuggets at the Chick-fil-A on East Market Street. Lila has never been happier to watch a kicker warm up.

JC Evans has taken the throws for the Dukes the last two games, and Camden Coleman handled most of the season with 1,814 yards and 17 touchdowns. George Pettaway leads the runners with 824 yards and 8 touchdowns, and Corey Scott is the top receiver at 562 yards. For Coastal, Clayton Coppock Jr. has 565 receiving yards and 7 touchdowns, and Marcellius Pulliam has made 115 tackles, more than anybody on either side.

"Pulliam's going to be in on every play," Goldie says. "You'll be sick of his name by halftime."

Here's how I see Saturday. The band alumni get the stadium rocking before the opening kickoff, and JMU scores on its first two drives behind Pettaway. Bailey answers with a touchdown to Coppock that quiets things for a minute, but then he forces one into coverage and Hooten comes down with it. The Dukes kick a field goal before halftime and the whole student section cheers like it just won a bowl game, because it just won fries. Coastal scores again in the third quarter, Pulliam piles up tackles, and the Dukes pull away late.

Goldie stays for the alumni band's postgame show, and when the last note ends she admits, out loud and in front of witnesses, that the trumpets were on key. Lila gets it on video before Goldie can take it back.

My call: James Madison Dukes 36, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 18.

Bring a can of soup or a new, unwrapped toy to the box office at Center Parc Credit Union Stadium on Saturday and you get into Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns vs Georgia State Panthers for free, because Georgia State's finale is the Giveback Game and Senior Day rolled into one. Malik Overstreet rode MARTA in with two grocery bags full of canned beans, and Mimi Fontenot drove in from Lafayette with a toy fire truck under one arm and a Ragin' Cajuns flag under the other, ready to be generous with everything except the scoreboard.

"Look at this," Malik says, holding up a bag. "Black beans, green beans, baked beans. A whole bean portfolio. That's my ticket."

"I brought a fire truck," Mimi says. "It has a ladder and a siren. You know what your ticket is? Beans."

"Beans feed a family, Mimi."

"Then the family's going to need dessert. I'll bring a pie next year."

That's how it goes with these two, generous and competitive in the same breath. The donations go to people in need around Atlanta, and both of them feel good about that. The game is another story.

Mimi's Ragin' Cajuns are 8-3 and rolling, with three straight wins over South Alabama, UL Monroe and Coastal Carolina. Lunch Winfield threw for 229 yards and three touchdowns against Coastal last week, and JJ Garner has run for 635 yards and eight scores. Jake St. Andre leads the defense with 83 tackles, and Maxie Baudoin IV is the man up front.

"We eat well, we run hard and we dance after," Mimi says. "That's the whole plan. It's worked eight times."

"It didn't work in Ruston," Malik says.

Mimi sets the fire truck down. "Thirty-two to thirty-one. You had to go there."

"Or Hattiesburg."

"You're not getting a slice of that pie, Malik."

Malik's Panthers are 5-6, and a win gets them to six, which means Senior Day could end with a bowl conversation. Last week was a heartbreaker, a 28-27 loss at Marshall, with Ayden Pereira throwing three touchdowns and Qwantavius Wiggins running for 114 yards. Pereira took over the offense in late October, and Rodshaun Dorsey has been his go-to target in the end zone, with 10 touchdown catches on the year.

The Panthers' best player might be on defense. Xavier Esqillion has 10.5 sacks from linebacker, and Malik talks about him the way people in Atlanta talk about traffic, like a force of nature you plan your whole day around.

"Esqillion is coming," Malik says. "He's like the Connector at five o'clock. You can't avoid him, and he'll ruin your afternoon."

"Lunch Winfield runs around people," Mimi says. "He's a quarterback named Lunch. You think he's scared of a linebacker? He's never missed a meal in his life."

The history here is close, too. Georgia State won 20-17 the last time these two met. Louisiana won 21-17 and 34-31 before that. Malik says every game in this series feels like it's decided by whoever brought the most snacks.

Here's how Saturday goes. The seniors are honored before kickoff, and the stadium is full of people who paid their way in with groceries. Georgia State comes out fired up, and Pereira hits Dorsey for a touchdown on the first drive. Louisiana answers with Garner, carry after carry, and Winfield finds a receiver over the middle to tie it. The game swings back and forth, with Esqillion getting to Winfield twice and the home crowd roaring each time. Late in the fourth, Louisiana leads by three, and Georgia State drives into field-goal range. Then St. Andre makes a big stop on third down, the Panthers have to settle for a long try that sails wide, and the Ragin' Cajuns run out the clock.

Malik will drop the last can of beans in the donation bin on the way out, because a good deed doesn't depend on a final score. Mimi will slip her fire truck in right next to it.

My call: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 30, Georgia State Panthers 27.

display.fanatic_story:
Liberty Flames vs Missouri State Bears is Senior Day at Plaster Stadium, and Clementine Bilyeu wants the Flames to know exactly where they are. They're in Springfield, Missouri, in the Ozarks, where folks still talk about a Saturday last November when Missouri State beat Liberty 21-17. She brings it up before anybody can say hello.

"Twenty-one to seventeen," she says. "I just want that in the air when they get off the bus."

Gideon Fairweather drove in from Lynchburg, Virginia, and he did it with a smile, because his team is 10-1. The Flames haven't lost since the opener at James Madison. They've won ten straight, they're 7-0 in Conference USA, and they already have their ticket to the league title game on December 4.

"I'm not here to argue about last year," Gideon says. "I'm here to watch us go 11-1. That's a different team in that room."

"Different team, same field," Clementine says.

This is Missouri State's second season in Conference USA, and it's been a rough one. The Bears are 4-7. They lost 50-0 at Texas A&M in the opener and gave up 61 at Delaware. But they've hung around with almost everybody lately. They beat Kennesaw State 24-21 and Sam Houston 24-3 at home, lost to FIU by three on the road, beat New Mexico State in overtime on Homecoming, and lost by five at Jacksonville State last week.

"We've been close every week for a month," Clementine says. "We're not getting embarrassed. We're getting better. And Saturday is for the seniors."

The school is asking folks to show up early and be in their seats to honor the senior class before kickoff, in their final regular-season home game. Students get in free with their BearPass. Clementine says she'll be there when the gates open, and so will her whole row.

Gideon has heard about Missouri State's receiver, and he's a little worried. Isaiah Myers has 55 catches for 1,065 yards and nine touchdowns, and he's been the best thing about this Bears offense all fall. Henry Belin IV has started at quarterback since the middle of the season, and he looks for Myers first, second and third.

"That kid can play," Gideon admits. "But he hasn't seen our secondary."

Liberty is built on running the ball and stopping everybody else from running it. Jamey Chadwell's team ran for a season-high 370 yards against Middle Tennessee. Kam Davis has 821 yards and nine touchdowns. Deshawn Purdie doesn't throw a ton, but he doesn't give it away either, with 14 touchdowns and one interception, and last week he threw for 344 yards against Western Kentucky. Makai Jackson has 850 receiving yards and eight touchdowns.

And the Flames' defense gives up 14.5 points a game. That's the part Clementine doesn't like talking about.

"Jared Lloyd has 126 tackles," she says. "He's going to add a bunch more on Saturday, because they're going to run it right at him all day, and he's going to be there every time."

Gideon thinks the Flames have bigger things on their mind, and that's what makes Clementine nervous and hopeful at the same time.

"They've got a title game in six days," she says. "If I'm them, I want to get out of here with everybody healthy. And if I'm us, I want to make that really hard."

"We'll be fine," Gideon says. "We were fine against everybody else."

Here's how it plays out. Liberty comes out and runs the ball, and Kam Davis scores early. Missouri State answers with a long throw to Myers that gets the crowd loud. Liberty's defense settles in after that, and the Bears have trouble running it. The Flames take a big lead in the second half and start resting people when it's safe. The seniors still get a late touchdown, and Plaster Stadium sends them off loud.

Clementine stays in her seat until the seniors walk off for the last time. Gideon tips his cap to her row on the way out, and she tells him she'll see him next time.

My call: Liberty Flames 33, Missouri State Bears 18.

display.story_text:
Pitbull Stadium is supposed to be a sea of white this weekend, when FIU honors its seniors and its fans in the final home game of the program's 25th season. My Sam Houston vs FIU pick is Florida International Panthers −11.5 and the Under 41.5, because the Panthers' defense is the best group on the field and the Bearkats have had a hard time finding points all fall.

Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate has the day planned. "Pastelitos for the press box, white shirts in the stands, and one more win for the seniors. That's the whole plan."

Lem Coxwell answers in his orange road hat, slow as a campfire. "Lourdes, we lost to Middle Tennessee by three last week. We're closer than that record says, and that's the truth."

Lem's right about the last game. Sam Houston lost 31-28 to Middle Tennessee, and Mason Holtzclaw went 16 of 25 for 191 yards and three touchdowns in his first game with the most throws this year. But the Bearkats' leading passer, with 1,869 yards and 14 touchdowns, had taken those snaps for nearly the whole season, so the Bearkats are 1-10 and still sorting out who runs the offense.

FIU's defense allows 22.0 points a game. DeeJay Holmes Jr. has 7 sacks, and DeAndre Boykins leads the team with 63 tackles. Sam Houston, meanwhile, has been held to a touchdown or less four times since the start of October. The Bearkats score 17.5 a game and give up 27.7.

FIU's offense isn't a fireworks show. JJ Kohl has 2,579 yards with 14 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. But Devonte Lyons has 760 rushing yards, Maguire Anderson has 803 receiving yards, and FIU won this game 56-16 last year. A team playing at home for its seniors against a 1-10 team should be able to get to 27 without needing anything fancy.

My margin is 13, a point and a half past the number. That's built on FIU's defense holding Sam Houston to two touchdowns while Lyons wears the Bearkats down in the second half.

The Under comes from the same place. I have 41, a half point under. But Sam Houston's scoring has been in the teens or lower most of the year, and FIU has been in four games this season where the teams combined for 28 or fewer. DraftKings opened Florida International Panthers −10.5 with a 39.5 total, and both have climbed since, to −11.5 and 41.5.

The room is mixed. The Formula has FIU 27-18, likes Sam Houston +11.5 and likes the Over 41.5. Next Man Up has 23-11, takes the Panthers and likes the Under. Letdown Watch has 30-14, likes FIU −11.5 and likes the Over. In The Trenches has no score this week, sees the fronts as split, and takes neither side nor total. Next Man Up: "The Formula took a 1-10 team. That's brave, or that's a typo."

The Formula: "A three-point loss last week, Next Man Up. You'd know that if you read anything but the depth chart."

My final is Florida International Panthers 27, Sam Houston Bearkats 14. Lourdes passes out the last pastelitos. Lem tips his hat and starts a story about next year.

display.fanatic_story:
FIU has asked everybody at Pitbull Stadium to wear white on Saturday, and Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate has already ironed two shirts, one for her and one for her abuela, who has been to more Panther games than most of the roster. Sam Houston Bearkats vs FIU Panthers is Senior Day and Fan Appreciation Day at the last home game of FIU's 25th season of football, and Lem Coxwell is flying in from Huntsville in an orange cowboy hat that will stand out in a sea of white like a campfire in the dark.

"Twenty-five years," Lourdes says. "The first FIU team took the field in 2002. My abuela was there. She says she knew we'd make it."

"Your abuela says a lot of things," Lem says.

"She's been right about most of them."

There's a real sense of history around this game in Miami. FIU has played in six bowl games in its 25 seasons, won six Shula Bowls, and sent guys like T.Y. Hilton and Jonnu Smith to the NFL. Last year, in Willie Simmons' first season, the Panthers went to their first bowl since 2019. This year has been harder. FIU is 4-7, and Saturday is the last game for a senior class that helped make last season happen.

"That's why we wear white," Lourdes says. "Clean slate. One more for the seniors, then we start building again."

Lem settles in, the way he always does, with a campfire story. His is about a season that never stopped being close. Sam Houston is 1-10, but the Bearkats lost to Troy by three to open the year, to Tulsa by six, to New Mexico State by six, and to Middle Tennessee by three last Saturday. Their only win was a 59-0 blowout of Nicholls back in September.

"We've been on the doorstep all year," Lem says. "We've knocked. We've rung the bell. We've sat on the porch. Nobody's let us in."

Last week's loss had a new face in it. Mason Holtzclaw took most of the throws against Middle Tennessee and threw three touchdowns, after another quarterback handled the job for most of the season and piled up 1,869 yards and 14 touchdown throws. Chris Reed leads the receivers with 511 yards, and Grady O'Neill caught seven balls last week. On defense, Dean Ford has 63 tackles and Josh Alexander-Felton has 5 sacks.

"Whoever's throwing it, he's got Chris Reed," Lem says. "That boy catches the ball like it owes him money. Bigger than the Huntsville statue."

"In Miami, we'd call him a very nice receiver for a team that's 1-10," Lourdes says, and hands him a pastelito so he can't argue.

The Panthers have their own guys to brag about. JJ Kohl has 2,579 yards and 14 touchdowns, and he threw for 367 against Buffalo back in September. Maguire Anderson is his go-to target with 803 receiving yards. Devonte Lyons has 760 yards on the ground. The defense has carried FIU for long stretches this year: DeeJay Holmes Jr. has 7 sacks, and DeAndre Boykins leads the team in tackles. Last year, FIU beat Sam Houston 56-16.

Lourdes hands out a dominoes nickname for the visitors' offense. "The double-blank," she says. "It's in the box. Nobody wants to play it."

"Now that's just mean," Lem says, grinning.

"It's dominoes. Dominoes is mean."

Here's how Saturday goes. The seniors walk out to a white-shirted crowd, and the FIU defense sets the tone on the first series with a sack from Holmes. Sam Houston moves the ball in spurts and gets a touchdown in the first half to keep Lem upright. Then Lyons starts finding room, Kohl hits Anderson twice on third down, and the Panthers pull away in the third quarter. The Bearkats score once more late, Lem stands up and waves his hat, and the seniors get the sendoff they wanted.

Lourdes heads for the tunnel to find her abuela, who will tell everybody she called it in 2002. Lem pulls his hat low and starts working on next year's campfire story on the walk to the parking lot.

My call: Florida International Panthers 27, Sam Houston Bearkats 14.

display.fanatic_story:
Some second grader in Rutherford County read for 20 minutes a night for 15 nights back in October, turned in a reading log, and earned a free seat at Floyd Stadium for Saturday's game. Opal Stonebriar would like that kid to know it's going to be a good one. New Mexico State Aggies vs Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders is Senior Day, Education Day and Lightning's Reading Club Day in Murfreesboro, and Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya has come all the way from Las Cruces to spoil the party for a team that just made a bowl.

"We're bowl eligible," Opal says. "First time since 2022. Do you know how long four years is in Murfreesboro? It's forever. Forever and a half."

"I know exactly how long a bad season feels," Esperanza says. "I'm living one. That's why I came here to ruin yours."

New Mexico State is 3-8, and the Aggies have dropped four straight. But Esperanza can tell you about every one of those games, because none of them were blowouts. They lost 27-21 in overtime at Missouri State. They lost 30-14 to Liberty and 42-30 to Delaware last Saturday, and in that last game Trey Hedden threw four touchdown passes.

"We're a play away," Esperanza says. "Every week. One play. One stop. I'd like that play on Saturday."

The Aggies have James Jones, and Esperanza says his name like she's reading it off a highway sign. Jones has run for 1,184 yards. He gets stronger as the game goes on, and he doesn't go down on first contact. AJ Williams III is the top receiver at 534 yards. On defense, Gabe Peterson has 6.5 sacks off the end and Tory Gethers leads the team with 83 tackles.

Opal's team has had the better year, and it's been a fun one. Middle Tennessee is 6-5, a year after starting 1-9 and finishing 3-9. Derek Mason brought in a new offensive coordinator and a new coach for the big guys up front, and that group has turned into one that pushes people around. Roman Gagliano has 2,290 yards and 19 touchdowns and has led four game-winning drives. Antonio Martin has 821 rushing yards. Cam'ron Lacy has 70 catches. Korey Smith has 106 tackles at linebacker.

And the Blue Raiders have finally figured out the close ones. They won 31-28 at Sam Houston last week on a game that came down to a fourth-and-10 tackle by Camari Hall. Terrence Brown Jr. broke a 75-yard touchdown run on the first play after Sam Houston tied it. Mason said afterward he felt like a little kid, and that he might grab one of those candy cigarettes for the flight home.

"I want one too," Opal says. "Grape."

Esperanza points out that Gagliano also turned it over three times in that game, and that Middle Tennessee gave up 44 to Kennesaw State and 42 to Western Kentucky this season. Opal points out that the Blue Raiders won the Western Kentucky game 51-42.

"So you score a lot and give up a lot," Esperanza says.

"We're entertaining," Opal says. "There's a difference."

The series has its own story. New Mexico State won 13-7 in 2023 and 36-21 in 2024, and then Middle Tennessee won 31-24 last year. Esperanza calls it a rivalry. Opal calls it a coincidence. Neither one is budging.

Here's how I see it. The Raider Walk through Walnut Grove is louder than usual, the Band of Blue gets the student section going, and Middle Tennessee scores early on a long throw from Gagliano to Lacy. Then the Aggies settle in and do what they do. Jones carries on six of eight snaps on a drive that takes half the first quarter, and New Mexico State ties it. The game goes back and forth all afternoon. Hedden hits Williams for a score. Martin answers. Jones goes over a hundred yards in the third quarter, and the Aggies take the lead in the fourth. Gagliano has one more game-winning drive in him, and the Blue Raiders kick the go-ahead field goal late.

Opal celebrates by finding a kid with a Lightning's Reading Club certificate in the next row and giving him a high five. Esperanza shakes her head, smiles, and goes looking for the gate.

My call: Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 28, New Mexico State Aggies 26.

Beau Cheraw tips his garnet cap. "Two straight wins in your stadium, Dixie-Lynn. We're starting to like the drive up."

That's the story of the week. He's still the most dangerous player on the field, with 661 rushing yards and 17 touchdown throws, and Clemson had no answer for him two years ago. display.fanatic_story:
Saturday in Clemson is IPTAY Day, the afternoon the program sets aside to thank the donors who have been writing checks for Tiger athletes since IPTAY was founded in 1934, and South Carolina Gamecocks vs Clemson Tigers in the Palmetto Bowl is the game they get as a thank-you card. Dixie-Lynn Pruitt has been an IPTAY member longer than she's been married, she says, and Beau Cheraw drove up from Columbia in a garnet sweater with a grin that says the Gamecocks have won the last two trips to Memorial Stadium.

"Two in a row," Beau says, holding up two fingers. "Thirty-one to thirty. Seventeen to fourteen. Your house, Dixie-Lynn. I'm starting to think of it as my house."

"Your house is in Columbia, Beau, and it has a leaky roof."

"How would you know about my roof?"

"Everybody in this state knows about your roof."

That's the kind of thing two neighbors can say to each other when they've been feuding since before either one could drive. The Palmetto Bowl is the one game that splits families in this state, and Dixie-Lynn's own brother-in-law went to school in Columbia, which she describes as "a cross we bear together at Thanksgiving."

This year Dixie-Lynn has more to worry about than family dinner. Clemson is down to its third quarterback. Tait Reynolds tore up his knee against Georgia Tech, and Christopher Vizzina took a hard concussion in the same game and is out. So Trent Pearman, the third-string quarterback, got the keys, and all he did last Friday was go to Duke and win 20-10. He completed 17 of 27 throws for 164 yards and didn't throw an interception.

"Third string," Dixie-Lynn says, beaming. "Do you know what that means, Beau? It means he spent years getting beat up in practice with nobody watching, and then he went to Durham and beat a team everybody said was better. That's the most Clemson thing that has ever happened."

"It's a nice story," Beau says. "LaNorris Sellers is a nicer one."

Beau's not wrong. Sellers has 661 rushing yards and seven scores to go with 17 touchdown throws, and two years ago he ran all over Death Valley for 166 yards and two touchdowns in a win the Gamecocks still talk about at breakfast. Mazeo Bennett Jr. leads the receivers. Fred Johnson has 91 tackles at linebacker, and Tomiwa Durojaiye has four sacks.

"Sellers is my guy," Beau says. "He's built like a linebacker and runs like he stole something."

What Beau doesn't want to talk about is the last two weeks. South Carolina lost 34-6 at Arkansas and 34-6 at home to Georgia. Six points, then six points.

"We're saving them," Beau says. "For today."

"That's a lot of saving."

Dixie-Lynn's best argument is the Clemson defense. The Tigers give up 19.6 points a game. Will Heldt has seven sacks off the end, Corey Myrick leads the team with 82 tackles from safety, and Gideon Davidson and Jarvis Green give the offense enough of a ground game to keep a defense honest.

Bryant Wesco Jr. has 548 receiving yards and is Pearman's safety blanket. The Tigers are 7-4. Clemson has also won at Florida State and at Syracuse this year, and the road has been friendlier to this program lately than its own stadium.

"We play better when people expect us to lose," Dixie-Lynn admits. "Nobody's expecting anything from a third-string quarterback. Perfect."

Here's how Saturday goes. The IPTAY donors get their applause before kickoff, and the orange crowd is loud enough to rattle the hill. South Carolina strikes first when Sellers breaks loose for a long run that silences most of the stadium and sends Beau dancing in the aisle. Clemson answers with Davidson, and Pearman hits Wesco on a third down to keep a drive alive. The teams trade field goals and touchdowns all afternoon, and the game is tied in the fourth quarter. Sellers makes one more big play, scrambling for a first down that sets up the go-ahead field goal, and Heldt's late sack gives Clemson one last chance that comes up just short.

Beau will hum the Gamecock fight song all the way to the car. Dixie-Lynn will renew her IPTAY membership on her phone in the parking lot, out of spite and out of love.

My call: South Carolina Gamecocks 24, Clemson Tigers 22.

display.story_text:
Virginia vs Virginia Tech comes down to one ugly fact for Charlottesville. Virginia hasn't won a game in Lane Stadium since nineteen ninety-eight. The Cavaliers took the Commonwealth Cup last year at home, 27-7, and now they have to go get it in Blacksburg in James Franklin's first rivalry game with the Hokies. My Virginia vs Virginia Tech pick is Virginia Cavaliers +3 with the Under 51.5.

Ruthanne Dellinger doesn't mind the history one bit. "Since ninety-eight. Say it slow, Prescott. I want to hear it from you."

Prescott Ashby-Lowell is ready. "We've won two in a row. You've lost three in a row. Pick a year you'd rather talk about."

He's got the momentum part right. Virginia beat Cal 36-7 and North Carolina 41-24, and Beau Pribula threw for 297 yards and four touchdowns last week. He has 19 touchdown throws and three interceptions on the year. Virginia Tech lost 28-51 at SMU, 22-40 to Stanford at home and 20-28 at Miami, and has lost five of its last seven. Both teams are 6-5 and already bowl eligible.

The side is about a field goal and a coin flip. A home team that's been sliding gets three points from a road team that's been rolling. Virginia allows 21.7 points a game, Virginia Tech allows 25.7, and Virginia's losses to Duke and SMU were by three and ten.

The Under comes from both run games stalling. Virginia runs for 4.0 a carry against a Virginia Tech defense that allows 3.7. Virginia Tech runs for 3.6 against a Virginia defense that allows 4.3, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. had 38 yards on 14 carries at Miami. That puts it on Ethan Grunkemeyer, who has 21 touchdowns and five picks, and on Pribula and Jekail Middlebrook, who caught five balls for 140 against North Carolina.

DraftKings opened Virginia Tech Hokies −1.5 with a 53.5 total. The side has moved a point and a half toward the Hokies, and the total has dropped two points.

The room likes the Cavaliers and the Over. The Formula and Next Man Up both have Virginia 27-26 and take Virginia Cavaliers +3 with the Over 51.5. Letdown Watch has Virginia 28-24 and the Over. In The Trenches goes the other way, with 27-22 and Virginia Tech Hokies −3, with no over/under call. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Virginia Cavaliers vs Virginia Tech Hokies is the game Ruthanne Dellinger circles before the schedule even comes out, and this year she circled it twice. The last time Virginia won a football game at Lane Stadium was 1998. She was in grade school. She's now got kids of her own who've never seen it happen, and she would like to keep it that way.

"Twenty-eight years," Ruthanne says. "My son thinks it's a law. I haven't corrected him."

Prescott Ashby-Lowell drove in from Charlottesville with a thermos and the Commonwealth Cup on his mind. Virginia took it home last year, 27-7, and he says it looks good in Charlottesville. He's not ready to give it back.

"We had it last year," Prescott says. "We're keeping it. History is a nice thing to have when you don't have anything else."

That one stings, because this Hokies season has been hard. James Franklin came in with a lot of fanfare, and it started great. Virginia Tech beat VMI 73-3, won at Maryland and Boston College, and went into Clemson and won 20-16 to become bowl eligible in October. Then the wheels wobbled. The Hokies lost 51-28 at SMU, 40-22 at home to Stanford, and 28-20 at Miami last week. They've lost three straight.

"It's not about the record now," Ruthanne says. "It's about this one. You win this one, everybody forgets November."

Virginia's coming in the other way. The Cavaliers had a rough middle of the year, including a 51-7 loss at Wake Forest, but they've won two straight. They beat Cal 36-7 and then ran past North Carolina 41-24 last week to get to six wins. Beau Pribula threw for 297 yards and four touchdowns, and he's got 19 touchdowns and just three interceptions this season.

"Beau doesn't throw it to the other team," Prescott says. "Hasn't all year. Write that down."

"I'll write it on your car," Ruthanne says.

The guy Prescott can't stop talking about is Jekail Middlebrook. The running back caught five balls for 140 yards and a touchdown against North Carolina, and Prescott says that's what happens when you finally throw it to him.

Ruthanne has her own guys. Ethan Grunkemeyer has thrown for 2,869 yards and 21 touchdowns. Que'Sean Brown has 73 catches for 887 yards. Jeffrey Overton Jr. has 907 rushing yards, even if Miami held him to 38 last week. And Aycen Stevens has 8.5 sacks up front.

"Aycen's going to be in Pribula's ear all day," she says. "He'll hear him in his sleep."

Here's the thing about this game: neither team runs the ball well against the other. Virginia Tech's defense is tough to run on, and Virginia hasn't been great running it all year. Tech's ground game has been stuck for weeks. So this comes down to the quarterbacks, and two teams that are trying to get the bad taste out.

"Thanksgiving weekend in Blacksburg," Ruthanne says. "Cold and loud. I want them to feel every bit of it."

"We'll feel it," Prescott says. "We'll feel it on the bus home, with the Cup."

Here's how it goes. It's tight and physical early, with a lot of punts and long third downs. Pribula hits Middlebrook out of the backfield for a long touchdown, and Grunkemeyer finds Brown to answer. Neither team leads by more than a touchdown all day. Virginia gets the ball back late with a chance, but Stevens gets home on a big third down, and Tech holds on by one. Lane Stadium shakes for the first time in a month.

Ruthanne looks for Prescott in the parking lot afterward and finds him sitting on his tailgate with the thermos. She tells him the drought is safe for another year. He tells her the next one is in Charlottesville, and he'll be waiting.

My call: Virginia Tech Hokies 26, Virginia Cavaliers 25.

display.fanatic_story:
Somebody else will coach Arkansas State next fall, and the Red Wolves found that out a week before their last game. The school announced last Tuesday that Butch Jones won't be back in 2027, the change took effect right away, and Jalen Ortiz, the associate head coach who runs the cornerbacks, has the whole program for one Saturday against Troy. Troy Trojans vs Arkansas State Red Wolves is the season finale for both teams, and Ty Doucet-Harmon has been sitting in the duck blind behind his desk since Tuesday afternoon.

"Six years," Ty says, and gives one long, low duck call. "Three bowl trips in a row. Two bowl wins. Thirty wins. That's a man who did right by this town, and now we send him out with Fan Appreciation Day."

Marlo Pickens doesn't wait long. "Ty, I'm sorry about your coach. I mean that. But Troy didn't drive up here to be a going-away party. We came to crack some shells."

Here's the thing for Red Wolves fans. Jones won the 68 Ventures Bowl in 2024 and the Xbox Bowl last year, and this season fell apart anyway. Arkansas State is 4-7 and 2-5 in the Sun Belt. It's lost three in a row. The 19-17 loss at home to UL Monroe still hurts, the 28-21 loss at Coastal Carolina hurt, and then last week in Ruston was a 48-3 beating at Louisiana Tech that nobody in Jonesboro wants to talk about.

"We don't talk about Ruston," Ty says.

"I'll talk about Ruston," Marlo says.

"Then I'll talk about Statesboro."

Fair enough. Troy got crushed too, 45-7 at home by Georgia Southern, so neither one of these fan bases gets to walk in with its chest out. Troy is also 4-7 and 2-5 in conference. It's dropped three straight too, 41-17 to Louisiana Tech, 27-14 at South Alabama and then the Georgia Southern game.

"See, we're even," Marlo says. "Same record, same mood, same long week. It's a peanut pile, and you got to dig to the bottom."

Ty's case is the quarterback. Trey Owens has thrown for 2,559 yards and 12 touchdowns this year, and on a good night he's a problem. He threw for 418 yards and four touchdowns against South Alabama in a 56-49 shootout and threw for 325 at Memphis in the opener. Jaylen Bonelli has 43 catches for 612 yards, and Joe Drew has 103 tackles from his safety spot, which tells you how often the ball has gotten past the front seven.

"Owens throws it thirty times, and Bonelli catches it everywhere," Ty says. "That's mallards coming in over the decoys. You just wait and let them land."

Marlo's case is the stuff that doesn't show up on a highlight. Troy won 24-21 over Sam Houston in September and won 24-21 in overtime at James Madison in late October, and the Trojans have a habit of making a game messy and staying in it. Goose Crowder has 1,527 yards and 11 touchdown throws, and he was nearly perfect against Southern Miss, 18 of 21 for 225 yards in a 55-34 win. Donnie Smith has 9 sacks, and Keno Jones has 85 tackles in the middle.

"Donnie Smith is the peanut butter," Marlo says. "He's in everything. You can't get him off the knife."

The series history doesn't settle the argument either. Since 2016 these two have played eight times and split them four apiece. Troy won 48-19 in 2022 and 37-3 in 2023. Arkansas State answered with a 34-31 win in 2024 and a 23-10 win last year.

Saturday is also Senior Day in Jonesboro, so the Red Wolves seniors get their walk before the 2 p.m. local kickoff at Centennial Bank Stadium. The school is calling it Fan Appreciation Day, with concession specials for the crowd and a holiday food drive for the A-State Food Bank, and Ty is bringing two bags of canned goods.

There's also a real football reason to think the home team shows up. Players playing for an interim coach in the final game usually play hard for him, and Ortiz knows the secondary better than anybody on that staff. If he can get the Red Wolves defense to tackle in space for four quarters, Owens has enough to win a close one. Arkansas State is 3-2 at home and 1-5 on the road, and this is the right building for a last stand.

Troy will run Gavin Griffin, who has 512 yards on the ground, and try to keep Owens on the sideline. If Crowder takes care of the ball, Troy hangs around all afternoon. If he throws one up for grabs late, Joe Drew will be there.

Here's how I see it. Owens gets his yards. Crowder makes it close. The seniors get one last win in front of the home folks, the food bank gets its cans, and Ty blows that duck call so hard the press box hears it.

Marlo cracks a peanut, shakes his head and says, "Close enough to taste."

My call: Arkansas State Red Wolves 26, Troy Trojans 23.

Saturday is Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate again, Georgia is No. 1 and already headed to the SEC Championship Game, and my Georgia Tech vs Georgia prediction is Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets +35.5 with the Under 55.5.

Thad Okafor-Brandt has the numbers ready. "Eight straight in this series, Wendell. Nine would be the longest run either school has ever had. We're 10-1 and we gave up six points in Columbia last week."

Georgia Tech is 3-8 and has lost five of six, but this game means everything to Brent Key. "We have the biggest game of the year coming up," he said after the 50-29 loss to Wake Forest. The quarterback spot is unsettled. Alberto Mendoza took the throws most of the year, and Grady Adamson took over against Wake and ran for 143 yards. I'm pricing Adamson, and a running quarterback who keeps the ball on the ground also keeps the clock moving.

That's the Under case, too. Georgia's defense keeps games short, and a Tech offense that runs the quarterback eats time. The total opened at 55.5 at DraftKings, and the spread opened at 35.5. Neither has moved.

Wendell Quist still has the ticket stub from the eight-overtime game, and he says he keeps it in a drawer next to his birth certificate, because both of them prove he was there. Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets vs Georgia Bulldogs is back in Sanford Stadium for the 120th Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate, and Thad Okafor-Brandt says that 44-42 night in 2024 was the most fun he's ever had being terrified.

"Eight overtimes," Thad says. "I aged a year. I had to sit down in the fifth. I've never sat down at a Georgia game."

"And you still won," Wendell says. "That's the worst part. You always still win."

That part is true lately. Georgia has won eight straight in this series. One more makes it nine, and that would be the longest run either school has had against the other in a rivalry that's 120 games old. Wendell has heard about the streak so many times he can tell you the score of every one of them without being asked, which nobody has ever asked him to do.

But Wendell also has one thing he likes to point out. The last three games were all one-score games. The eight-overtime game in Athens. A 31-23 Georgia win in 2023. And last year's 16-9 game in Atlanta, where neither offense could find the end zone.

"Close," Wendell says. "Every year it's close. You're No. 1 and it's still close."

Thad would like to talk about this year's team, which might be the best one he's seen. Georgia is 10-1, ranked No. 1, and already headed to the SEC Championship Game on Dec. 5. The only loss was 27-24 to Auburn in October. Since then, the Bulldogs have beaten Florida, Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina by double digits every time. Gunner Stockton has 22 touchdown throws and only 4 interceptions. He went 19 of 23 for 281 yards at South Carolina last week. Talyn Taylor is the top receiver. Nate Frazier ran for two scores in Columbia. And the defense, led by Chris Cole with 71 tackles and 5.5 sacks, has given up 13.9 points a game.

"This team doesn't make mistakes," Thad says. "It just shows up, does its job and goes home. I love them. I'd like them to show some emotion once in a while, but I love them."

Wendell's team has shown plenty of emotion. Some of it the wrong kind. Georgia Tech is 3-8 and has lost five of its last six, including a 50-29 loss to Wake Forest last Saturday at Bobby Dodd. But that one win in the middle of it was a 20-6 stunner at Clemson, and Wendell has decided that's the version of the team that's coming to Athens.

"Brent Key said it's the biggest game of the year," Wendell says. "He's right. It's the only game that matters now."

The quarterback picture is the question. Alberto Mendoza threw it most of the year, with 2,123 yards and 11 touchdowns. Grady Adamson took over against Wake and ran 16 times for 143 yards and a score. Justice Haynes has 806 rushing yards, Jordan Allen has 664 receiving yards, and Tae Harris leads the defense with 68 tackles from safety.

"Run Adamson," Wendell says. "Run Haynes. Run the clock. Make them get bored."

"Georgia doesn't get bored," Thad says. "Georgia gets efficient."

Here's how I see it. Sanford Stadium is rocking for the rivalry, and Georgia scores on its first three drives. Stockton finds Taylor for one, Frazier runs for two, and the hedges are humming by the end of the first quarter. Tech gets a field goal and a long Adamson run to keep the visiting section on its feet. The Bulldogs pile on before halftime, and the starters take a seat early in the fourth. Wendell walks out of Sanford Stadium with his ticket stub in his pocket, the new one, and says he's putting it in the drawer too. Thad asks why. Wendell says it's proof he was there for the night Georgia Tech scored a touchdown on the No. 1 team in the country.

My call: Georgia Bulldogs 44, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 11.

Cole Tabb has 1,097 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns, and he added 7 catches for 110 yards and two scores in that win. The road has been tough, with losses at Arizona, West Virginia, Houston and Iowa State, but the West Virginia and Houston games were decided by a score.

display.fanatic_story:
Provo is bracing for the coldest home game of the year on Saturday, when Cincinnati Bearcats vs BYU Cougars closes the LaVell Edwards Stadium schedule on Thanksgiving weekend with a 1:30 kickoff that should end right around sunset. Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi packed two blankets, a jug of cocoa and a speech for every senior, and Lionel "Skyline" Abernathy flew in from Cincinnati wearing a windbreaker, which Bryce considers a cry for help.

"A windbreaker," Bryce says, handing him a blanket without being asked. "You came to Utah in November in a windbreaker."

"It's a thick windbreaker," Skyline says. "Cincinnati winters build character. I have a lot of character."

"Your character is going to be shivering by the third quarter."

"Then I'll shiver happy. We're a bowl team now, Bryce."

That's Skyline's big news, and he's going to say it a few more times before kickoff. Cincinnati beat Colorado 35-28 last week to get to 6-5, and JC French IV was nearly perfect, completing 18 of 19 throws for 208 yards and two touchdowns. Cole Tabb ran for 120 yards and two scores and caught seven balls for 110 more, which Skyline describes as "a one-man buffet." Tabb has 1,097 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns on the year.

"Eighteen of nineteen," Skyline says. "You know what the one miss was? A throwaway. On purpose. He felt bad for the defense."

Bryce has more to brag about, and he knows it. BYU is 9-2, ranked in the top ten, and this is the Cougars' ninth game on one of the big national networks this season. They beat Notre Dame 28-24 in October in this very stadium, and Bryce has the final score saved as the wallpaper on his phone.

"Notre Dame," Bryce says, slowly. "In Provo. I still get goosebumps."

"That might be the weather."

"It's not the weather."

Bear Bachmeier leads the offense with 2,299 throwing yards and 14 touchdowns, and LJ Martin ran for 127 yards at Kansas last week in a 31-29 overtime win. Legend Glasker is the top receiver with 735 yards. On defense, Cade Uluave has 71 tackles and Bodie Schoonover leads the team with four sacks. BYU gives up 19.5 points a game, and in Provo the Cougars have been tough to score on, with Baylor managing just seven two weeks ago.

"Our defense is like this campus," Bryce says. "Clean, polite and very hard to get into after dark."

Skyline admits the road has been rough. The Bearcats lost at Arizona, at West Virginia, at Houston and at Iowa State, and their defense gives up 30.4 points a game. But two of those road losses were one-score games, and the West Virginia one was a 45-42 shootout he still has nightmares about.

"We lose close," Skyline says. "We never lose boring."

The two teams met in this stadium in 2023, and BYU won 35-27. Last year BYU won 26-14. Skyline is counting on Jonathan Thompson, the Bearcats' leading tackler with 83, to make this one look more like the first game than the second.

Here's how Saturday goes. The seniors get their moment before kickoff, the crowd is bundled up and loud, and BYU takes the opening drive right down the field, with Martin pounding it in. Cincinnati answers with French finding Tabb out of the backfield, and the Bearcats are hanging around at halftime. Then the sun starts to drop behind the mountains, and so does Cincinnati's luck. Bachmeier hits Glasker for a long touchdown, Uluave stuffs a fourth-down run, and BYU pulls away in the third quarter. The Bearcats keep swinging, Tabb scores late, and the final margin stays respectable.

Bryce will walk Skyline to the shuttle with the blanket still wrapped around his shoulders. Skyline will try to give it back, and Bryce will tell him to keep it for the bowl game.

My call: BYU Cougars 34, Cincinnati Bearcats 20.
