display.story_text:
Duke vs Wake Forest is a big rivalry game for one team and a dress rehearsal for the other. Wake Forest is 10-1, has won eight straight, and already has its spot in the ACC title game against Miami next Saturday in Charlotte. Duke is 7-4 and has lost two in a row. My Duke vs Wake Forest pick is Duke Blue Devils +14.5 with the Under 56.5.

Eloise Brightman-Rowe has waited long enough. "Four years, Harrison. Four years since we beat you. It's Senior Day, we're the best team in the state, and I want it by forty."

Harrison Wexley-Moore IV doesn't flinch. "You've got Miami on the brain, Eloise. We're the only thing on ours."

That's the side. Wake Forest has a rematch with the only team that beat it, a week away. Duke has won the last four meetings and would love nothing more than to wreck Senior Day. Duke also has the best defense Wake will see before Charlotte, allowing 15.7 points a game, even if it gave up 36 at Miami and 20 to Clemson in the last two.

Duke can run, too. Nate Sheppard has 1,436 yards and 20 touchdowns, and he went for 116 against Clemson. The problem is that this matchup cancels itself out. Duke runs for 5.3 a carry against a Wake defense that allows 3.2. Wake runs for 5.2 against a Duke defense that allows 3.3. That's two good running teams hitting two tough fronts.

That's the Under. Eight of Duke's eleven games stayed under this total, and the Blue Devils won't want to trade scores. Walker Eget has 11 touchdowns and five picks and went 16 of 38 against Clemson, so Duke will try to shorten this game. Wake can score with anybody, and Gio Lopez has 21 touchdowns and one interception, with Carlos Hernandez at 1,184 receiving yards. But Wake also allows just 16.3 a game.

DraftKings opened Wake Forest Demon Deacons −10.5 with a 52.5 total. The side has jumped four points and the total four points since, which gives Duke plenty of room.

The room is lined up on this one. The Formula has 31-22 and takes Duke Blue Devils +14.5 with the Under 56.5. Next Man Up has 33-19, also with Duke and the Under. Letdown Watch has 32-20 with Duke and the Under. In The Trenches has no pick in this game. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "Letdown Watch, you finally found a team with a letdown. Do you want a trophy or just a nap?"

Letdown Watch: "I'll take the nap after Wake pulls its starters in the fourth. You'll still be up counting yards for a guy who's on the bench."

My final is Wake Forest Demon Deacons 32, Duke Blue Devils 20. Wake wins by twelve, inside the fourteen and a half, and 52 combined stays under the total. Lopez gets his numbers, Wake gets its win and its health, and Duke makes it a fight up front.

display.fanatic_story:
Duke Blue Devils vs Wake Forest Demon Deacons is the 106th time these two have met, and Eloise Brightman-Rowe has a problem with the last four. Duke won all of them. The last time Wake beat the Blue Devils was a 45-7 win in 2021, and she's done waiting. It's Senior Day in Winston-Salem, and she wants this class to walk off the field with that one checked off.

"Ten wins, a spot in Charlotte, and I'm still mad about Duke," Eloise says. "That's how you know it's a rivalry."

Harrison Wexley-Moore IV drove over from Durham and parked as close to the stadium as he could, which wasn't close. He's wearing a Duke scarf his grandfather wore to this game, and he wants everybody to notice.

"Four straight," Harrison says. "I don't even need to say anything else. I'll just stand here."

He's going to have to stand there a while, because Wake Forest is having a season. The Deacons are 10-1. They've won eight straight. They beat Louisville on the road, crushed SMU 49-7, and went into Atlanta last week and put up 50 on Georgia Tech. That win clinched a spot in the ACC title game against Miami in Jake Dickert's second year.

"I've been to Charlotte for a lot of things," Eloise says. "Never for this. I'm going to bring a sign. Maybe two."

Gio Lopez has been the whole show. He has 2,701 yards, 21 touchdowns and one interception. One. All season. Carlos Hernandez has 75 catches for 1,184 yards, and he had 145 in Atlanta last week.

"Gio doesn't throw it to the other team," Eloise says. "He throws it to Carlos. Sometimes he throws it to Carlos and three other guys at once. It's art."

Harrison has a runner he loves even more than his scarf. Nate Sheppard has 1,436 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns. He's carried Duke all year, and he went for 116 yards against Clemson last week even in a loss.

"Nate's the best running back in the ACC," Harrison says. "Ask Clemson. Ask anybody who tried to tackle him."

The problem for Duke is that the last two weeks haven't gone their way. The Blue Devils lost 36-25 at Miami and 20-10 to Clemson. Walker Eget threw it 38 times against Clemson and completed 16. Harrison doesn't want to talk about that part.

"The ball was cold," he says.

"The ball was fine," Eloise says.

And here's what has Eloise a little nervous: Duke's defense is the real deal. The Blue Devils give up 15.7 points a game. And Wake has to play Miami a week after this, the only team that beat them all season. She doesn't want her guys looking ahead.

"If anybody on that sideline is thinking about Charlotte before the fourth quarter, I'll be thinking about them," she says.

But she also thinks the Deacons are too good to let this one go. Wake's defense gives up 16.3 points a game, and Duke's run game is going to hit a wall. The Deacons have been tough to run on all fall, and Eloise expects Sheppard to have to work for every inch.

Here's how Saturday goes. The seniors get a big roar before kickoff, and the Deacons come out sharp. Lopez finds Hernandez deep on the opening drive, and Wake scores. Duke hangs around in the first half behind Sheppard, who gets loose for a touchdown in the second quarter. But Wake pulls away in the third, and Lopez throws two more scores. Duke gets a late one to make it look closer, and the Deacons finally break the Blue Devils' run in the series.

Afterward, Eloise finds Harrison by his car, still wearing the scarf. She tells him it looks better on a loser. He says he'll wear it next year too, and she'd better get used to it.

My call: Wake Forest Demon Deacons 32, Duke Blue Devils 20.

display.fanatic_story:
Stanford is giving away a football ticket for every ticket it sells this weekend. That's the deal for FansGiving, the Cardinal's fan appreciation game against SMU: buy a seat, and the school donates another one to an underserved community group, so somebody who's never been on The Farm gets to see a college football game on the last home Saturday of the year. There's also a food drive for Second Harvest of Silicon Valley, photos with Santa Claus at Fan Fest, and the seniors get one more walk out of the tunnel at Stanford Stadium.

Iggy Yamamoto-Ross has turned the whole thing into a pitch deck.

"It's a two-sided marketplace," he says. "Fans buy a ticket, the community gets a ticket. Growth on both ends. Honestly, I should've built this app years ago."

Tatum Delacroix-Price, who flew in from Dallas in a red coat she says is "aggressively Mustang," is not interested in the pitch deck.

"Iggy, it's a nice thing your school's doing. I respect it. But my team is coming out there to fix a bad two weeks, and I don't care how many Santas are at Fan Fest."

The bad two weeks are real. SMU was 7-2 and sitting pretty in the ACC in early November, then Wake Forest came to Dallas and won 49-7. Last week the Mustangs went to South Bend and lost 24-3 to Notre Dame. Kevin Jennings threw it 45 times in that one and never found the end zone.

"I graded the Wake Forest game an F," Tatum says. "Not the outfits. The football. The outfits were fine."

Iggy doesn't let it go. "So SMU's in a down round."

"SMU is 7-4 and has the best quarterback on that field. Write that in your deck."

She's got numbers to back her up. Jennings has thrown for 3,189 yards and 26 touchdowns with only 8 interceptions this year. He threw for 430 yards at Florida State in the opener and 439 against Missouri State. Kendrick Raphael has 909 yards on the ground and ran for 100 at Notre Dame even in a loss, and Yamir Knight caught nine balls for 115 yards in that same game. Marques White has 8.5 sacks. This is a team that beat Virginia Tech 51-28 and Cal 59-20 a month ago.

"We just need one good week," Tatum says. "One. Then I'll sit on The Farm and eat a three-dollar ice cream like a lady."

Iggy's case is that his team is finally shipping. Stanford is 6-5, already bowl-eligible, and has won two in a row on the road, 40-22 at Virginia Tech and 44-28 at Cal last week. Micah Ford has 1,051 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns, and he ran for 151 yards and two scores in Berkeley. Davis Warren has 2,620 yards and has thrown just 3 interceptions all season, which is the kind of number Iggy puts on slide one.

"We pivoted to the run game," Iggy says. "Product-market fit. Micah Ford is the killer feature."

"Micah Ford is a very good running back," Tatum says. "Your defense is a beta."

That hurts because it's true. Stanford gives up 35.1 points a game. Miami put 45 on the Cardinal at home. Wake Forest scored 57 in Winston-Salem. Notre Dame scored 58 and Louisville scored 52. When Stanford has played the best teams on its schedule, the defense hasn't held up, and SMU, on a normal day, is one of those teams.

The two programs haven't played much. SMU won 40-10 in 2024 and 34-10 last year, both after the Mustangs joined the ACC. Iggy calls those early versions of the product. Tatum calls them receipts.

"Two meetings, two wins," she says. "Both blowouts. And you want to talk to me about scaling?"

Stanford does have a few things working for it Saturday. It's home. It's the seniors' last game in that building. It's an early kickoff in California for a team that flew in from Dallas, and the Cardinal has a back who can keep SMU's offense standing on the sideline. If Ford gets 25 carries and the Stanford defense holds Jennings to field goals, this game gets tight.

Here's what I see, though. SMU is tired of hearing about the last two weeks. Jennings gets loose against a secondary that's been leaking all year. Ford runs hard and gets his, and Stanford's seniors make it a game for a while. But Raphael grinds out the second half, White gets home a couple of times, and the Mustangs pull away late.

Tatum will give the team an A-minus. She'll give Iggy's red sneakers a C. Iggy will thank everybody for coming and call it a learning round.

My call: SMU Mustangs 32, Stanford Cardinal 24.

Penn State lost to Rutgers on the final play last week, and the Nittany Lions now close the regular season at SECU Stadium against a Maryland team playing its home finale on Senior Day. My Penn State vs Maryland prediction is Penn State Nittany Lions −7 with the Over 50.5.

Luann Kessler is still mad about Saturday. "Rutgers. On the last play. With a two-point try. I'm not over it and I'm not getting over it until we score on the first drive in College Park."

Abby Chesapeake is all business. "We've won two of our last four under the interim. Everyone keeps telling me we're 4-7. I keep telling them we're playing at home."

Penn State is 6-5, and the loss to Rutgers had little to do with the offense. Rocco Becht went 14 of 21 for 233 yards, Chase Sowell caught 6 for 123, and Cam Wallace ran for 95. The Nittany Lions scored 29.6 points a game and allowed 19.4 this season. Tony Rojas leads the defense with 86 tackles and 6.5 sacks.

Maryland is 4-7 and has allowed 30.7 points a game. The Terps have the better story lately. Interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim won at Purdue 34-29 and beat Wisconsin 24-21, before a 35-21 loss at USC. Malik Washington is back at quarterback with 2,309 yards, but he has thrown 10 interceptions, two of them at USC. Chris Durr Jr. has 74 catches for 848 yards.

The series has been lopsided. Penn State won 44-7 the last time these teams met, in 2024, and 51-15 the year before. The only Maryland win in the run was 35-19 in 2020.

I'm pricing Washington at quarterback for the Terps and Becht for the Nittany Lions. Penn State's front gets to Washington, he throws a couple he wants back, and the Nittany Lions turn those into points.

display.fanatic_story:
Abby Chesapeake has a clipboard, a seating chart for her section and a list of names with check marks next to them, because she works the halls in Annapolis for a living and she runs Senior Day like a floor vote. "I need everyone loud on the opening kickoff," she says. "I've got commitments from three rows. The fourth row is undecided."

Penn State Nittany Lions vs Maryland Terrapins is the 49th meeting between the two schools, and it's Maryland's home finale at SECU Stadium. The Terps will honor their seniors before the game. Abby will be counting heads during it.

Luann Kessler played volleyball at Penn State, and she still sets everything up for somebody else. "Here's your opening," she tells Abby. "You're 4-7. Go ahead."

"Two wins in our last four," Abby says. "Under an interim coach who took over in October. I'll take that to any committee in the state."

Abby's Terps have had a strange season. Maryland opened with wins over Hampton and UConn, then lost five straight, including a 54-3 loss to UCLA that Abby refuses to discuss. The school made a coaching change, and Aazaar Abdul-Rahim took over as the interim. Then came a 34-29 win at Purdue and a 24-21 win over Wisconsin. With Malik Washington hurt for that one, Cardell Williams made his first start for the Terps and completed 19 throws in a row, a program record.

"Nineteen in a row," Abby says. "Ask me about it. I'll tell you every one."

Washington came back at USC and threw for 251 yards in a 35-21 loss. He has 2,309 yards this season. Chris Durr Jr. has 74 catches for 848 yards, DeJuan Williams has 592 yards on the ground, and Zion Elee leads the defense with 6 sacks.

Luann has a sore spot of her own. Penn State had won three straight, and then last Saturday happened. Senior Day at Beaver Stadium. A 24-10 lead in the third quarter. Rutgers drove down the field, scored on the last play and went for two. They got it, and won 25-24.

"I've watched that two-point try maybe forty times," Luann says. "It doesn't get better. I keep hoping somebody falls down."

What Luann does like is that the offense showed up. Rocco Becht went 14 of 21 for 233 yards and ran for a score. Chase Sowell caught 6 for 123. Cam Wallace broke a 56-yard touchdown run on the third play of the game. Tony Rojas made 15 tackles. Becht has 19 touchdown throws and only 5 interceptions this season, and Sowell has 758 receiving yards.

"We're 6-5," Luann says. "That's a bowl team. And a bowl team doesn't lose twice in a row to teams it beats every year."

Penn State has won almost every one of these lately. The Nittany Lions won 44-7 in 2024, the last time these two played, and 51-15 the year before. The one Maryland win in that run came in 2020, 35-19. These two had played every season for 11 years before skipping last year.

Here's how I see it. Abby's section is loud on the opening kickoff, all four rows of it. Maryland moves the ball early, and Durr makes a couple of big catches. But Penn State gets to Washington, and an interception sets up a Becht touchdown throw to Sowell. Wallace breaks another long run before halftime. Maryland keeps it close into the third quarter with a DeJuan Williams touchdown, and then Penn State pulls away late.

Abby checks off every name on her list on the way out and says the vote was close, but not close enough. Luann tells her Penn State had the votes the whole time. Abby says she'll be calling her back next year.

My call: Penn State Nittany Lions 32, Maryland Terrapins 21.

A 10-1 UCLA team is getting points at home against an 8-3 USC team, with the Victory Bell and a trip to Indianapolis on the table. This USC vs UCLA prediction backs UCLA Bruins +6.5 as the home underdog, and with the total down nine points since the open, my over/under call is Over 46.5.

Kensington "Kenzie" Rhee is at the Rose Bowl early. "Win and we're in the Big Ten title game. Simple."

Sterling Ashworth-Vance doesn't look up from his phone. "Win with who, Kenzie? Your quarterback got carted off in Ann Arbor."

That's the story of the week. Ty Dieffenbach was carted off after a big hit in the first overtime of the 18-16 loss at Michigan, and third-stringer Madden Iamaleava finished the game. Who starts Saturday is the question of the week, and I won't guess.

Here's what I know. UCLA is 6-0 at the Rose Bowl, and only Purdue scored more than 14 there. The Bruins allow 14.5 points a game. Wayne Knight has 875 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns, which gives any quarterback a running game to hand off to. Sammy Omosigho has 5.5 sacks and Jalen Woods has 75 tackles.

display.fanatic_story:
The Victory Bell weighs 295 pounds, and on Saturday at 12:30 in Pasadena it goes to whichever team wins USC Trojans vs UCLA Bruins and gets painted that team's colors. Kensington "Kenzie" Rhee has already picked out the blue she'd like to see. Sterling Ashworth-Vance, who grew up a few blocks from the Coliseum, has been narrating the bell's history to anyone who stands still near the tailgate.

"Cardinal and gold," Sterling says. "It's been cardinal and gold for most of my life. The bell likes us."

"The bell is a bell, Sterling. It doesn't have feelings."

"It has a preference."

Kenzie lets that one go, because she has the better season to talk about. UCLA is 10-1, ranked fourth in the country and sitting first in the Big Ten. The Bruins beat Oregon 17-15 on the road in October and haven't lost at the Rose Bowl all year. Beat USC and they're in the Big Ten title game in Indianapolis. Lose, and if Indiana, Iowa and Oregon all win, a four-way tie hands those two spots to Oregon and Iowa.

"So no pressure," Sterling says, grinning.

"Plenty of pressure. Pressure is fine. We like pressure."

Then there's the part neither of them wants to say out loud first. Last week at Michigan, quarterback Ty Dieffenbach got carted off after a big hit in the first overtime, and third-stringer Madden Iamaleava finished the 18-16 loss. Kenzie watched it from her couch with her hands over her mouth.

"I'm not talking about it," she says. "I'm talking about Wayne Knight."

That's fair, because Knight is a problem. He has 875 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns, and the UCLA defense behind him gives up 14.5 points a game. Jalen Woods leads the team with 75 tackles, and Sammy Omosigho has 5.5 sacks. Nevada didn't score at the Rose Bowl. Wisconsin scored seven.

Sterling's Trojans come in 8-3 after a 35-21 win over Maryland on Senior Day that took a while to get going. USC woke up at halftime and scored 22 straight points, with freshman Trent Mosley catching two touchdowns. Mosley has 720 receiving yards and eight scores this year. Jayden Maiava has thrown for 3,072 yards and 23 touchdowns, and King Miller leads the ground game with 797 yards.

"Freshman," Sterling says. "Wait until you see him as a sophomore. You'll want to move to Arizona."

"I'd rather see him this Saturday so I can watch him get tackled."

The road has been the Trojans' issue. They scored seven at Wisconsin and 13 at Indiana in their last two trips. Sterling blames the time zones. Kenzie points out that Pasadena is not in a different time zone.

"Rose Bowl's a road game in spirit," Sterling says. "It's a whole different vibe out here. Mountains. Fresh air. It's disorienting."

"It's down the freeway from your house."

"Not with traffic it isn't."

The history cuts both ways. USC has won seven of the last ten meetings, including 29-10 last year. Kenzie brings up 2006, when UCLA beat a No. 2 USC team 13-9 at the Rose Bowl, and Sterling says he was too young to be emotionally scarred by it, which is a lie, because he brings it up himself every November.

Here's how it goes. The bell gets rung by both sides before kickoff, the stadium splits right down the middle, and USC moves the ball early, with Maiava finding Mosley for a touchdown. UCLA hands it to Knight over and over, and he answers with two scores before halftime. The Trojans take a late lead, but Knight breaks one in the fourth quarter, and the Bruins' defense stops USC near midfield on the final drive. Kenzie cries. Sterling stares at the bell.

He'll admit afterward that blue isn't a terrible color. He'll say it quietly. He'll deny it the next day.

My call: UCLA Bruins 27, USC Trojans 24.

Tulane vs South Florida is the last scheduled game the Bulls will play at Raymond James Stadium before they move into their new on-campus stadium next fall. It's also Senior Day, and Brian Hartline's first season needs a better ending than three straight losses. My Tulane vs South Florida pick is South Florida Bulls −6.5 with the Over 43.5.

Reina Valdés-Kowalski is done with the last three weeks. "I sat through six hours and a tornado in Boca to watch us lose by three touchdowns. I've earned a good afternoon at home."

Antoine "Twan" Ducros-Labat is feeling a lot better about his team. "Two fourth-quarter comebacks in a row. We're bowl eligible again. You can keep your stadium send-off. We'll take the win."

The Green Wave did pull off back-to-back late rallies, beating Rice 20-17 and North Texas 28-24. But North Texas outgained them by nearly a hundred yards, and Tulane has been rough away from home. It lost 3-17 at Duke, 20-31 at Kansas State and 17-20 at Army, and it allows 27.6 points a game. This team needed a late touchdown with just over two minutes left to beat North Texas at home.

The Bulls have been bad for three weeks, no doubt. But the one before Boca was a 41-52 loss to Memphis in which they ran all over the Tigers. display.fanatic_story:
South Florida Bulls vs Tulane Green Wave is goodbye to Raymond James Stadium, and Reina Valdés-Kowalski has her speech ready. The Bulls first took the field in 1997. This is season 30. And on Saturday, they play their final scheduled game at Ray-Jay before they move into the new on-campus stadium next fall. Reina wants this one to feel like a party, not a funeral.

"Thirty years," Reina says. "Thirty years of driving to that stadium and fighting for parking. Now we'll have our own place on campus. But I'm not sad. Not yet. Ask me at the end of the fourth quarter."

The school is making it a Senior Day and a celebration of the Bulls' history in that building. Reina plans to cry once, during the senior walk, and then she plans to yell for three hours straight.

Antoine "Twan" Ducros-Labat drove in from the Big Easy, and he's here to crash the party. His Green Wave are 6-5 and bowl eligible for the fifth straight season, and they're coming off two straight fourth-quarter comebacks.

"We don't do anything easy," Twan says. "We wait until you think you've got us, and then we take it. Two weeks in a row."

He's not wrong. Tulane beat Rice 20-17, and then last week the Green Wave trailed North Texas 24-14 with under eight minutes left. Trace Johnson threw two touchdowns late, including a 28-yarder to Cameron Roberts with 2:13 left, and E'Zaiah Shine picked one off on the last play. Johnson threw for 283 yards and four touchdowns.

"Trace was a different guy last week," Twan says. "He looked like he finally figured it out."

Reina has had a rough month. The Bulls started 4-0 in Brian Hartline's first year as head coach, and everyone in Tampa was happy. Now they've lost three straight. They lost 20-17 at East Carolina, then 52-41 to Memphis, and then last week came the FAU game. The Bulls lost 35-14 in Boca in a game that lasted six hours and got stopped three times for weather, including a tornado warning.

"A tornado," Reina says. "A real one. On video. I've been to a lot of bad games, but that's the first one where the sky was against us too."

She does like her quarterback. Luke Kromenhoek threw for 385 yards against FAU, and his interception that day was his first of the season. D.J. Crowther has 689 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, and against Memphis, the Bulls ran for 268 yards as a team.

"When we run the ball, we're good," Reina says. "When we forget to run the ball, we lose to FAU in a tornado. It's simple."

Tulane's defense has had some bad days, too. The Green Wave gave up 60 to Tulsa at home and 42 to UTSA, and North Texas ran all over them last week. Dickson Agu, though, is a tackling machine. He has 109 tackles, and he had 13 against North Texas.

"Agu's everywhere," Twan says. "If your running back goes anywhere, Agu's already there, waiting."

Tulane leads the series 4-1, and the Bulls' only win came in 2017. Twan brings that up three times before lunch.

"You've beaten us one time," he says. "One."

"And Saturday, it's two," Reina says. "Write it on the stadium. It's the last thing we'll ever write there."

Here's how it goes. The crowd is loud early, and the Bulls come out running. Crowther breaks one for a touchdown in the first quarter, and Kromenhoek hits a long one before halftime. Tulane hangs around with a couple of Johnson throws, and Twan starts getting that comeback look in his eye. But the Bulls' defense finally holds late, and South Florida adds a field goal to put it away.

When it's over, Reina takes a picture of the scoreboard and a picture of the field. Twan offers to take one of her with both. She says she'll frame it and hang it in the new place.

My call: South Florida Bulls 28, Tulane Green Wave 19.

Northern Illinois is 0-11 in its first Mountain West season, and Saturday's Senior Day game against UTEP in DeKalb is the last shot to put a win on the board. My UTEP vs Northern Illinois pick is Northern Illinois Huskies −4.5 and the Over 48.5, because the Huskies have been closer to winning than their record says and UTEP has been nowhere close.

Nola Brandvik puts it the DeKalb way. "Eleven losses, and the crop's still in the ground. Saturday we harvest, or we plow it all under."

Neto Galindo isn't conceding a thing. "We're one and ten, Nola. That's one more than you. Bring the chile, we're bringing the heat."

He can say it, but UTEP's one win came against Texas Southern in September. Since then the Miners have scored 17 or fewer points in all nine games, and they lost 52-3 at Air Force last Friday. UTEP scores 13.2 a game and gives up 35.3. Raymond Moore III leads the team in throwing and running, with 722 yards in the air and 678 on the ground, which tells you how little the passing game has given them.

Northern Illinois has its own problems, but it moves the ball. Taron Dickens has 2,330 yards and 13 touchdowns, and DeAree Rogers has 86 catches for 899 yards. The Huskies rallied in the second half at North Dakota State last week before losing 31-25, and they lost 28-24 to Illinois State and 31-24 at UNLV. That's three one-score losses. UTEP lost 14-17 to Hawai'i, and nothing else has been close since September.

These two have no recent meetings, so there's no history to go on, just two last-place teams in a new league.

My margin is nine. That clears the 4.5 with room for a UTEP late score.

On the total, I have 51. Northern Illinois has scored 19 or more in five of its last six, and both defenses give up more than 35 a game. DraftKings opened Northern Illinois Huskies −4.5 with a 49.5 total, and the side hasn't moved while the total has come down a point to 48.5.

The room is all on the Huskies. The Formula has Northern Illinois 28-22 and goes Northern Illinois −4.5 and the Over. Next Man Up has 32-23 and likes the Huskies and the Over 48.5. Letdown Watch has 29-19, likes Northern Illinois and goes Under. In The Trenches has no score this week, sees the fronts as split, and takes neither side nor total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "Both these offenses are on their backup plan, and mine still says 55."

Letdown Watch: "Your plan's been wrong all year, Next Man Up. Ask Northern Illinois."

My final is Northern Illinois Huskies 30, UTEP Miners 21. Nola calls it knee-high by the Fourth of July. Neto rolls his sleeves up and heads back to the mine.

display.fanatic_story:
Somebody's leaving DeKalb on Saturday with a lot of losses and nothing to show for the season. Northern Illinois is 0-11 in its first year in the Mountain West, UTEP is 1-10, and both of them are 0-7 in league play, so when the Miners and the Huskies meet at Huskie Stadium in the season finale, one team finally gets a conference win and the other goes home with a goose egg next to its name.

Nola Brandvik has been looking at a cornfield photo on her phone for about a week.

"You plant in April," she says. "You do everything right. Then it doesn't rain. That's this season. But you still go out and harvest what's there. Saturday, there's something there."

Neto Galindo, who drove up from El Paso with a cooler full of green chile and no winter coat, has a different view of the forecast.

"It's going to be cold, I'm going to be miserable, and we're going to win," he says. "That's the most UTEP sentence I've ever said."

Let's be fair to both of them, because neither one of these seasons has been fun.

UTEP's only win came back in September, 51-10 over Texas Southern, when EJ Colson Jr. threw four touchdowns. Since then it's been hard. The Miners lost 61-7 at New Mexico and 52-3 at Air Force last Friday, and they've scored 17 or fewer points in all nine games since the Texas Southern win. Raymond Moore III took over at quarterback in October and has given them a pulse, mostly with his legs. He leads the team with 678 rushing yards, and on the season he has more yards running than most of the Miners' receivers have catching.

"Raymond Moore runs like a jalapeño," Neto says. "Not the hottest, but it gets you every time."

The closest UTEP came was a 17-14 loss to Hawai'i at home in early November. Neto rates that game a ghost pepper. He rates the Air Force game "a bell pepper. No heat. Just sad."

Northern Illinois has been closer more often, which is what makes 0-11 hurt so much. The Huskies lost 28-24 to Illinois State in the home opener. They lost 31-24 at UNLV. They went to Fargo last week and came storming back in the second half at North Dakota State before falling 31-25. Taron Dickens threw three touchdowns in that one, and DeAree Rogers caught six balls for 116 yards.

"That's the one that kept me up," Nola says. "We were right there. A bushel short."

Dickens has thrown for 2,330 yards and 13 touchdowns this year. Rogers has 86 catches for 899 yards and is one big afternoon away from four figures. Telly Johnson Jr. has 721 rushing yards, and Elijah Porter ran for 107 at North Dakota State. Jack Murray leads the defense with 84 tackles. On paper, this is the better offense on the field, and by a good bit.

The problem is that both defenses have been getting run over. Northern Illinois gives up 35.5 a game, and UTEP gives up 35.3. Hawai'i put 56 on the Huskies in October. If you're looking for a game where somebody gets stuffed on fourth-and-goal to save the day, this probably isn't it.

These two don't have any recent history, so this is a new rivalry built entirely on misery. Neto says that's the best kind. Nola says the best kind is the one you win.

Here's the thing about Senior Day for a team that hasn't won. Those seniors at Northern Illinois have been through a move to a new conference, and a season where they lost close and lost big. Saturday is their last chance to walk off that field in DeKalb with a win. That's a lot of motivation for a group of guys who've heard nothing good since Labor Day.

UTEP has motivation too. Nobody wants to fly home 1-11. But the Miners have been held to a field goal in their last game, and it's hard to see the offense suddenly catching fire in the cold in northern Illinois.

Nola will put the cornfield photo away and say, "Knee-high by the Fourth of July," which is a very big deal for her. Neto will eat green chile in the parking lot and tell everybody it was cold.

display.fanatic_story:
Darcy Fenwick tapes her old goalie stick before every home game, the same way she did before every game she ever played in, and she props it against the wall of the Slater Family Ice Arena on her way to Doyt Perry Stadium. Massachusetts Minutemen vs Bowling Green Falcons is the last game of the year for the Falcons and Senior Day in Bowling Green, and Darcy says the seniors deserve a ritual too, so she's making the walk with her stick taped up blue and orange.

Abner Kettleworth drove out from the Pioneer Valley, and he talks the way he drives: slow, careful and with plenty of pauses. "Darcy," he says. Then he waits. "We were up nineteen on Akron."

"I heard."

"Nineteen," Abner says again. Then he waits again. "Then we weren't."

That's the story of the UMass season in one game. The Minutemen opened 4-0, beating Rutgers on the road to start the year, and Abner says he enjoyed every minute of that September. Then October hit. Losses to Eastern Michigan, Miami (Ohio), Buffalo in overtime and UConn. A 31-30 overtime win over Ball State. A shutout at Toledo. And then the Akron game last Wednesday night in Amherst, where UMass led by nineteen in the second quarter and lost 34-33.

Joe Harasymiak didn't sugarcoat it. He called it disgusting and said it was his fault. Abner says he appreciated that. "Man stood up there and said it. I like a man who says it."

Now the math is simple. UMass is 5-6. A win at Bowling Green gets the Minutemen to six. Six wins would be the first shot at a bowl game for UMass since it moved up to the FBS, and even then the Minutemen would need an opening.

"We're not the ones who decide," Abner says. "We're the ones who show up. So we show up."

Logan Inagawa took the throws the last two games and threw 3 touchdowns against Akron. William Watson III has 1,349 yards and 9 touchdown throws this year. Elijah Faulkner ran for 105 yards against Akron and leads the team with 508. Timmy Hinspeter has 98 tackles, and William DePaepe has 4 sacks.

Darcy's Falcons are 3-8, but she'll tell you they're 3-4 in the conference, and she'll also tell you what happened last year. Bowling Green 45, UMass 14. Abner doesn't remember it. Darcy remembers all of it.

"And we've got Myles Bradley," Darcy says. "Sixteen sacks. Sixteen. He lives in the other team's backfield. He's got a mailbox back there."

Bradley is the reason anyone in Bowling Green feels good. Dorian Pringle has 105 tackles behind him. The offense is the problem. The Falcons got shut out 19-0 at Toledo last week. Austin Novosad has taken over at quarterback the last two games, and he threw 3 touchdowns in a 33-28 win over Kent State. Jeremiah Scoby, the tight end, leads the team with 37 catches.

"Novosad gives us a chance," Darcy says. "Bradley gives us a better one."

Here's how I see it. Bowling Green honors its seniors, the crowd is loud, and Bradley gets home early on Inagawa. The Falcons go up by ten in the second quarter. But UMass doesn't fold the way it did against Akron. Faulkner runs it in, Inagawa hits a big throw in the fourth, and the Minutemen tie it late. Then Bowling Green drives into range, and the Falcons win it with a field goal.

Abner takes a long time to say anything after the kick. Darcy waits him out. Finally he says he'll be checking the bowl lineup in the truck all the way home. Darcy grabs her stick at the ice arena and says the seniors went out the right way.

My call: Bowling Green Falcons 24, Massachusetts Minutemen 22.

display.fanatic_story:
The last time Jacksonville State played a football game in Newark, it was 1978, and Henrietta "Hen" Lofland has spent all week telling people at the Delaware Stadium gate that her uncle was there and is still mad about the parking. On Saturday at 3:30, Jacksonville State Gamecocks vs Delaware Blue Hens closes the home schedule in an 18,500-seat stadium, kids get discounted tickets, students get in free, and Burl Ashcraft-Neeley has driven up from Alabama with a cooler full of sandwiches and a very relaxed attitude.

"We already clinched," Burl says. "Title game. Liberty. December fourth. I'm here on vacation."

"You drove all the way from Alabama for a vacation?"

"I drove all the way from Alabama to watch Caden Creel. Vacation's a bonus."

Hen has heard plenty about Caden Creel this week, and she'll admit he's earned it. Last Saturday, the Gamecocks trailed Missouri State 20-3 going into the fourth quarter, and ESPN's win numbers gave them barely more than a one-in-a-hundred chance. Then Creel threw touchdown passes of 59 and 21 yards, ran for a 22-yard score, and Jacksonville State won 25-20 on Senior Day.

"One in a hundred," Burl says, holding up a finger. "My uncle has a better shot at the lottery, and he doesn't even play."

"Your uncle and my uncle should meet."

Creel leads the team in passing and rushing, with 2,417 yards and 19 touchdowns through the air and 892 on the ground. Deondre Johnson is the big-play receiver with 651 yards, and kicker Garrison Rippa set the school record with his 51st career field goal last week. On defense, safety Caleb Nix has 73 tackles and Tae Floyd has five sacks.

Hen's answer is Nick Minicucci, and she says the name like it's a family member. He set Delaware's career record for touchdown passes in the 42-30 win at New Mexico State, throwing for 398 yards and five scores, and the Blue Hens are bowl eligible for the second straight year. He has 23 touchdown throws against four interceptions. Sean Wilson is his top target with 782 yards, and tight end Scott Moore caught three touchdowns last week alone.

"Twenty-three to four," Hen says. "You know how many interceptions that is? Barely any. I've lost more umbrellas."

"You've lost more umbrellas in a month."

"In a week, Burl. I'm not proud of it."

Gavin Moul leads the Delaware defense with 84 tackles and Blake Matthews has five sacks. Hen is less excited about the rest of the defensive numbers. The Blue Hens give up 28 points a game, they lost 42-3 at Virginia in September, and Liberty came into Newark in October and won 30-14.

"Liberty," Burl says. "The same Liberty we play next week. You're a practice round."

"We're a final exam."

The two teams met last year, and Jacksonville State won 38-25. Hen remembers the score and refuses to say it out loud. She just points at the scoreboard and makes a face.

Here's how Saturday goes. The students fill the stands early, the kids wave homemade signs, and Minicucci comes out throwing, hitting Wilson for a long touchdown on the first drive. Creel answers by running it in himself. Delaware's offense keeps moving the ball, but Rippa gets the Gamecocks points every time they stall. Late in the fourth, with Delaware up by two, Creel scrambles out of trouble, finds Johnson down the sideline, and sets up the go-ahead field goal. Minicucci gets one last chance and comes up just short near midfield.

Burl will pack up his cooler, shake Hen's hand and promise to come back before another forty-eight years go by. Hen will tell him to bring his uncle.

My call: Jacksonville State Gamecocks 27, Delaware Blue Hens 26.

UAB vs North Texas comes with a quarterback problem in Denton. Tayven Jackson, who has thrown for 3,005 yards and 23 touchdowns, is out. His backup, Chris Jimerson Jr., left the Tulane game hurt early in the second half, and North Texas finished that game with a wide receiver taking snaps. My UAB vs North Texas pick is North Texas Mean Green −3.5 with the Over 47.5.

Grady Mayhew-Ochoa isn't panicking. "We ran it twenty-nine straight times at Tulane and still had them beat until the kick coverage fell apart. We don't need a quarterback. We need a handoff."

Ozella Birchfield has heard that before. "Then hand it off into the best secondary in the country. Oh wait, you won't be throwing anyway. Good luck."

Grady's point is real. North Texas ran for over three hundred yards at Tulane without a real quarterback and led by ten with under eight minutes left. Jahiem White has 1,366 yards and 16 touchdowns, and he went for 148 at Tulane. North Texas runs for 5.1 a carry against a UAB defense that allows 4.3, and Brendon Haygood added a hundred more and two scores last week. Even a one-dimensional North Texas scores; the Mean Green score 40.2 points a game.

The UAB offense is the other half of the side. Ryder Burton has six touchdown throws and nine interceptions, and he went 10 of 25 for 118 yards against UTSA. UAB scores 22.6 a game, and it runs for 4.0 a carry against a North Texas defense that allows 4.5. The Blazers will need more than that on the road.

The Over is the cleanest number on the card. Every North Texas game this season has gone over this total, all eleven of them. The lowest was 50 combined, against UNLV. North Texas allows 31.0 points a game, so UAB will get its share, too.

DraftKings opened North Texas Mean Green −4.5 with a 48.5 total. Both have come down a point since, so the side and the total got a little cheaper.

The room agrees on everything here. The Formula has 34-21 and takes North Texas Mean Green −3.5 with the Over 47.5. Next Man Up has 39-24 with North Texas and the Over. Letdown Watch has 34-24 with North Texas and the Over. In The Trenches has no pick in this game. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "He doesn't have to throw it. Thirty-nine is what happens when White carries it forty times. You'd know that if you watched the second half last week."

My final is North Texas Mean Green 36, UAB Blazers 23. North Texas wins by thirteen, well past the three and a half, and 59 combined clears the total. The Mean Green run it, run it again and wear down a UAB defense that's built to stop the throw.

display.fanatic_story:
UAB Blazers vs North Texas Mean Green is the regular-season finale in Denton, and Grady Mayhew-Ochoa spent the week making peace with a strange idea. His team might not throw the ball much on Saturday, and he's fine with that. Tayven Jackson is out with an injury he got at UTSA. Chris Jimerson Jr. got hurt early in the second half at Tulane. By the end of that game, a wide receiver named James Tyre was playing quarterback, and North Texas ran it 29 times in a row.

"Twenty-nine straight," Grady says. "I counted. Out loud. The guy next to me asked me to stop around twenty."

And here's the thing: it almost worked. The Mean Green ran for 302 yards at Tulane and led 24-14 with under eight minutes left. Then the kick coverage fell apart, Tulane hit two quick touchdowns, and it ended 28-24. Grady's still angry about it.

"We didn't lose that because we couldn't throw," he says. "We lost it on a kickoff. Coach Brown said so, and he's right."

Ozella Birchfield drove over from Birmingham with a cooler full of sandwiches and a lot of swagger. Her Blazers are 6-5 and bowl eligible for the first time since 2022. A win in Denton gets them to 7-5, their first seven-win regular season since 2021.

"I made enough sandwiches for both of us," Ozella says. "Consider it a peace offering, since you're going to need it."

UAB's whole identity is defense. The Blazers lead the country in passing defense, allowing 120.6 yards a game, and they've held all 11 opponents under 200 passing yards. If they keep North Texas under 307 on Saturday, they set a school record.

"Three hundred and seven," Grady says. "Ozella, we might not throw for seventy."

"That's the point," Ozella says. "You can't."

But North Texas doesn't need to. Jahiem White is the best running back these two have watched all year. He has 1,366 yards and 16 touchdowns, and he went for 148 at Tulane, his eighth 100-yard game of the season. Brendon Haygood added 103 yards and two scores, including a 46-yarder.

"Jahiem doesn't run past you," Grady says. "He runs through your whole family tree."

The Mean Green score 40.2 points a game, and Grady thinks they'll find a way even without a real quarterback. He's seen this team put up 50 on Charlotte and 52 on Rice.

Ozella's worried about her own offense. Ryder Burton has six touchdowns and nine interceptions, and last week against UTSA he completed 10 of 25 passes. The Blazers lost 19-17, and UTSA's last nine points came on a fumble return and a safety.

"We're not a pretty offense," Ozella says. "But we've only lost one home game all year. We'll take ugly."

"You're not at home," Grady reminds her.

UAB leads the all-time series 6-3, and Ozella says that's all she needs to know. Grady points out that North Texas won 53-24 last year, and that's all he needs to know.

Here's how it goes. North Texas comes out in the same Wildcat look it used at Tulane, with White and Haygood taking direct snaps. White breaks a long one on the first drive. UAB answers with a field goal and a short touchdown run from Rod Robinson II. But the Mean Green keep running, and by the third quarter the Blazers' front looks tired. White scores twice, Haygood adds one, and the Mean Green pull away. UAB gets a late touchdown, and Ozella still gets her school record, since North Texas barely throws it at all.

After the game, Grady eats one of her sandwiches. He says it's the best thing he's had all season, except for the 29 straight runs.

My call: North Texas Mean Green 36, UAB Blazers 23.

display.story_text:
Missouri has lost only once at Memorial Stadium this year, and Saturday's Senior Day finale against No. 22 Oklahoma is the last chance for this group to finish with a winning SEC record. My Oklahoma vs Missouri pick is Missouri Tigers −1.5 and the Over 41.5, because the Tigers are tough at home and Austin Simmons is the best quarterback in this game.

Delphine Arceneaux-Moss hits the ticker sound. "Breaking news: Missouri is good at home. Film at eleven. Also film at three-fifteen, on Faurot Field."

Savannah Redbird-Lowe doesn't flinch. "Boomer!" She waits. Nobody answers. "Three straight wins, Delphine. We roll the Schooner into Columbia and roll it right back out."

Savannah has the hot team. Oklahoma has won three in a row, 23-7 at Florida, 24-17 over Ole Miss and 28-7 over Texas A&M, and the Sooners give up just 17.9 points a game. John Mateer threw for 269 yards and three touchdowns against the Aggies. Owen Heinecke has 90 tackles.

But Oklahoma's offense comes and goes. The Sooners score 22.8 a game, lost 21-13 at home to Kentucky and 42-25 to South Carolina, and Mateer has thrown 8 interceptions. Lloyd Avant leads the team with only 469 rushing yards.

Missouri's offense is steadier. Simmons has 2,693 yards with 25 touchdowns and just 4 interceptions, and he went 17 of 22 for 314 yards and four scores in the 28-14 win over Kentucky last week. Jamal Roberts has 1,200 rushing yards. Cayden Lee has 940 receiving yards. Daeden Hopkins has 9 sacks. The Tigers beat Florida 45-17 and Texas A&M 27-6 in this building and score 29.2 a game.

These two have split the last two meetings. Missouri won 30-23 at home in 2024. Oklahoma won 17-6 last year.

My margin is two. That's half a point past the 1.5, so there's no room to spare here.

On the total, I have 44. Oklahoma's defense is real, but Simmons has thrown 25 touchdowns, and Missouri has scored 20 or more in ten of its eleven games. DraftKings opened Missouri Tigers −1.5 with a 42.5 total, and the side hasn't moved while the total has come down a point to 41.5.

The room is split everywhere. The Formula has Missouri 24-23 but takes Oklahoma +1.5 and likes the Over 41.5. Next Man Up has Missouri 21-18, goes Missouri −1.5 and likes the Under. Letdown Watch has Missouri 23-21, goes Missouri and likes the Over. In The Trenches has no score this week, sees the fronts as split, and takes neither side nor total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

The Formula: "My score has Missouri winning, Next Man Up. My side says it won't be by two. That's not a contradiction, that's math."

Next Man Up: "It's a contradiction with a calculator."

My final is Missouri Tigers 23, Oklahoma Sooners 21. Delphine breaks the news that Missouri won. Savannah says they'll roll the Schooner again.

Missouri Tigers 23, Oklahoma Sooners 21. Missouri Tigers cover the 1.5. Over 41.5.

display.fanatic_story:
For the first time since 2013, not counting the 2020 season, Missouri isn't playing Arkansas to finish its regular season. Instead it gets Oklahoma, a ranked team on a three-game win streak, on Senior Day in Columbia, and Delphine Arceneaux-Moss has been treating the schedule change like a scoop for a full week.

She hits the ticker sound on her phone. "Breaking news. The season finale is not against Arkansas. Developing."

"It's been on the schedule since last year," Savannah Redbird-Lowe says.

"Still developing."

Savannah came up from Norman in a crimson jacket and the boots she wore when she rode in rodeos, and she starts the way she always does. "Boomer!"

She waits. Delphine sips her coffee.

"You're supposed to say Sooner."

"I'm a Missouri fan in Missouri, Savannah. I'm going to let that one sit."

Here's why both of them showed up early. Missouri and Oklahoma are both 7-4. The Tigers are 4-4 in the SEC, and a win would give them a winning conference record and move them up into fifth in the league. Oklahoma is 5-3 in conference and has won three straight, including a 28-7 win over Texas A&M in Norman last week. This is the last regular-season game for both teams, and it's going to feel like a bowl game in November.

Delphine's case starts with the building. Missouri is 5-1 at home this season. It beat Florida 45-17 and Texas A&M 27-6 there in October, and it beat Kentucky 28-14 last week. Austin Simmons has been terrific all year, with 2,693 yards, 25 touchdown throws and only 4 interceptions, and he went 17 for 22 for 314 yards and four scores against Kentucky. Jamal Roberts has carried it 251 times for 1,200 yards. Cayden Lee has 940 receiving yards, and Donovan Olugbode caught two touchdowns against the Wildcats.

"Breaking," Delphine says. "Austin Simmons doesn't throw it to the other team. More at eleven."

"Four interceptions," Savannah says. "I'll give him that."

Savannah's case starts with the defense. Oklahoma allows only 17.9 points per game. The Sooners held Florida to 7, Ole Miss to 17 and Texas A&M to 7 in the last three weeks, and Owen Heinecke has 90 tackles in the middle of all of it. David Stone has 4.5 sacks up front. John Mateer has 18 touchdown throws and threw three of them against the Aggies, and he ran one in too.

"Mateer reads a defense like a barrel pattern," Savannah says. "Tight around the first one, open it up on the second, and fly home on the third."

"Delphine has no idea what that means," Delphine says, about herself, in her news voice.

Missouri's worries are real, too. It lost at home to Texas, 34-20, and got beat 48-21 at Georgia and 31-3 at Ole Miss. When the Tigers have played the best defenses on their schedule, they've had trouble finishing drives. Daeden Hopkins has 9 sacks and will need a couple more, because Mateer is dangerous if he gets out of the pocket.

Oklahoma has its own holes. The Sooners lost 21-13 at home to Kentucky, the same Kentucky team Missouri just beat by two touchdowns, and they gave up 42 to South Carolina. Mateer threw three interceptions against the Wildcats. Lloyd Avant leads the team with only 469 rushing yards, so it's mostly on the quarterback.

The recent history is as even as it gets. Missouri won 30-23 at home in 2024, and Oklahoma won 17-6 in Norman last year. One each. Saturday breaks the tie.

Kickoff is 3:15 local on Faurot Field, and the Mizzou seniors will get their names called one last time before the game.

Here's how I see it. Oklahoma's defense keeps it tight for most of the afternoon, and Mateer makes a couple of plays that make the visiting section loud. But Simmons doesn't give the ball away, Roberts wears down the Sooners in the second half, and Missouri gets one more stop late with Hopkins coming around the corner.

Delphine will hit the ticker one more time. "Breaking news: we won." Savannah will put her chin up and say they'll roll the Schooner again next year.

My call: Missouri Tigers 23, Oklahoma Sooners 21.

display.story_text:
A week ago Rutgers won at Beaver Stadium on a lateral as time ran out and a two-point throw. Now the Scarlet Knights come home to SHI Stadium to send off their seniors against a Michigan State team that has lost two straight. My Michigan State vs Rutgers prediction is Rutgers Scarlet Knights +3.5 with the Over 47.5.

Vinny Scolari has watched the ending more times than he'll admit. "Surace to Raymond, Raymond to Black, and then the two. I'm getting it framed. I'm getting the two-point try framed separately."

Shay Kowalczyk isn't interested in the replay. "We beat Michigan in the Big House this month. Nobody in New Jersey wants to talk about that."

These two teams are both 3-8, and the numbers say it should be close. Michigan State scores 17.7 points a game and allows 25.3. Rutgers scores 23.4 and allows 31.5. Michigan State's quarterback situation has been a mess. Alessio Milivojevic took most of the throws this year, but Kayd Coffman started the 45-7 loss to Oregon. I'm pricing Coffman for the Spartans and AJ Surace for Rutgers. Surace went 24 of 39 at Penn State.

Rutgers has a runner. Antwan Raymond has 911 yards and 8 touchdowns, and he ran for 101 and two scores at Penn State. KJ Duff has 774 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns. That's the Over case. Michigan State gave up 45 to Oregon and 21 to Washington in its last two games.

The Spartans' defense isn't the problem. Dion Crawford has 65 tackles and Anelu Lafaele has 4.5 sacks. The offense is. Michigan State has scored 7, 14 and 15 points in its last three games.

The spread opened at Michigan State −3.5 at DraftKings and hasn't moved. The total opened at 48.5 and dropped to 47.5. I'm on the other side of that move.

Rutgers Scarlet Knights 26, Michigan State Spartans 25 is an outright home win, so Rutgers Scarlet Knights +3.5 covers easily, and 51 total points clears 47.5.

All four cards take the Knights with the points, and three of them have the game within a field goal. The Formula has Michigan State 26-23 and takes Rutgers +3.5 with the Over. Next Man Up has Michigan State 27-26, likes Rutgers with the points and likes the Over. Letdown Watch has Michigan State 25-24, likes the Knights to cover and takes the Over. In The Trenches is the only card with Rutgers winning, 26-24, and it likes the Knights plus the points and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Shay Kowalczyk keeps a whiteboard on her refrigerator in East Lansing, and this season it has a list of Michigan State quarterbacks on it. Milivojevic. Hannan. Fancher. Coffman. She's left room at the bottom for one more. Michigan State Spartans vs Rutgers Scarlet Knights is the season finale for both teams at SHI Stadium, and Shay says she'll fill in the last name when she sees who runs out for warmups.

Vinny Scolari has his own wall decoration now. It's a still photo of Antwan Raymond lateraling the ball to Ben Black III as the clock hit zero at Beaver Stadium last Saturday. Vinny printed it at the drugstore, put it in a frame from the dollar store and hung it over his television.

"I'm getting a second one," Vinny says. "For the two-point try. Surace to Thevenin. Separate frame."

It was a game Rutgers fans will be talking about for years. The Scarlet Knights were down 16-0 early and 24-10 in the fourth quarter at Penn State. They put together a 19-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that ate almost ten minutes. Then, with six seconds left and the ball two yards away, AJ Surace threw to Raymond, Raymond pitched it to Black, and Black walked in. Greg Schiano went for two. Surace found Clay Thevenin on a swing throw, and Rutgers won 25-24. It was the school's first win over Penn State since 1988, in front of 106,200 people.

"Thirty-eight years," Vinny says. "I was waiting thirty-eight years for that. I was ready to wait forty."

Shay isn't impressed. She has her own win over a blue-blood to talk about. Michigan State went into Michigan Stadium on Nov. 7 and won 15-6.

"Fifteen to six in the Big House," Shay says. "Nobody in New Jersey brings that up. That's fine. I bring it up enough for everybody."

Both teams are 3-8, and both have had a rough fall. The Spartans opened 2-0 and then lost six of their next seven, including a 38-37 overtime loss to Illinois and a 24-21 loss to Northwestern. Since beating Michigan, they've lost to Washington and Oregon, scoring 14 and 7. Alessio Milivojevic has thrown for 1,559 yards this year, but Kayd Coffman started against Oregon. Jaziun Patterson leads the team with 6 rushing touchdowns, and Chrishon McCray has 42 catches. On defense, Dion Crawford has 65 tackles and Anelu Lafaele has 4.5 sacks.

Rutgers has been up and down too. The season opened with a loss to UMass. There was a 58-7 win over Howard, a 37-30 win at Maryland and a 31-0 loss to Nebraska. Then Penn State happened. Raymond has 911 yards and 8 touchdowns on the ground, and he ran for 101 and two scores in State College. KJ Duff has 774 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns. Sean Allison made 12 tackles against Penn State, and Sekou Kromah had two sacks.

The Scarlet Knights will honor their seniors on the Scarlet Walk before the game. Vinny says he's going early so he can clap for every one of them by name.

"These guys beat Penn State," Vinny says. "They get the Scarlet Walk and they get a parade if I'm in charge."

"You're not in charge," Shay says.

"Not yet."

Here's how I see it. Rutgers comes out flying in front of the home crowd and Raymond scores early. Michigan State answers with a short Patterson touchdown run, and the game goes back and forth all afternoon. McCray makes a big catch to give the Spartans a lead in the fourth quarter. Then Surace leads one more late drive, and Raymond punches it in from close range.

Vinny says the wall over his television is getting crowded and he'll have to move a lamp. Shay writes the last quarterback's name on her whiteboard on the drive home, and then she erases the whole thing and says next year starts clean.

My call: Rutgers Scarlet Knights 26, Michigan State Spartans 25.

Colorado State and Boise State already played this season, three weeks ago, in this same stadium, and the Broncos won 64-38. Now the Pac-12's first-ever Flex Week sends them back to Canvas Stadium for a Saturday 4 p.m. kickoff that doesn't count in the conference race, and Ansel Rimrock is treating Boise State Broncos vs Colorado State Rams like a second chance at a first impression.

"Rematch," Ansel says, zipping his jacket up to his chin. "Nobody gets a rematch in November. We got one. That's a gift."

Thatcher Bluestem drove down from Boise with two thermoses and a very calm look on his face.

"It's not a gift, Ansel. It's a scheduling quirk. We play San Diego State for the title on December fourth. This is a tune-up."

"A tune-up? You scored 64 here."

"That's what a tune-up looks like when it goes well."

Ansel doesn't love that answer, but he can't argue the numbers. Boise State's 64 points in that first game were the most the Broncos had scored in a road game since 1952, and they piled up 669 yards. Max Cutforth threw for 317 yards and four touchdowns that day, and Thatcher has a photo of the scoreboard he's been using as his computer background.

"Change it," Ansel says.

"Never."

The Broncos are 9-2, but they lost 22-20 to San Diego State last Saturday on Senior Night, losing it in the final seconds, and Thatcher is still a little sore about it. He spent the drive down replaying the last minute in his head and arguing with it. Dylan Riley has 1,360 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns. Maddux Madsen has 20 touchdown passes against just three interceptions, and Rasean Jones leads the team with 940 receiving yards.

"We lost by two to the team we play next," Thatcher says. "So I'm not worried. I'm just annoyed."

Ansel's Rams are 3-8, and he's not going to pretend this has been a fun fall. They gave up 73 at Washington State two weeks ago. They lost 49-42 at Fresno State last week. But Hauss Hejny threw for 413 yards in that Fresno game and ran for two touchdowns, and Tommy Maher had 111 receiving yards. Oumar Diomande has made 103 tackles, which Ansel says is because he's the only guy who never gets tired.

"Our offense is fine," Ansel says. "Our defense is a work in progress."

"Your defense gave up 64 to us."

"Like I said. Progress."

Colorado State has scored 35 or more six times this year, including the 56-49 win over San Diego State in October. That's the game Ansel brings up whenever anyone from Boise is in earshot.

"We beat the team that beat you," he says.

"And we beat you by 26."

"Football's weird, Thatcher."

Here's how it goes Saturday. Boise State comes out with Riley carrying it over and over, because nobody wants to get hurt a week before the title game. The Broncos take a two-score lead, but Hejny keeps throwing, and Maher catches a long one to keep the Rams in it at halftime. In the second half, Boise turns the game into a long run of handoffs and short throws, and the clock moves fast. Colorado State scores late to make the final look respectable, and Ansel celebrates the touchdown like it's the Rams who just clinched a trip somewhere.

Thatcher will shake his hand and tell him the Rams looked better than last time. Ansel will say it couldn't have looked worse, and then he'll ask Thatcher to bring the second thermos back next year, full this time, because a rematch deserves a rematch.

My call: Boise State Broncos 45, Colorado State Rams 26.

The Under comes from the Kansas side of the ledger. Not one of Kansas's eleven games this season reached 66 points. The Jayhawks allow 24.4 a game, and their run defense allows 4.0 a carry against an Oklahoma State offense that runs for 5.1. Leroy Harris III has 8.5 sacks and will be in Drew Mestemaker's face all night.

Mestemaker is the reason anyone takes the Over. He has 3,533 yards, 30 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, and Oklahoma State scores 41.1 a game. Caleb Hawkins has 1,270 rushing yards. Justin Bowick has 963 receiving yards and 10 scores. But Mestemaker threw no touchdowns at Arizona State, and Texas Tech held the Cowboys to 27 the week before.

display.fanatic_story:
Kansas Jayhawks vs Oklahoma State Cowboys gets a history lesson from Dusty Ridgeway before anybody parks. The last time Kansas won a football game at Boone Pickens Stadium was 2007, the year the Jayhawks went 12-1 and won the Orange Bowl. Dusty thinks it would take another year like that for it to happen again. And Kansas is 4-7.

"Twelve and one," Dusty says. "That's what it took. Twelve and one, and a whole lot of luck. Fitz, you've got four wins and a lot of excuses."

Fitz Calloway drove down from Lawrence anyway, wearing a crimson-and-blue hoodie under a heavy coat. It's supposed to be a brisk night in Stillwater, and he plans to be loud the whole time.

"They're not excuses," Fitz says. "They're scars. There's a difference."

He has a lot of them. Kansas lost to Arizona State by seven, TCU by six, UCF by one and BYU by two in triple overtime last week. That BYU game was strange, too. Not a single flag was thrown on either team all night.

"No flags," Fitz says. "None. The refs just stood there. And we still lost by two. You can't even blame anybody."

Dusty has his own complaint: the Cowboys can't seem to play a first half. They've been behind or tied at halftime in seven of their eight Big 12 games. Last week they came back to win 30-27 in overtime at Arizona State. The week before that, Texas Tech came into Stillwater and beat them 52-27.

"I've had to wait until halftime all year," Dusty says. "My blood pressure doctor is a big Kansas fan now."

But when Oklahoma State gets going, it can score with anybody. Drew Mestemaker has 3,533 yards and 30 touchdowns this year. The Cowboys put up 66 at Kansas State, 57 on Colorado and 39 on Oregon. Caleb Hawkins has 1,270 rushing yards, and Justin Bowick has 963 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns.

"Mestemaker throws it like he's mad at the ball," Dusty says. "I love it. It makes me nervous, and I love it."

Fitz's whole offense is Isaiah Marshall. The sophomore leads Kansas in passing with 2,054 yards and in rushing with 782. He's thrown some bad interceptions, including two against BYU, but he's also the reason they were in it.

"He's a sophomore, and he's carrying the whole thing," Fitz says. "Next year he's going to be a problem for the whole conference."

The guy Dusty doesn't want to talk about is Leroy Harris III. Kansas's defensive end leads the Big 12 with 16 tackles for loss and has 8.5 sacks. He had nine tackles against BYU.

"He's going to get to Mestemaker," Fitz says. "And when he does, the whole stadium's going to get quiet. I'll be the only one cheering."

"You'll be the only one in crimson, too," Dusty says.

Kansas has won two of the last three in this series, including a 38-21 win last year. Fitz brings that up whenever Dusty brings up 2007.

"You've got last year," Dusty says. "I've got the last nineteen years in this building."

Here's how it goes. Kansas comes out fast again. Marshall runs for a touchdown on the first drive, and Harris gets a sack that gets Fitz on his feet. The Cowboys are behind at halftime for the eighth time in nine conference games, and Dusty is pacing. Then Mestemaker finds Bowick for a long score, Hawkins runs one in, and the Cowboys take control in the third quarter. Kansas keeps coming, though, and gets a touchdown late to make it a one-score game again. The Cowboys recover the onside kick.

After the game, Dusty finds Fitz at the gate. He says that's five one-score losses now, and Kansas should get a trophy for it. Fitz says he'll put it right next to the Orange Bowl one.

My call: Oklahoma State Cowboys 34, Kansas Jayhawks 29.

San Diego State has clinched a spot in the Pac-12 championship game against Boise State, and Saturday's trip to Pullman is a flex game that doesn't count in the conference race. Washington State gets a second shot at the team that beat it 26-20 in San Diego on Halloween, on its own field and on Senior Day. My San Diego State vs Washington State pick is Washington State Cougars −2.5 and the Over 45.5, because one team has everything to play for and the other has next week to worry about.

Hank Palouse has the tape from the first game, literally. "Cassette, labeled October 31. I've played it eleven times. We had the ball at the end, and we're getting it back."

Kai Delgado-Sorensen shrugs it off. "Dude, we just knocked off Boise in their house. Pullman in November is a small swell. We paddle out, we paddle in, we go surf the big one next week."

That's the problem for the Aztecs. They won 22-20 at Boise State last Saturday, and the real game is the rematch with the Broncos. Stone Saunders has only 3 touchdown throws and 5 interceptions in 140 attempts, and San Diego State has scored 26 or fewer in seven of its eleven games. Javion Kinnard has 812 rushing yards, and Sione Hala has 101 tackles, but this is not an offense that wins by blowing teams out.

Washington State is 2-9 and lost 42-14 at Texas State last week. But the Cougars beat Colorado State 73-7 at home two weeks ago, and they had the Aztecs on the ropes in San Diego. Owen Eshelman threw for 299 yards in that game. Branden Ganashamoorthy has 597 receiving yards, and Kirby Vorhees has 8 rushing touchdowns.

Washington State also won 36-13 in Pullman last year and 29-26 in 2024.

My margin is four. That clears the 2.5 with a little room.

On the total, I have 50. San Diego State gives up 31.1 a game, Washington State scores 23.5, and the Aztecs went 56-49 at Colorado State earlier this year. DraftKings opened San Diego State Aztecs −3 with a 46.5 total, and the side has flipped all the way to Washington State Cougars −2.5 while the total has come down a point.

The room splits on the side. The Formula has Washington State 27-25, takes San Diego State +2.5 and likes the Over 45.5. Next Man Up has Washington State 25-19, likes the Cougars and goes Under. Letdown Watch has Washington State 31-20 and likes the Cougars and the Over. In The Trenches has San Diego State 28-25 and likes the Aztecs +2.5, with no total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

display.fanatic_story:
Hank Palouse has a cassette tape on his kitchen table with "OCT 31" written on the label in black marker. He recorded the radio call of Washington State's 26-20 loss in San Diego, the one where the Cougars drove for the go-ahead score in the final minute and got turned away, and he's been listening to it in the combine all month. Now the Cougars get the Aztecs again, in Pullman, on Senior Day, and Hank has already hung Ol' Crimson out the front window.

"Second chance," Hank says. "You don't get many of those in life. I'm not wasting this one."

Kai Delgado-Sorensen flew up from San Diego with a beanie, two sweatshirts and a very relaxed attitude about the whole thing.

"Hank, my man, respect. But this is a flex game. It doesn't count. We beat Boise on the blue turf last week, and we play them again for the whole thing on December 4. This one's a small wave. We're just out here keeping our arms loose."

That's the setup for Saturday. The rebuilt Pac-12 added a flex week this year, and the results don't count in the league standings. San Diego State is 6-5 overall and 5-2 in the conference, and its 22-20 win at Boise State last week clinched a spot in the championship game. Washington State is 2-9 and 1-6 in league play, sitting in seventh place. The league paired them up for one more game, and Pullman gets a home date with a team that has its mind on next week.

"They're looking past us," Hank says. "Good. Let them look."

Kai doesn't argue with that so much as wave it off. "We don't look past anybody. We just look at the forecast."

The Aztecs have done it with defense and a running game. Javion Kinnard has 812 rushing yards. Sione Hala has 101 tackles, and Djibril Rahman has 5 sacks. Stone Saunders took over at quarterback in October and the Aztecs have won four of five since, including the win over the Cougars in San Diego, but the throwing part is still a work in progress. He has 3 touchdowns and 5 interceptions this year. San Diego State has also given up 31.1 points per game, and it lost 66-14 at Oregon State and 56-49 at Colorado State.

"Wipeouts," Kai says. "Everybody wipes out. You paddle back out."

Hank's case is the quarterback on his side. Owen Eshelman threw for 299 yards against the Aztecs in October and ran for two touchdowns, and he went 13 for 14 when the Cougars put up 73 on Colorado State two weeks ago. Branden Ganashamoorthy has 597 receiving yards. Kirby Vorhees has 8 rushing touchdowns. Keith Brown has 89 tackles.

Last week wasn't pretty. Washington State lost 42-14 at Texas State, and Hank told a 20-minute story on the drive home about a wheat harvest years back that went sideways, which is what he does after a bad loss.

"Cougs never quit," Hank says. "You heard me say it after Texas State. I'll say it again on Saturday, but louder."

The Cougars do have recent history in their corner. They're 3-2 all-time against San Diego State and won the only previous meeting in Pullman, 36-13 last season. They also won a 29-26 game in 2024. Kai calls those different eras. Hank has the tapes of both.

"Of course you do," Kai says.

The Cougars will honor their seniors before the 3:30 local kickoff. It's the last game in Martin Stadium for a group that's been through a lot, and Hank wants them to go out on a high note. The Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation are presenting the game, and Hank says he'll bring the Ol' Crimson flag for the senior walk.

Here's where I come out. San Diego State is the better team on paper, but the Aztecs have a title game in six days, and they'll be careful with the guys they need. Washington State has nothing left to save. Eshelman throws it around Martin Stadium like it's October again, Vorhees punches one in, and this time the Cougars get the stop at the end.

Hank will wave Ol' Crimson until his arms hurt. Kai will say "wipeout, dude," pull his beanie down and fly home to get ready for Boise.

My call: Washington State Cougars 27, San Diego State Aztecs 23.

display.story_text:
Tennessee is No. 9 in the country and 9-2, and Vanderbilt is playing for nothing but pride and its seniors in the regular-season finale at FirstBank Stadium. My Tennessee vs Vanderbilt prediction is Vanderbilt Commodores +13.5 with the Over 43.5.

Earl Haskew drove in on Interstate 40 at dawn. "We've beaten Alabama, Kentucky, Texas A&M and LSU. Our defense gives up 14.2 a game. Pippa, I'm being polite by showing up."

Pippa Ashcroft doesn't look up from her notes. "You beat LSU with 79 yards through the air, Earl. You're running the ball because you have to."

Pippa has a point. Tennessee wins with defense and the ground game. DeSean Bishop has 1,215 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns. George MacIntyre has taken the throws since October, and against LSU he went 12 of 21 for 79 yards. Faizon Brandon ran for 112 yards and two scores in that game. The defense is the real thing, with Tyree Weathersby at 7 sacks and Arion Carter at 75 tackles.

That's the problem with laying 13.5. A team that throws for 79 yards doesn't pull away from many opponents. Tennessee won 22-7 at Texas A&M and 27-13 over LSU. Those are wins by 15 and 14. Both barely clear the spread, and both were games Tennessee controlled.

Vanderbilt is 4-7, but the Commodores can move the ball through the air. Jared Curtis has 2,080 yards, and Junior Sherrill has 69 catches for 996 yards. Sherrill had 149 yards at Florida in a 34-27 loss. Sedrick Alexander ran for 129 in that game. The problem is defense, at 29.1 points allowed per game.

I'm pricing MacIntyre for Tennessee and Curtis for Vanderbilt. Vanderbilt gets a couple of big plays to Sherrill, Tennessee runs the ball, and the Volunteers win without pulling away.

The Over is the other half. Tennessee has scored 31.0 points a game, and Vanderbilt gives up 29.1. Vanderbilt scored 27 at Florida. A total of 43.5 is low for two teams that combine for more than 50 points a game on offense.

Tennessee Volunteers 30, Vanderbilt Commodores 19 is an 11-point Tennessee win, so Vanderbilt Commodores +13.5 covers by two and a half, and 49 total points clears 43.5.

Three of the four cards take Vandy with the points. The Formula has Tennessee 31-18, takes Vanderbilt Commodores +13.5 and likes the Over. Letdown Watch: "Tennessee wants to make a statement for the committee. Big win, big margin."

display.fanatic_story:
Pippa Ashcroft teaches English at a school in Nashville, and she grades everything with a red pen, including the game program. By kickoff on Saturday night, she'll have circled every typo in it and written "see me" next to the Tennessee roster. Tennessee Volunteers vs Vanderbilt Commodores is the regular-season finale at FirstBank Stadium and Senior Day for the Commodores, and Pippa says the seniors deserve a clean program, so she's bringing an extra one to hand in.

Earl "Rocky Top" Haskew drove in from Knoxville on I-40, and he's wearing so much orange that Pippa says he looks like a construction zone. "That's on purpose," Earl says. "Everybody slows down when they see me coming."

Earl has a lot to be happy about. Tennessee is 9-2 and ranked No. 9 in the country. The Volunteers have beaten Alabama, Auburn, Arkansas, Kentucky, Texas A&M and LSU. The two losses were 20-17 to Texas and 27-24 at South Carolina. The defense has allowed 14.2 points a game.

"We beat LSU by two touchdowns last week," Earl says. "We held Texas A&M to seven. I'm not worried about anybody."

The Volunteers win with the ground game and the defense. DeSean Bishop has 1,215 yards and 13 touchdowns. George MacIntyre has been the quarterback since October, and Faizon Brandon ran for 112 yards and two scores against LSU. Mike Matthews has 608 receiving yards. Tyree Weathersby has 7 sacks, and Arion Carter has 75 tackles.

Pippa listens, takes notes and circles one number. "Seventy-nine yards, Earl. That's what your quarterback threw for against LSU. I'd give that a C-minus."

"We didn't need to throw it."

"That's what everyone says right before they need to throw it."

Pippa's Commodores are 4-7, and it's been a hard year after last fall, when Vanderbilt went undefeated at home for the first time at FirstBank Stadium. Clark Lea was the SEC Coach of the Year two seasons running, and this year the wins have been harder to find. Vanderbilt beat Austin Peay, Delaware, NC State and Mississippi State. The losses include Georgia, Ole Miss, Arkansas, Kentucky, Alabama and a 34-27 game at Florida last week.

But Pippa can still point to her offense. Jared Curtis has thrown for 2,080 yards and 10 touchdowns. Junior Sherrill has 69 catches for 996 yards. Sherrill had 149 yards at Florida, and Sedrick Alexander ran for 129 in the same game. CJ Heard leads the defense with 83 tackles.

"Sherrill needs four yards to get to a thousand," Pippa says. "He'll get them on the first drive. I've already written the sentence."

Pippa also keeps a short list of Vanderbilt wins over Tennessee taped inside her grade book. Three in a row from 2016 to 2018, including a 45-34 game in 2016. Earl keeps a longer list. Tennessee won every meeting from 2019 through 2024, including 56-0 in 2022 and 36-23 in 2024.

"Your list is longer," Pippa says. "Mine is better written."

Here's how I see it. The seniors are honored before the game, Pippa hands in her program, and Vanderbilt scores first on a long throw from Curtis to Sherrill. Sherrill goes over a thousand yards on the play. Tennessee answers with Bishop, and the Volunteers' defense takes over in the second quarter. Brandon breaks a long run, Bishop scores again, and Tennessee goes up by two touchdowns in the third. Vanderbilt keeps throwing and gets a late touchdown to make it respectable.

Earl heads for I-40 with his orange on and his windows down, singing. Pippa marks the final score in red and writes "acceptable" next to it, which she says is the highest grade she has ever given Tennessee.

My call: Tennessee Volunteers 30, Vanderbilt Commodores 19.
