display.fanatic_story:
For the first 125 games of a series that goes back to 1891, Indiana and Purdue never played each other at night. Then came 2024, and now, for the third straight year, the Old Oaken Bucket game is under the lights, with Purdue Boilermakers vs Indiana Hoosiers kicking off at 7 p.m. Saturday at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington. Mallory Penhallow is in the parking lot with a garment bag, a folding table and a printed spreadsheet she calls "the Bucket plan."

"What's in the garment bag?" asks Barnaby Wolcott-Reese, who drove down from West Lafayette and parked next to her on purpose.

"The jersey I wear when we carry the Bucket off the field."

"You have a special jersey for carrying a bucket."

"I have a special jersey for winning. The Bucket is just where it ends up."

Barnaby has heard this before. Indiana has held the Bucket since 2024, and the last two games ended 66-0 and 56-3. That's 122 points to three, and Mallory has it on her spreadsheet in bold, right under a row labeled "Bucket polish schedule."

"You put that in bold?"

"I put everything in bold, Barnaby. It's a celebration."

Purdue is 3-8, and Barnaby isn't going to pretend otherwise. The Boilermakers have lost five in a row, including 42-10 to Wisconsin last week on their own field. Ryan Browne has 2,551 passing yards, Fame Ijeboi has 724 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns, and Asaad Waseem leads the team with 816 receiving yards. Charles Correa has 83 tackles. But there were good days early, like a 41-13 win over Minnesota and a 24-17 win at Illinois.

"We beat Illinois," Barnaby says. "On the road. Write that in bold."

"I'll write it in a footnote."

Mallory's Hoosiers are 9-2, and they lost 27-24 in overtime at Washington last week, which she describes as "a scheduling error." Indiana's coach, Curt Cignetti, said afterward that the team was down five or six starters. Josh Hoover came off the bench to lead a touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, and Charlie Becker caught six balls for 167 yards, including a 74-yard score.

"Becker's got 1,117 yards," Mallory says. "Eleven touchdowns. He's going to catch two more on Saturday and I'm going to cry both times."

"You cry at kickoffs."

"I cry at the national anthem, Barnaby. I'm an emotional person."

The Indiana defense is the real reason Mallory brought the garment bag. Tobi Osunsanmi has 10 sacks, Isaiah Jones has 77 tackles, and the Hoosiers give up 13.8 points a game. Western Kentucky and Howard didn't score in Bloomington. Purdue has scored three points in the last two meetings combined.

"Three," Barnaby says. "We kicked a field goal. That's a start."

"That's not a start. That's a souvenir."

Here's how Saturday goes. The lights come up, the student section is loud before the team even gets out of the tunnel, and Indiana gets the ball first. Lee Beebe Jr. runs it straight at the Purdue front, and Becker gets loose for the first touchdown. Purdue answers with a field goal, and Barnaby high-fives three strangers. Then Osunsanmi gets to Browne on third down, Indiana scores again before halftime, and the second half turns into a long walk for the visitors. Purdue gets a late touchdown on an Ijeboi run, which is more than the last two years combined.

Mallory will carry the Bucket out of the stadium in her special jersey. Barnaby will ask to take a picture with it, just once, so he can remember what it looks like up close. Then he'll drive back to West Lafayette and start counting the days until next November.

My call: Indiana Hoosiers 38, Purdue Boilermakers 13.

display.story_text:
Auburn vs Alabama is the Iron Bowl, and this week the biggest question is on the Auburn sideline. Alex Golesh pulled Byrum Brown two plays into the Samford game, and Tristan Ti'a went 17 of 18 for 341 yards and four touchdowns in a half. Golesh hasn't said who starts in Tuscaloosa. My Auburn vs Alabama pick is Auburn Tigers +16.5 with the Over 48.5.

Mary-Kathryn "MK" Strickland sounds very relaxed about it. "Start Brown, start Ti'a, start the band director. We've won seven straight Iron Bowls in this building."

Lacey Bellamy fires right back. "And we beat Georgia in Athens, MK. You lost to them at home. Let's see who's relaxed at halftime."

That's the side. The number opened at ten and has jumped six and a half points, and that's a lot of rivalry points to lay. Six of the last ten Iron Bowls were decided by fewer than seventeen points. Auburn won 27-24 at Georgia, and Alabama scored 17 against Georgia and 10 at Tennessee. When the Tide play a real defense, the margins shrink. Auburn allows 23.9 points a game and 3.5 yards a carry.

The Over is about who these teams are on offense. Alabama scores 36.8 a game, and Keelon Russell has 21 touchdowns and six picks. He sat out against Chattanooga, and Austin Mack threw four touchdowns in his place. Auburn scores 29.0 a game, and eight of its eleven games have gone over this total. Keshaun Singleton has 744 receiving yards and eight scores. Whoever plays quarterback, Auburn will take shots down the field.

The risk is the Alabama run defense, which allows just 2.7 yards a carry. Auburn runs for 4.3. That means Auburn has to throw, and Auburn throwing against Yhonzae Pierre and that pass rush cuts both ways. A sack-and-turnover game could get away fast. But turnovers also put points on the board, and that's fine for the Over.

DraftKings opened Alabama Crimson Tide −10 with a 52.5 total. The side is up six and a half since, and the total has dropped four.

The room likes the Over across the board. The Formula has 33-19 and takes Auburn Tigers +16.5 with the Over 48.5. Letdown Watch has 33-18 with Auburn and the Over. Next Man Up has 36-19 and takes Alabama Crimson Tide −16.5 with the Over. In The Trenches has no pick in this game. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "Letdown Watch, you can't even tell me who Auburn's quarterback is, and you want the points?"

Letdown Watch: "Neither can Golesh, and he's the one getting the points. Bring a sweater to Tuscaloosa and keep your opinions warm."

My final is Alabama Crimson Tide 34, Auburn Tigers 19. Alabama wins by fifteen, a point and a half inside the number, and 53 combined clears the total. The Tide get their eighth straight at home, and Auburn hangs around long enough to cover.

display.fanatic_story:
Auburn Tigers vs Alabama Crimson Tide is a Saturday night Iron Bowl in Tuscaloosa, and Mary-Kathryn "MK" Strickland has been counting. Alabama has won the last seven Iron Bowls played at Bryant-Denny Stadium. She wants eight. She's already planning what she'll text her cousin in Opelika when it's over.

"Seven straight here," MK says. "I don't like to brag. I just like to say it out loud, slowly, to people from Auburn."

Lacey Bellamy came over from Auburn with an orange-and-blue scarf and an attitude. Her Tigers are 7-4, and she thinks that's a lot better than it sounds, because one of those wins came in Athens.

"We went to Georgia and won," Lacey says. "Twenty-seven to twenty-four. Y'all played them in Tuscaloosa and lost. In your own house."

MK pretends she didn't hear that.

Alabama is 9-2 and ranked third. The Tide lost to Georgia 20-17 and at Tennessee 26-10, but they've won four straight since, including 31-13 at LSU and 21-6 at Vanderbilt. Keelon Russell sat out last week against Chattanooga, and the coaches said he could have played. They just didn't want to risk him before this one.

"Keelon's fine," MK says. "He was resting. Like a racehorse. You don't run your racehorse in the practice race."

Russell has 2,480 yards, 21 touchdowns and six interceptions. Lotzeir Brooks is his go-to receiver, with 597 yards. The Tide score 36.8 points a game and give up 17.2.

And then there's the Alabama defense. It allows just 2.7 yards a carry. Yhonzae Pierre has 6.5 sacks. The Tide have 31 sacks as a team, and they've taken five interceptions back for touchdowns.

"That's the scary part," Lacey admits. "Our blockers have given up 39 sacks. If your guys get loose, I'm hiding my eyes."

The other question is who Lacey's watching at quarterback. Byrum Brown has started all year. He's thrown for 2,035 yards and leads Auburn in rushing with 644. But in the Samford game, Alex Golesh pulled him after two plays, and Tristan Ti'a came in and went 17 of 18 for 341 yards and four touchdowns in one half.

"I don't know who's starting," Lacey says. "Golesh doesn't either, or he isn't telling. I'd play Ti'a. I'd play both. I'd play anybody who can throw it to Keshaun."

Keshaun Singleton has 744 receiving yards and eight touchdowns, and Chas Nimrod had 157 yards against Samford. Auburn scores 29.0 points a game, and Lacey thinks the Tigers can get to 20 against anybody.

"We put 41 on Mississippi State," she says. "We put 39 on Florida. We can score."

"You lost to Florida," MK says.

"By five," Lacey says. "Close ones count for something."

"Not in this state they don't," MK says. "In this state, you win the Iron Bowl or you hear about it until next Thanksgiving."

Here's how Saturday goes. Bryant-Denny is loud from the start. Auburn takes a deep shot early and hits it, and Lacey jumps out of her seat and stays up there a while. Alabama answers with a long drive, and Russell finds Brooks for a touchdown. The Tide's rush starts getting home in the second quarter, and Pierre gets a big sack that leads to an Alabama field goal. Alabama pulls away in the third. Auburn gets a couple of late scores to keep it respectable, and Lacey is still standing at the end.

When it's over, MK sends the text to her cousin in Opelika. It just says: Eight. Lacey tells her she'll see her next year, and that she's going to be insufferable when it's her turn.

My call: Alabama Crimson Tide 34, Auburn Tigers 19.

display.story_text:
Pitt doesn't know who its quarterback is for Saturday, and it's still laying 9.5 on the road. Holden Geriner started at Louisville and got pulled in the third quarter of a 42-10 loss, Corey Dailey started the Florida State game before that, and Mason Heintschel has been out since he tore his ACL at Virginia Tech in October. My Pitt vs Cal pick is Pittsburgh Panthers −9.5 and the Over 47.5, because whoever plays quarterback for Pitt is going against the worst defense it's seen in weeks.

Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci blows the homemade whistle. "Louisville was a yikes. Big yikes. But yinz seen Cal's defense? That's a yinz week if I ever saw one."

Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch has a sign ready. It reads RESPECT THE BEAR. "Pittsburgh has lost five of its last six. You're asking a team in crisis to travel to Berkeley and dominate. I reject the premise."

Quentin can reject it, but the numbers are rough for Cal. The Bears are 3-8, have lost five straight, and gave up 44 to Stanford at home last week. Cal allows 33.1 points a game and scores 21.1. Over the five-game skid, it's given up 41, 59, 31, 36 and 44. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele has 2,019 yards and 12 touchdowns, and Adam Mohammed ran for 90 yards against Stanford, but Cal hasn't scored more than 28 in any of those five losses.

Pitt is 6-5 and already bowl-eligible, and it still scores 27.9 a game. Damon Ferguson Jr. has 740 rushing yards, Cataurus Hicks has 750 receiving yards, and the defense gives up 21.5 a game. Cruce Brookins has 80 tackles. Pitt also beat Georgia Tech 34-11 with Geriner at quarterback in late October.

These two met in 2024, and Pitt won 17-15.

My margin is 12. That clears the 9.5 by two and a half, which leaves room for one Cal touchdown late.

On the total, I have 50. Cal's defense has given up 31 or more in five straight games, and Pitt only needs a normal day on offense to get into the 30s. DraftKings opened the Pittsburgh Panthers −7.5 with a 47.5 total, and the side has moved two points to −9.5 while the total hasn't moved.

Every card in the room is on Pitt. The Formula has Pitt 31-21 and goes Pitt −9.5 and likes the Over 47.5. Next Man Up has 31-20, goes Pitt and likes the Over. Letdown Watch has 31-20, goes Pitt and likes the Over. In The Trenches has Pitt 31-16 and likes Pittsburgh −9.5, with no total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "I wrote 31 without knowing who the quarterback is. That's the job."

Letdown Watch: "You wrote 31 because we all wrote 31. That's copying."

My final is Pittsburgh Panthers 31, California Golden Bears 19. Yinz yells it so loud the board op flinches. Quentin organizes a peaceful protest against the punter.

Pittsburgh Panthers 31, California Golden Bears 19. Pittsburgh Panthers cover the 9.5. Over 47.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Cal and Pitt played five times between 1955 and 1966, then went almost six decades without seeing each other until a 2024 game in Pittsburgh. Cal won two of the three games ever played at its place. Now they're ACC opponents, Cal is closing out its season at Databricks Field on Saturday, and Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch is standing outside California Memorial Stadium with a cardboard sign that reads HISTORY IS ON OUR SIDE.

Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci reads it twice and blows his homemade whistle.

"History? Quentin, buddy, the guys in that history are your grandpa's age. I'm talking about this week."

"History is a living document," Quentin says. "Also, I made a second sign."

The second sign says RESPECT THE BEAR. He made a third that says DEFEND THE TURF, and he's got a backup roll of tape in his jacket in case the wind kicks up.

The truth is both of these fan bases could use a good Saturday.

Cal is 3-8 and has lost five in a row. The skid started with a 41-7 loss to Wake Forest, ran through a 59-20 loss at SMU, and ended last week with a 44-28 loss at home to Stanford, which is the one that keeps Quentin up at night. A loss to Pitt would leave the Bears at 3-9, their worst finish since a 1-11 season back in 2013. Cal is tied with Georgia Tech for last place in the ACC.

"I'm not saying it's been a good year," Quentin says. "I'm saying the year isn't over. There's a difference, and I'm prepared to march about it."

Pitt's year has been strange in a different way. The Panthers started 5-0, and Mason Heintschel looked like one of the best young quarterbacks in the league. He threw seven touchdowns against Miami (OH) and six against Bucknell. Then he tore his ACL at Virginia Tech on Oct. 2, and Pitt has gone 1-5 since. Holden Geriner and freshman Corey Dailey have traded the job back and forth, and Geriner got pulled in the third quarter of last week's 42-10 loss at Louisville. Nobody outside the Pitt building knows yet who's taking the first snap in Berkeley.

"Yikes," Yinz says. "That whole stretch is a yikes. I've had the whistle in my mouth since October and I haven't blown it for anything good."

He's not wrong. Pitt is 0-3 on the road since Heintschel went down. The Panthers lost 16-10 at home to Florida State with Dailey under center, and the offense has scored 10 points in each of the last two games.

But here's what Yinz keeps coming back to. Pitt is 6-5 and already going to a bowl. Damon Ferguson Jr. has 740 yards on the ground. Cataurus Hicks has 750 receiving yards on just 38 catches, so he turns a lot of them into big gains. Cruce Brookins has 80 tackles, Jaeden Moore has 4.5 sacks, and the Pitt defense gives up just 21.5 points a game. When the Panthers beat Georgia Tech 34-11 on Halloween, Geriner was the quarterback.

"So it can be done," Yinz says. "I've seen it. I got it on my phone."

Cal's defense hasn't been able to slow much of anybody down lately. The Bears give up 33.1 a game and have allowed 31 or more in five straight. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele has 2,019 yards and 12 touchdowns, and Chase Hendricks has 69 catches, but the offense hasn't topped 28 in any of the last five games. Adam Mohammed ran for 90 yards and a touchdown against Stanford, and he's the guy Quentin wants to see carry it 25 times.

"Give it to Adam," Quentin says. "Power to the play-call. Run the ball, keep their quarterback, whoever it is, standing on the sideline."

"That's a good plan," Yinz says. "That's a real yinz plan. You just don't got the guys to stop us after."

Quentin writes that down on the back of the RESPECT THE BEAR sign so he can protest it later.

The one recent meeting was close. Pitt won 17-15 in Pittsburgh in 2024. Pitt leads the all-time series 4-2, and the Panthers have never lost to Cal at home. In Berkeley, it's a different story, and that's the whole point of Quentin's first sign.

Kickoff is 4:30 local, so the sun will be going down over the bay by the second half. It's the last game of the year for Cal, and for a lot of those guys in blue and gold, it's the last time they'll play in that stadium.

Here's how I see it. Pitt figures out who's playing quarterback by Thursday and keeps it simple. Ferguson carries it, Hicks gets behind the Cal secondary once or twice, and the Panthers defense does what it does to a Cal offense that's been stuck. Mohammed gets his yards, and Cal scores enough to make Quentin wave his signs in the fourth quarter. But Pitt pulls away.

Yinz will yell "Yinz SEE that?!" so loud the board op flinches. Quentin will fold up his signs, look at the sunset, and announce a peaceful protest against the punter.

My call: Pittsburgh Panthers 31, California Golden Bears 19.

Oregon scores 34.8 points a game.

Demond Williams Jr. has 2,182 yards and 14 touchdowns, and Chris Lawson has 61 catches for 910 yards. Alex McLaughlin leads the defense with 78 tackles. The Huskies allow 21.4 points a game.

The issue for Washington is the pass rush. Uiagalelei and the Ducks' front can make Williams uncomfortable, and Washington doesn't have a sack leader with more than 3. That's a big gap up front.

display.fanatic_story:
Vangie Tollefsrud rows on Lake Washington at five in the morning, every morning, and she says it's the only time of day in Seattle when nobody is talking about Oregon. Washington Huskies vs Oregon Ducks is Senior Day at Autzen Stadium, and Vangie is making the drive down Interstate 5 with her rowing gloves still in the back seat.

Nix Wyatt-Aldana rides a yellow scooter to Autzen on game days, and she parks it in the same spot every time. "Same spot, same helmet, same result," Nix says. "We've won four in a row. I'm not changing anything."

Nix has reasons to be superstitious. The Ducks were 4-3 after a 21-10 loss at Illinois in late October, and people in Eugene were starting to grumble. Then Oregon rattled off four straight. A 34-26 win over Northwestern. A 41-28 win at Ohio State. A 31-7 win over Michigan. And a 45-7 win at Michigan State last Friday night. Now a win over Washington likely sends the Ducks to Indianapolis for the Big Ten championship game.

"Indianapolis," Nix says. "I've already looked up the parking."

The Ducks have a quarterback playing his best football. Dylan Raiola has 16 touchdown throws and just 2 interceptions. He threw for 341 yards and 4 scores against Michigan. Dakorien Moore has 9 touchdown catches, Dierre Hill Jr. leads the team in rushing, and Brandon Smith ran for 121 yards and two scores at Michigan State. On defense, Matayo Uiagalelei has 9.5 sacks and Devon Jackson has 66 tackles.

Vangie listens to all of it, and then she brings up last Saturday.

"Indiana," she says. "The defending national champions. In overtime. In Husky Stadium. I don't need to say anything else."

She says plenty else anyway. Washington is 7-4, and the Huskies have been close in all four losses but one. They lost 27-24 to Minnesota, 25-21 at USC and 28-25 to Penn State. Demond Williams Jr. is back at quarterback, with 2,182 yards and 14 touchdowns. He ran for 88 yards and a score against Indiana. Chris Lawson has 61 catches for 910 yards, and Dezmen Roebuck caught 10 throws against the Hoosiers. Alex McLaughlin leads the defense with 78 tackles.

"We don't get blown out," Vangie says. "We get close. Sometimes we win."

Nix has an answer. "You got blown out here last time. Forty-nine to twenty-one."

This rivalry has been wild lately. Washington won three straight in 2022 and 2023, including two in the same season, the second one in the conference title game. Then Oregon won 49-21 in 2024. Vangie remembers the first three. Nix remembers the last one.

Then there's the quarterback picture, which has been a story in both towns. Oregon opened the year with Dante Moore, who threw for 378 yards against Boise State and 4 touchdowns against Portland State, before Raiola took over at USC in late September. Washington went to Elijah Brown for three games in October, and he threw for 302 yards at Purdue, before Williams got the job back.

"We've both changed quarterbacks," Vangie says. "At least ours came back."

Here's how I see it. Autzen is loud from the start, and Raiola hits Moore for a touchdown on the first drive. Washington answers with a Williams run, and the Huskies hang around through halftime. Then Uiagalelei gets to Williams twice in the third quarter, and Oregon scores on back-to-back drives. Smith breaks a long one, and the Ducks pull away. Washington adds a late score.

Nix rides her scooter home with the Indianapolis parking map open on her phone. Vangie drives back up I-5 and says she'll be on the lake at five in the morning, and that nobody on the water will be talking about Oregon.

My call: Oregon Ducks 33, Washington Huskies 18.

Saturday night in Tucson is the hundredth meeting in the Territorial Cup, and Arizona comes in 8-3 after winning in overtime at Kansas State while Arizona State is 6-5 after losing in overtime to Oklahoma State. My Arizona State vs Arizona prediction goes with the home team to win by more than a touchdown, Arizona Wildcats −8.5, and stays low with the Under 54.5.

Inez Paloverde has a cup of prickly-pear lemonade and a plan. "Seven o'clock kickoff. Sun's down. I can finally watch a game without squinting."

Skylar Vanterpool, up from Tempe, has a plan too. "Keep it close, steal it late, take the Cup home. Our defense has been good for a month."

The side starts with Noah Fifita. He has 3,473 passing yards, 26 touchdowns and just 6 interceptions, and he threw for 323 yards and ran for a score in the overtime win at Kansas State. Isaiah Mizell has 990 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. Arizona is 5-1 at home, and the only loss came 40-39 to Utah.

Arizona State's offense has been a moving target. Cutter Boley, Mikey Keene and Jake Fette have all led the team in attempts, and Fette has been the guy for the last four games. The Sun Devils scored 28 or fewer in nine of their last ten games. Reed Harris is the threat, with 1,159 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns, including 11 catches for 172 yards against Oklahoma State. On the road, they lost at Texas A&M, Texas Tech and BYU, and won at UCF.

The defense is the reason Skylar is hopeful. Owen Long has 110 tackles and Jalen Thompson has 8 sacks, and the Sun Devils held Colorado to 10 and UCF to 13. That keeps the score down, but it also makes eight and a half hard to get.

The market moved toward Arizona. DraftKings opened Arizona −4.5 and 52.5, per ESPN. Our card has Arizona −8.5. Arizona Wildcats 34, Arizona State Sun Devils 20 is a 14-point win, comfortably clear.

The Under is Arizona State's offense. Four of the Sun Devils' last five games finished under this total, and the only one that didn't needed overtime. Kedrick Reescano has 9 rushing touchdowns for Arizona, and a lead lets the Wildcats run the clock. I have 54.

The room is all Arizona on the side. The Formula has 32-22, takes Arizona Wildcats −8.5 and goes Under 54.5. Next Man Up has 35-21, likes Arizona and goes Over 54.5. Letdown Watch has 34-19, likes Arizona and goes Under. In The Trenches has no score this week and takes neither side nor total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "Thirty-five to twenty-one. Fifita at home, on Fox, in a rivalry. He's going to throw it all over the place."

The Formula: "Thirty-two to twenty-two. They win by ten, and it's not as wild as you think."

My final is Arizona by 14 with 54 points, half a point under. Fifita makes the throws, the defense handles Arizona State, and the Cup stays in Tucson.

Arizona and Arizona State have played ninety-nine times, and on Saturday night at Casino Del Sol Stadium they play the 100th Territorial Cup, with Arizona leading the all-time series 52-46-1. Kickoff for Arizona State Sun Devils vs Arizona Wildcats is 7 p.m. in Tucson on Fox, and Inez Paloverde has staked out a spot with a cooler of prickly-pear lemonade and a hand-lettered sign that just says "52."

Skylar Vanterpool drove down from Tempe and read the sign out loud.

"Fifty-two. Wow. You know there's a forty-six on the other side of that."

"I know. That's why it's on my sign and not yours."

"I'm bringing a sign next year. It's going to say forty-seven."

"That's a sign about losing, Skylar."

"It's a sign about progress."

Inez has a good reason to be feeling it. Arizona is 8-3 and ranked No. 19, and last week the Wildcats won 35-28 in overtime at Kansas State, in the rain, with Noah Fifita throwing for 323 yards and running in a touchdown. Fifita has 3,473 passing yards and 26 touchdowns against six interceptions this year, and Isaiah Mizell has 990 receiving yards and 10 scores. This will be Arizona's 11th nationally televised game this season.

"Eleven times on national television," Inez says. "People in Ohio know who Fifita is now. My aunt in Ohio called me about it."

"Your aunt in Ohio doesn't watch football."

"She does now."

Skylar's Sun Devils are 6-5 after a 30-27 overtime loss to Oklahoma State, and he spent the drive down talking himself out of being upset about it. Jake Fette has taken over at quarterback, and Reed Harris caught 11 balls for 172 yards and two touchdowns in that game. Harris has 1,159 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns this season, and Skylar calls him "the best receiver in this state, and I'll say it in your parking lot."

"You just did," Inez says.

"And I'll say it again at halftime. Louder. Right next to your lemonade."

The Arizona State defense is the part Skylar feels best about. Owen Long has 110 tackles, Jalen Thompson has eight sacks, and the Sun Devils held Colorado to 10 points and UCF to 13 earlier this month. Arizona's defense has Chase Kennedy, with 6.5 sacks, and Taye Brown, with 73 tackles.

"Your defense is good," Inez admits. "Your offense has had three quarterbacks."

"Three quarterbacks means depth."

"Three quarterbacks means nobody knows who's starting."

The last two meetings went 49-7 to Arizona State and 23-7 to Arizona, and both fans have chosen to remember only one of them. Inez likes the most recent one. Skylar likes the one with more points.

Here's how Saturday goes. The stadium is packed for the hundredth meeting, the band is loud from warmups on, the student section is on its feet from the first snap, and Arizona gets the ball first. Fifita hits Mizell on a long one down the sideline, and the Wildcats are up early. Arizona State hangs in with Cardae Mack running hard and Harris making a big catch for a touchdown before the half. In the second half, Arizona's offense finds another gear, and Reescano punches in a short score. Fette keeps throwing, but Kennedy gets to him on a big third down, and Arizona pulls away late.

Inez will hold up her sign and cross out the 52, writing a 53 under it in marker. Skylar will ask if she has another marker, and she'll say no. He'll drive back up to Tempe with forty-seven already written on a napkin in his cup holder, ready for next year.

My call: Arizona Wildcats 34, Arizona State Sun Devils 20.

display.fanatic_story:
Nevada Wolf Pack vs UNLV Rebels is a cannon game, and Ridge Corbell has it circled in blue. The Fremont Cannon has been painted red for four years now, and the Tahoe ski patroller who doesn't scare easily wants it back. He drove down from Reno with a can of blue paint in the trunk, and he says it's not a joke.

"I'm not saying I'll need it," Ridge says. "I'm saying I'll be ready."

Monroe-Kalani doesn't have time for that. The former headliner dancer, who treats every UNLV game like a show, has already reviewed this one. She calls the opening act fine and the cannon the best part.

"It's red," Monroe-Kalani says. "It looks good red. It photographs well red. Leave it red."

But Ridge has more than the cannon on his mind. Nevada is 5-6. A win at Allegiant Stadium gets the Pack to six, and six gets them their first bowl trip in five years. Jeff Choate's first two seasons in Reno were rough, and this year hasn't been easy either. The Pack lost to Montana State in the second week, lost in double overtime to Air Force, and got shut out at UCLA. Then they went home and scored three points against New Mexico.

"That was rock bottom," Ridge says. "I mean, three points. I've seen avalanches with more offense."

Since then, Nevada has won two straight. The Pack beat Northern Illinois 28-7 on the road and completed six passes doing it. Then they beat Hawai'i 16-8 at home in a game Ridge describes as two guys fighting over a parking spot. The defense has carried this team. EJ Smith has 107 tackles, and Dylan LaBarbera has 6.5 sacks. Herschel Turner has 746 rushing yards and six scores.

"We don't throw," Ridge says. "We don't need to throw. We run it, and then we run it again, and then the other team gets tired."

Monroe-Kalani has a much better offense to sell. Jackson Arnold has 18 touchdown throws. Kayden McGee has 568 receiving yards on just 25 catches, which means every time he catches it, something good happens. Jai'Den Thomas has 817 rushing yards. The Rebels won at New Mexico and at San José State in the last two weeks, and they're 7-4 under Dan Mullen.

"We've got the quarterback," she says. "We've got the receiver. We've got the stadium. Ridge has paint."

The Rebels have had their own bad nights, though. North Texas beat them 44-6. Wyoming came to Allegiant and won 41-35. And UNLV doesn't win big. Its last three wins came by seven, four and two.

"That's my whole plan," Ridge says. "Stay close. Get to the fourth quarter. Let the blue paint do the talking."

Monroe-Kalani reminds him that UNLV won this game 42-17 last year and 38-14 the year before. Ridge reminds her that Nevada won it 51-20 in 2021, and he's got that box score saved on his phone.

"You need to delete that," she says. "It's five years old."

"I'm keeping it forever," Ridge says.

Here's how it goes. Nevada runs the ball on every early down and keeps Arnold on the bench. Turner breaks a long run for a touchdown in the second quarter, and the Pack lead at halftime. Monroe-Kalani starts pacing. In the second half, Arnold hits McGee deep for a score, and Thomas runs one in. Nevada gets a late field goal to make it a four-point game and has one more chance, but the Rebels' defense stops them near midfield. The cannon stays red.

Ridge leaves the paint in the trunk. He says he'll be back next year with a bigger can. Monroe-Kalani says she'll review that show, too, and that she's already bored.

My call: UNLV Rebels 25, Nevada Wolf Pack 21.

display.story_text:
One of the last games on the board this weekend is a 9:30 Eastern kickoff in Houston, and the Cougars may not have their senior quarterback for his own Senior Night. Conner Weigman got hurt at Colorado and missed last week's 34-31 win at West Virginia, where freshman Keisean Henderson threw for 268 yards in his first start. My Baylor vs Houston pick is Baylor Bears +5.5 and the Under 55.5, because I don't trust a freshman quarterback to win this by a touchdown against a defense this good.

Yo Pacheco is already on the countdown. "Houston, we have a quarterback. Two of them, maybe. Henderson went to Morgantown and stuck the landing. Five-and-oh at home, and we're not scrubbing the launch on Senior Night."

Maggie Whitlock opens her binder. "We had a rough two weeks, Yo. We're taking it down to the studs. But you know what doesn't need renovating? Our defense."

Maggie's right about the defense. Baylor gives up just 18.3 points a game, and it held Colorado to 13 and UCF to 9. Garrick Ponder has 4.5 sacks and Travion Barnes has 80 tackles. The problem has been the offense lately. Baylor lost 28-7 at BYU and 20-10 to Texas Tech, and DJ Lagway threw it 48 times in that last one for 236 yards. Gavin Freeman has 81 catches for 901 yards, but Ryelan Morris leads the team with only 381 rushing yards.

Houston scores 35.0 a game, but a lot of that came with Weigman, who has 25 touchdown throws and just 3 interceptions. Makhi Hughes ran for 158 yards and three touchdowns at West Virginia and has 870 on the year, and Amare Thomas has 10 touchdown catches. The Cougars give up 24.1 a game, and they lost 42-32 at Colorado and 21-13 at Utah.

These two have played close games. Houston won 25-24 in 2023 and 31-24 last year, and Baylor won 20-10 in 2024.

My margin is three. That keeps Baylor inside the 5.5 with room to breathe.

On the total, I have 51. Baylor's defense keeps games in the 40s, and Houston will ride Hughes if Henderson plays. DraftKings opened Houston Cougars −4.5 with a 54.5 total, and the side and total have each gone up a point, to −5.5 and 55.5.

Most of the room is with Baylor. The Formula has Houston 27-24 and likes Baylor +5.5 and the Under 55.5. Next Man Up has Houston 29-22, goes Houston −5.5 and likes the Under. Letdown Watch has Baylor 26-25 and likes Baylor and the Under. In The Trenches has no score this week, sees the fronts as split, and takes neither side nor total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "Senior Night, freshman quarterback, last game of the year. Houston's the one I'm watching."

Next Man Up: "Watch Henderson then. He's the next man up. Literally my whole name."

My final is Houston Cougars 27, Baylor Bears 24. Yo says Houston, we have a win. Maggie claps once and says the reveal comes next year.

display.fanatic_story:
Houston has a chance on Saturday night to go through a whole season without losing at home. The Cougars are 5-0 at TDECU Stadium, and the last one is Senior Night against Baylor, an 8:30 local kickoff with the crowd told to wear black and the team in black uniforms. Yo Pacheco has had the countdown clock running since the West Virginia game ended.

"T-minus five days," Yo says. "All systems go. Houston, we have a blackout."

Maggie Whitlock flew in from Waco with a three-ring binder labeled RENOVATION PLAN and a green-and-gold scarf she says is "just a pop of color."

"Yo, I love a dark room," Maggie says. "Black walls, moody lighting. Very in right now. But we're not here to admire your paint job. We're here to win a football game."

The biggest question of the week is in Houston's quarterback room. Conner Weigman, the senior who's thrown 25 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions this year, got hurt at Colorado on Nov. 13 and missed last week's game at West Virginia. Freshman Keisean Henderson took over and was terrific in his first college game as the No. 1, going 18 for 28 for 268 yards and a touchdown in a 34-31 win in Morgantown. Weigman is one of the seniors being honored Saturday night. Whether he plays in it is something everybody in Houston is waiting to hear.

"Two quarterbacks, one launch pad," Yo says. "Mission control is fine either way."

"Mission control is nervous," Maggie says. "I can tell. You keep tapping the table."

Yo stops tapping the table.

Here's what Houston has going for it no matter who's throwing. Makhi Hughes ran for 158 yards and three touchdowns at West Virginia, and he has 870 yards on the season. Amare Thomas has 853 receiving yards and 10 touchdown catches. The Cougars score 35.0 points a game, they beat Oklahoma State 35-32 and Cincinnati 31-24 at home, and they've been in the Top 25 for 11 straight polls, the longest run to begin a season at the school since 1990.

"Houston, we have a running back," Yo says. "Makhi Hughes is the booster rocket."

Maggie's case starts with her defense, and she opens the binder to the first tab. Baylor gives up 18.3 points a game. It held UCF to 9, Colorado to 13 and TCU to 17. Travion Barnes has 80 tackles, and Garrick Ponder has 4.5 sacks. It's been a strange year in Waco. The school fired Dave Aranda in the middle of the season, and the Bears still got to 6-5 and a bowl.

"The foundation is good," Maggie says. "The bones are good. We just need new fixtures on offense."

That's the second tab. Baylor scored 7 at BYU and 10 against Texas Tech the last two weeks, both losses. DJ Lagway has 2,295 yards and 17 touchdown throws with only 5 interceptions, and Gavin Freeman has 81 catches for 901 yards, but Ryelan Morris leads the team with just 381 yards on the ground. When the Bears can't run it, Lagway ends up throwing it 48 times, like he did against Texas Tech.

"I'd knock out a wall and put in a running game," Maggie says. "Open concept. Let the backs breathe."

These two have turned into a real Texas rivalry since Houston joined the Big 12. Houston won 25-24 in 2023, Baylor won 20-10 in 2024, and Houston won 31-24 in Waco last year in the final regular-season game for both teams.

"Three games, two Houston wins," Yo says. "Houston, we have a trend."

"Three games, all one score or close to it," Maggie says. "Houston, you have a problem."

Yo thinks about it and decides that's fair.

Here's how I see it. Baylor's defense keeps the game tight, and Lagway hits Freeman enough to keep the green-and-gold section loud. But Hughes wears the Bears down after halftime, the crowd in black gets louder as it gets later, and Houston makes one more play in the fourth quarter to finish the home season perfect.

Yo will yell "Houston, we have a WIN!" right as the clock hits zero. Maggie will close the binder, clap once and say the big reveal comes next year.

My call: Houston Cougars 27, Baylor Bears 24.

Hyrum Tolleson hasn't let go of the kick. "Wide left, Yesenia. In the final seconds. I watched it from my kitchen and I haven't sat in that chair since."

display.fanatic_story:
Hyrum Tolleson went out to his pasture in Cache Valley the week after the San Marcos game with a tape measure and a football. He marked off forty-eight yards from a fence post and tried the kick himself, over and over, until the cows lost interest. Texas State Bobcats vs Utah State Aggies is the rematch at Maverik Stadium, and Hyrum says he never made the kick either, but he wasn't wearing a uniform, so he has an excuse.

"Wide left," Hyrum says. "Every time. It's like the posts move."

Yesenia Calderwood bought her first real winter coat for this trip. She lives in San Marcos, where the river is the main event in summer and a hoodie is plenty in November. She tried it on in the store and said she looked like a sleeping bag with arms.

"I'm not complaining about Logan," Yesenia says. "I'm just telling you I'm wearing every shirt I own under this."

The first game is still a sore spot in Logan. Texas State won 20-17 on Oct. 24 after Utah State missed a 48-yard field goal wide left in the final seconds. The Aggies' defense was terrific that day. They held Brad Jackson to 167 throwing yards and sacked him four times. But Jaylen Jenkins took a kickoff back 100 yards for a Texas State touchdown in the first quarter, and that was the difference.

"One kick returned and one kick missed," Hyrum says. "That's the whole game."

"And the score," Yesenia says. "The score was also part of the game."

Yesenia's Bobcats have been one of the stories of the year in their first season in the Pac-12. Texas State is 7-4 and has won three straight, beating Oregon State 42-21, Fresno State 37-35 and Washington State 42-14. The only losses since September were by two at San Diego State and by one at Boise State, a 46-45 shootout.

Jackson has thrown for 2,624 yards and 23 touchdowns with only 6 interceptions. Torrance Burgess Jr. has 1,371 rushing yards and ran for 146 against Washington State. Chris Dawn Jr. leads the receivers with 649 yards. Jayden Bradley has 69 tackles from the secondary.

Hyrum's Aggies have had a harder fall. Utah State is 4-7 and out of the bowl picture after a 31-24 loss at Oregon State last week. McCae Hillstead has taken over at quarterback the last four games, and he threw for 277 yards in Corvallis. Grady Brosterhous started most of the year before that. Eli Wood has 479 receiving yards and 5 touchdowns. Brevin Hamblin leads the defense with 84 tackles.

"We don't have a bowl," Hyrum says. "We have this game. That's enough. Beat the team that beat us. Then go home and milk the cows."

"The cows can wait," Yesenia says.

"The cows cannot wait," Hyrum says. "You have never met a cow."

Here's how I see it. Maverik Stadium is cold and loud for the last home game. Utah State's defense starts the way it did in San Marcos and holds Texas State to a field goal on the first drive. Hillstead hits Wood for a touchdown, and the Aggies lead early. But Burgess starts running through tackles in the second quarter, and Jackson finds Dawn for a score before halftime. Texas State pulls ahead in the third quarter and adds a late touchdown. Utah State scores again, but it doesn't get close enough to need a kick.

Hyrum says that's the best part, because nobody had to try a forty-eight-yarder. Yesenia zips her coat all the way up and says she's flying home to San Marcos before her toes stop speaking to her.

My call: Texas State Bobcats 31, Utah State Aggies 22.

Oregon State and Fresno State met on Oct. 31, and the Bulldogs won 38-22 at home. Four weeks later the Pac-12's first Flex Week sends the Beavers back to Fresno for a nonconference rematch, with both teams at 6-5 and playing for a seventh win. Taking the field goal is my Oregon State vs Fresno State prediction, Oregon State Beavers +3, and the Under 57.5 gets my total call.

Juniper Ostrowski wants a do-over. "We didn't play like us last time. We get to fix it."

Rosalind "Roz" Ayala is not interested. "You lost by 16. That's not a do-over. That's a pattern."

The Beavers look different now. Maalik Murphy has thrown the most passes in the last two games, including 396 yards and 3 touchdowns in a 46-41 loss at Boise State and a 31-24 win over Utah State last week. Jesse Legree is the big target, with 1,418 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns. On defense, Takari Hickle has 7.5 sacks and Aiden Sullivan has 89 tackles.

Fresno State plays close games. Its losses to Boise State, San Diego State, Utah State and Texas State came by 7, 3, 7 and 2, and it beat Colorado State 49-42 last week. Jayden Mandal went 15 for 17 for 191 yards and 3 touchdowns in that game, and Bryson Donelson ran for 165. Josiah Freeman has 820 receiving yards. The Bulldogs are 4-1 at home.

That's why the field goal matters. Fresno State Bulldogs 29, Oregon State Beavers 27 is a two-point game, and a Fresno team that lives in one-score games gives the Beavers a real path. Oregon State scored 41 in Boise, and it can score again here.

The market has moved toward Fresno. DraftKings opened the Bulldogs −1.5 with a total of 56.5, per ESPN, and it's −3 and 57.5 now.

The Under is about the Fresno defense. The Bulldogs allow 24.0 a game, and they held Oregon State to 22 the first time. Fresno State's games went over 57.5 in only five of eleven. Utah State held Fresno to 10 three weeks ago. I have 56.

The room mostly sides with Oregon State but splits on the total. The Formula has Fresno 29-28, takes Oregon State Beavers +3 and goes Under 57.5. Next Man Up has Fresno 30-29, takes Oregon State and goes Over 57.5. Letdown Watch has Fresno 31-24, likes Fresno State Bulldogs −3 and likes the Under. In The Trenches has no score this week and takes neither side nor total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "Thirty-one to twenty-four. They beat these guys by 16 a month ago. Same building. Same result."

The Formula: "Twenty-nine to twenty-eight. One point. It's a rematch, not a rerun."

My final has Fresno by two with 56 points. The Bulldogs win, the Beavers stay inside the number, and nobody is happy with the defense.

display.fanatic_story:
Oregon State and Fresno State have already played once this fall, on Halloween, and Fresno State won 38-22 at Valley Children's Stadium. This time it's the conference's brand-new Flex Week that brings them back to the same field for a 7 p.m. kickoff on The CW, a nonconference game with both teams sitting at 6-5 and both trying to get to seven wins. Oregon State Beavers vs Fresno State Bulldogs, take two.

Juniper Ostrowski drove down from Corvallis in a beat-up hatchback and calls this trip "the rematch nobody asked for but everybody needed." Roz Ayala, who has lived in Fresno her whole life and owns more red than any person should, calls it "a second helping."

"A second helping of what?" Juniper asks.

"Of us beating you."

"We were a different team on Halloween."

"You were dressed up as a team that loses by sixteen."

Juniper takes that one on the chin and moves on. The Beavers are bowl eligible after beating Utah State 31-24 last week, when Reichle scored three touchdowns. Maalik Murphy has thrown the most passes in the last two games, including 396 yards and three touchdowns in a 46-41 loss at Boise State that Juniper still thinks they should've won. Jesse Legree is the headline, though, with 1,418 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns.

"Fifteen touchdowns," Juniper says. "Fifteen. He catches everything. He'd catch your car keys if you threw them from the top row."

"Don't give me ideas."

"You'd miss. He wouldn't."

Roz shakes her head, but she's smiling. Fresno State has been through it this year, too. The Bulldogs lost 39-0 at USC to open the season, then dropped close ones to Boise State, San Diego State, Utah State and Texas State, all by a touchdown or less. Last week they beat Colorado State 49-42, and Jayden Mandal was nearly perfect, going 15 for 17 for 191 yards and three scores. Bryson Donelson ran for 165 yards, and Josiah Freeman caught two touchdowns.

"Mandal threw two incompletions," Roz says. "Two. One of them was on purpose."

"How do you throw an incompletion on purpose?"

"You throw it away, Juniper. It's called being smart."

On defense, Fresno has K'vion Thunderbird with 84 tackles and Dylan Hampsten with six sacks. Oregon State counters with Takari Hickle, who has 7.5 sacks, and Aiden Sullivan, who has 89 tackles. Both teams have given up big numbers in the past few weeks, and Roz says that's because both defenses have been "busy."

"Busy doing what?" Juniper asks.

"Chasing people."

The two teams also played last September, and Fresno State won that one 36-27. Juniper reminds Roz that Oregon State won the meeting before that, 35-32 in 2022. Roz reminds Juniper that 2022 was a long time ago.

Here's how it goes. The stadium is loud for a night game, the Fresno crowd is in red, and the Bulldogs come out running Donelson right at the Beaver defense. Oregon State answers with Murphy finding Legree for a long touchdown, and it's tight at halftime. The second half goes back and forth, with Mandal hitting Freeman for a score and Legree catching another. Late in the fourth, Fresno kicks a field goal to go up two, and Oregon State gets the ball back with a minute left. Hickle has already sacked Mandal twice, and Roz has been yelling at the refs for most of the quarter, but the Beavers run out of clock in Fresno territory.

Roz will hand Juniper a Bulldogs foam finger on the way out as a souvenir. Juniper will toss it in the back seat, and it will still be there in March.

My call: Fresno State Bulldogs 29, Oregon State Beavers 27.

Sacramento State vs Hawai'i closes the night, and the season, for two teams that would like to forget most of it. Hawai'i is 3-8. Sacramento State is 2-9 in its first season in the MAC and hasn't played since November 11. My Sacramento State vs Hawai'i pick is Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors −14 with the Over 39.5.

Kainoa Akana-Baird is wearing white, like the school asked. "Senior Night, White Out, last game of the year. I want a blowout and I want to be home by ten."

Mateo Villaseñor flew out from Sacramento with a sunburn already. "Seventeen days off. My guys are rested, healthy and ready. You're the ones who just scored eight points in Reno."

He's right that Hawai'i's offense has stalled lately. The Warriors managed eight at Nevada and 13 against North Dakota State. But Sacramento State has been run over by just about everybody with a pulse. The Hornets lost by 46 at Fresno State, 41 to Ohio, 29 to UMass and 28 at Bowling Green. Seven of their nine losses came by more than fourteen points. They score 16.1 a game and allow 29.2.

The quarterback spot is another problem for the visitors. Brian Salazar Jr. became the third Hornet to start this season late in the season, and he went 13 of 28 for 103 yards at Central Michigan. Micah Alejado has 2,815 yards for Hawai'i and has thrown for over 300 four times.

The Over comes from the Sacramento State side. Nine of the Hornets' eleven games went over this total, mostly because the other team kept scoring. Central Michigan ran for over three hundred yards against them last time out. Sacramento State allows 4.9 a carry, and even a Hawai'i ground game that has managed just 3.0 a carry should find room. DeVon Rice has seven rushing touchdowns.

DraftKings opened Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors −14.5 with a 44.5 total. The total has come down five points since, which gives the Over plenty of room.

The room is lined up on Hawai'i and the Over. The Formula has 32-13 and takes Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors −14 with the Over 39.5. Letdown Watch has 32-12 with Hawai'i and the Over. Letdown Watch: "Next Man Up, you've got Hawai'i by sixteen and the total by a half point. Live a little."

Next Man Up: "I've got the right side and the right total. Your extra four points just make you feel brave."

My final is Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors 30, Sacramento State Hornets 13. Hawai'i wins by seventeen, past the fourteen, and 43 combined clears the total. The seniors go out in white with a win, and the Hornets head home for a long winter.

display.fanatic_story:
Sacramento State Hornets vs Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors is Senior Night at the Ching Complex, and Kainoa Akana-Baird pulled his white shirt out of the closet on Tuesday. The school wants everybody in white for the seniors, and he takes that seriously. He also wants the seniors to walk off with a win, because this season has given them very little.

"Three and eight," Kainoa says. "That's not how you send anybody off. Give them one good night. That's all I'm asking."

Mateo Villaseñor flew in from Sacramento, and he's been on the beach for two days. He says he's here for football, but his sunburn says otherwise. His Hornets are 2-9 in their first season in the MAC, and they haven't played since November 11.

"Seventeen days off," Mateo says. "That's not rust. That's a vacation. Same as me."

The Hornets have had a long first year at this level. They lost by 46 at Fresno State and 41 to Ohio. They gave up 319 rushing yards at Central Michigan in their last game. They've started three different quarterbacks, and Brian Salazar Jr. got the last start. They did beat Kent State 31-10, and they lost to Toledo by just three.

"We're new," Mateo says. "You'd struggle too if you showed up to the big party and everybody already knew each other."

Kainoa's had his own rough fall. Hawai'i lost at Stanford, lost to UNLV at home, and lost six of its last eight games. The Warriors scored eight points at Nevada last week, and Micah Alejado threw for just 95 yards. The week before that, North Dakota State came to the Ching Complex and won 21-13.

"It's been a lot of close nights and not enough fun ones," Kainoa says. "I'm due a fun one."

Alejado has had better nights than last week. He has 2,815 yards on the year, and he threw for over 300 four times. He put up 323 yards and three touchdowns at Northern Illinois in a 56-21 win. Kainoa thinks that's the Alejado who shows up on Saturday.

"Micah throws it like he's never heard of a punt," Kainoa says. "I love that about him. Sometimes it scares me. Mostly I love it."

DeVon Rice has seven rushing touchdowns, and Kainoa expects him to get a lot of work against a Sacramento State defense that just let Central Michigan run wild.

Mateo has a guy he loves, too. Boogsie Silvera is a senior safety with 88 tackles, and he's had four games with at least ten. Matt Coleman has 545 receiving yards and six touchdowns. And the Hornets have a punter, Hamish Adams, who boomed one 62 yards at Central Michigan.

"Our punter's the best player on the field," Mateo says. "That's not a complaint. That's a compliment to the punter."

"Bring him," Kainoa says. "We'll let him punt all night."

Mateo laughs. Then he admits he isn't sure who's playing quarterback.

Here's how it goes. The stadium fills up in white, and the Warriors come out sharp. Alejado hits a couple of long throws early, and Rice punches one in for a touchdown. Sacramento State gets a field goal after a nice drive, and Mateo cheers like it's a touchdown. Hawai'i adds two more scores before halftime and pulls away. The Hornets get a late touchdown, and Mateo says it was worth the flight.

After the game, the seniors walk out onto the field, and the whole place stays to cheer them. Kainoa takes his white shirt off and waves it over his head. Mateo says he'll come back next year, if only for the beach.

My call: Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors 30, Sacramento State Hornets 13.

Sacramento State vs Hawai'i closes the night, and the season, for two teams that would like to forget most of it. Hawai'i is 3-8. Sacramento State is 2-9 in its first season in the MAC and hasn't played since November 11. My Sacramento State vs Hawai'i pick is Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors −14 with the Over 39.5.

Kainoa Akana-Baird is wearing white, like the school asked. "Senior Night, White Out, last game of the year. I want a blowout and I want to be home by ten."

Mateo Villaseñor flew out from Sacramento with a sunburn already. "Seventeen days off. My guys are rested, healthy and ready. You're the ones who just scored eight points in Reno."

He's right that Hawai'i's offense has stalled lately. The Warriors managed eight at Nevada and 13 against North Dakota State. But Sacramento State has been run over by just about everybody with a pulse. The Hornets lost by 46 at Fresno State, 41 to Ohio, 29 to UMass and 28 at Bowling Green. Seven of their nine losses came by more than fourteen points. They score 16.1 a game and allow 29.2.

The quarterback spot is another problem for the visitors. Brian Salazar Jr. became the third Hornet to start this season late in the season, and he went 13 of 28 for 103 yards at Central Michigan. Micah Alejado has 2,815 yards for Hawai'i and has thrown for over 300 four times.

The Over comes from the Sacramento State side. Nine of the Hornets' eleven games went over this total, mostly because the other team kept scoring. Central Michigan ran for over three hundred yards against them last time out. Sacramento State allows 4.9 a carry, and even a Hawai'i ground game that has managed just 3.0 a carry should find room. DeVon Rice has seven rushing touchdowns.

DraftKings opened Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors −14.5 with a 44.5 total. The total has come down five points since, which gives the Over plenty of room.

The room is lined up on Hawai'i and the Over. The Formula has 32-13 and takes Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors −14 with the Over 39.5. Letdown Watch has 32-12 with Hawai'i and the Over. Letdown Watch: "Next Man Up, you've got Hawai'i by sixteen and the total by a half point. Live a little."

Next Man Up: "I've got the right side and the right total. Your extra four points just make you feel brave."

My final is Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors 30, Sacramento State Hornets 13. Hawai'i wins by seventeen, past the fourteen, and 43 combined clears the total. The seniors go out in white with a win, and the Hornets head home for a long winter.
